Who would have ever imagined that a little germ which cannot be seen with the human eye, has put the entire globe in a tizzy, a panic, and an economic disruption? I have not seen a pandemic of this magnitude in my lifetime and, when this first emerged, I was one of the gainsayers who could not believe it would cripple our world to this extent. Questions abound, conspiracy theories are propagated, and fear has run rampant throughout the world as the entire globe responds to the pandemic. Will there be a cure, or will this continue to be a scourge in our world? If this little virus trespasses into my physical body, what is the chance of survival? Will it affect any of my loved ones? The questions are innumerable. Where it has come from has been theorized by many, but does anyone really know? Where is God in the whole thing? Did it surprise Him? Is it God’s judgment on humanity? These and many other questions are being asked by many sincere people and the answers that are given often contradict one another.

One of the outfalls of the pandemic is the government invasion into the church and our personal lives in a way that has been unprecedented in my and your lifetime. Suddenly, we are faced with decisions that many of us have not thought through. When, and how much, should the government mandate things in our lives when we clearly believe in separation of Church and state? What are my rights? What will I do if I lose my business? Will I cash in the stimulus check that is supposed to arrive in the mail in the near future?

There is a verse in Peter that reminds me that if anyone should have answers in this time of pandemic, we as Christians should. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: –1Pe 3:15. We may not know the origin of the virus, nor the outcome, but we do know Who knows all things, and that it was not a surprise to Him. It is the right time to turn to the Lord Jesus Christ, the One who holds all things by the power of His Word. If anytime in recent history the Christian has an opportunity to be salt in the earth and light in the world, it is during this time of upheaval. So, what should the response of the Christian be?

Consider this verse in Luke: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth… –Luk 21:26. For the Christian, earthquakes, famines, and pestilence should be no surprise since they have been prophesied to us through the Word of God. And while these things are happening and will happen, God has provided clear scriptural mandates for us as Christians to follow. We are clearly commanded in the scripture to not worry about tomorrow: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Mat 6:34.

So, we as Jesus’ disciples know that God will give us wisdom and grace for the difficulties of today. We are commanded to not borrow tomorrow’s troubles. We need to be reminded once again, in this time, as always, God will provide grace for today that will be great enough to sustain peace in the midst of the storm, and will provide it tomorrow if we live. Let us learn a lesson from Peter and the disciples—to focus on Jesus. We need to trust Jesus even when He seems to be asleep in the boat, rather than focusing on the storm that is raging all around us. Jesus was in control whether he was sleeping or awake and still is. But we might say, “How do I know if I will have food or clothing, or my business tomorrow?” And again, we hear the Savior say, “Look at the lilies, the fowls of the air, and learn a lesson from them!” We cannot even do some of the simplest things by God’s estimation, like add a cubit to our stature, so why would we try to deal with the hard things of providing for a tomorrow that is out of our control? Do these commands fit for the year 2020 and the pandemic that we are facing? I am sure that, in theory, we can agree, but can we internalize these verses and make them a very prominent place in our lives today?

There are principles given in God’s Word that, if we have not embraced them, we will also ‘reel in a tizzy’ when faced with things like the pandemic that is completely out of our control. One of those principles is the clear teaching that suffering is a way of life for the follower of Jesus. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17.

The ‘health and wealth’ gospel that is peddled by many preachers today is a false doctrine and can leave a person reeling when they are faced with health or economic loss. We need to be okay with suffering, we need to embrace it; we need to arm ourselves with the same mind as Christ. The loss of our business, home and yes, even our own lives also, by economic disaster, storms, or accidents is not outside the realm of the will of God for the Christian. We know that God can eliminate any of these calamities and will protect us from them all IF He so wills. But whether He does or not is God’s prerogative and we are the happiest IF we surrender our lives completely to Him in faith, and trust Him to keep us, whether with little or with much.

Another principle we need to reckon with is that we have no rights except the right to the Tree of Life. For us as Christians it makes little difference if we are citizens of the United States or not. We have many privileges for which we are very grateful for, but we should not think we have a right to own, keep, or buy, or that we have a stake to claim in this world. In the Holy Scriptures we are reminded that we are but pilgrims and strangers here (see Heb 11:13-16). As Abraham and the other patriarchs, we have no abiding city here but look for a city …whose builder and maker is God –Heb 11:10.

There are plenty of lawyers offering to fight for our rights, but the truth of the matter is, our citizenship is in Heaven and we are just ambassadors here and can be kicked out by society and need to leave all anytime without a moment’s hesitation. If this will be a reality, we need to live our lives with all our things held with an open hand. We do not have the right (only the privilege)—to own land, to have enough food, to enjoy good health, and to live without suffering—nor should we fight for those so-called rights, but we, God’s people, must put on the mind of Christ and be willing to leave all behind for the sake of Christ and trust Him completely for our sustenance. Jesus said He sees one sparrow fall to the ground and reminds us that we are worth more than many sparrows. Jesus calls us to hate all that we hold dear here on this earth: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple –Luk 14:26.

As Christians, we do not plan to stay here on this earth; we are anticipating Heaven. The scriptures express this sentiment when it not only considers the whole earth groaning to be delivered from this death and decay, but that we ourselves are also groaning to be delivered. Should there be such a strong pull to be here that our hearts fail us …for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth…? –Luk 21:26. Should we much rather cry out “how long Lord Jesus” “so come”? Even as the apostle intimates as he wrestles with being “betwixt two”—For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. –Php 1:23-24. The apostle clearly indicates “having a desire to depart and be with Christ is far better,” and the only thing that holds him here is the fact that there is work to be done.

Another area we should be awake to, is our vulnerability during this time of no church services. We may be tempted to go on-line and be fed spiritually by those who are false prophets or those who teach false doctrine. We need to “try the spirits” and know whose feet we are sitting at. Be selective to whom you might listen, or from whom you might allow your family to take nourishment. We, as fathers, are called to lead and lead we must. The burden is on our shoulders to help our families navigate through these uncertain times. We as fathers may need to be more proactive during this time. It is a call to us to rise up and lead our wives and children. Not only do we have to watch “whose feet we are sitting at”, but we need to lead our families with confidence, calling them to trust in God, and leading them in prayers of faith. We need to provide them with an example of faith and trust in God that no amount of buffeting will shake. This time of upheaval will not knock us off our feet IF we are rooted and grounded in Christ.

At a time like this, we need to make wise decisions, even decisions concerning the future, but still refrain from falling into the panic mode and running around as if we have no Heavenly Father. We also need to lead our families in being careful not to believe everything that one hears, but to be aware of where our news is coming from and to consider how reliable it is. Conspiracy theories abound concerning how this virus started and the political agenda theorized to be behind it. Refrain from spending time following these conspirators and rather follow the scripture mandate, “casting down imaginations.” The simple truth is this, we do not know, and if we did know it still should not change the way we live and our overall response. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, of love and a sound mind. John tells us to not “believe every spirit, but to try the spirits to see whether they be of God.”

I believe that this is an awesome opportunity to reach out to our fellow brothers and sisters by praying for one another and by staying in touch so that we can ‘weep with those that weep’ and ‘rejoice with those that rejoice’. Some of us have jobs and some do not. God’s Word tells us that those who have are to give to those who do not have so that there may be an equality. It is a time to reach out to the elderly in our church or community and stay in touch by mail or phone. This is a time in which the lonely will only get lonelier. A cheery word, or a letter in the mail, and whatever other resources you can appropriately use may be just the thing that those around you need.

During the times of mandatory “stay at home”, there is a whole group of our society that will face challenges that they have not seen up to this time. According to various news sources there has been an increase in domestic violence since family members are spending much more time together than they normally do. But let this not once be named among us. This is the time for us as God’s children to maximize on “in home” relationships. The Bible calls us to “redeem the time” and this can be done by making the most of our time together as a family. Spend time together—reading the Bible, praying together, singing together, and just simply doing enjoyable things together—things that will nurture growth and love in our relationships. We need to be creative as fathers in bringing our family together in a way that will produce an atmosphere of unity and oneness.

One question that begs an answer is this, “Should the government dictate whether we have church or not?” This is something we need to answer since for some areas of the country it is more than a suggestion but has become mandatory. I believe that since the suggestion/order to not meet together during this time is for the purpose of not spreading a virus that is quite contagious, this then fulfills the scripture “to love our neighbor as ourselves.” It is a good opportunity to show the public that if the mandate does not ask us to violate the scripture, then we choose to honor the government. There may come a time soon enough that we will be asked to do something that we cannot do with a clear conscience and then we will need to stand and “obey God rather than men.”

Some feel a twang of guilt because of the verse, “to not forsake the assembling of ourselves together”, however, this seems to be addressing a habit or a way of life. I suppose this is dealing with the lazy, slothful heart that does not see the benefit of getting together. We want to get together… As soon as we can get together again, we will take advantage of it. There is a big difference between those who cannot get together for a short time and those that choose not to since they do not see the value of it. For the present time, it seems the best testimony to our world and public relations to honor the mandate since they are not fighting against our faith and God. Let’s just take care to not let this become our new normal. Let’s keep our eye on a path forward to once again practically function as a local body.

What can we do? Pray more than ever that God would use this to win the lost and refine the church. Spend time building relationships with those you are closest to and have been encouraged to stay home with. Let this pandemic prepare us for what God has for us in the future. Let us be very careful how we talk about the government and some of the rulings that have come out through this all. We are called to honor the king and we need to spend more time thanking God for our freedoms than maximizing on the negative—I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; –1Ti 2:1-3. For the Christian, …we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Rom 8:28.

Wie sou ooit kon dink dat ’n klein kiem wat nie met die menslike oog gesien kan word nie, die hele wêreld in ’n warboel en paniek sou dompel en ekonomiese ontwrigting sou veroorsaak? Ek het in my leeftyd nog nie ’n pandemie van hierdie omvang gesien nie, en toe dit die eerste keer uitgebreek het, was ek een van diegene wat dit teëgespreek het omdat ek nie kon glo dat dit ons wêreld in hierdie mate sou lamlê nie. Vrae is volop, samesweringsteorieë word versprei en vrees het wêreldwyd hoogty gevier terwyl die hele wêreld op die pandemie reageer. Sal daar ’n geneesmiddel wees, of sal dit ’n plaag in ons wêreld bly? As hierdie klein virus my liggaam binnedring, wat is die kans dat ek dit sal oorleef? Sal dit enige van my geliefdes raak? Die vrae is ontelbaar. Baie mense het teorieë oor waar dit vandaan kom, maar weet enigiemand werklik? Waar is God in dit alles? Het dit Hom verras? Is dit God se oordeel oor die mensdom? Baie opregte mense vra hierdie en talle ander vrae, en die antwoorde wat gegee word, weerspreek mekaar dikwels.

Een van die gevolge van die pandemie is dat die regering op ’n ongekende manier in my en jou leeftyd by die kerk en ons persoonlike lewens inmeng. Skielik moet ons besluite neem waaroor baie van ons nie voorheen nagedink het nie. Wanneer, en in watter mate, behoort die regering dinge in ons lewens voor te skryf, wanneer ons duidelik in die skeiding van kerk en staat glo? Wat is my regte? Wat sal ek doen as ek my onderneming verloor? Sal ek die stimulustjek wat na verwagting binnekort in die pos sal aankom, inwissel?

Daar is ’n vers in Petrus wat my daaraan herinner dat ons as Christene antwoorde behoort te hê as enigiemand dit in hierdie tyd van pandemie behoort te hê. Maar heilig die Here God in julle harte, en wees altyd gereed om aan elkeen wat julle vra, ’n antwoord te gee oor die hoop wat in julle is, met sagmoedigheid en eerbied: –1Pe 3:15. Ons weet dalk nie waar die virus vandaan kom, of wat die uitkoms sal wees nie, maar ons weet Wie alles weet, en dat dit Hom nie verras het nie. Dit is nou die regte tyd om ons tot die Here Jesus Christus te wend, Hy wat alles deur die krag van sy Woord onderhou. As Christene ooit in die onlangse geskiedenis die geleentheid gehad het om sout op die aarde en lig in die wêreld te wees, is dit gedurende hierdie tyd van omwenteling. Wat behoort die Christen se reaksie dus te wees?

Dink aan hierdie vers in Lukas: …terwyl die mense se harte beswyk van vrees en verwagting oor die dinge wat oor die wêreld kom… –Luk 21:26. Vir die Christen behoort aardbewings, hongersnode en pessiektes geen verrassing te wees nie, aangesien dit deur die Woord van God aan ons geprofeteer is. En terwyl hierdie dinge gebeur en nog sal gebeur, het God duidelike opdragte in die Skrif gegee wat ons as Christene moet volg. Die Skrif beveel ons duidelik om ons nie oor môre te bekommer nie: Wees dan nie besorg oor môre nie, want môre sal hom oor sy eie dinge bekommer. Elke dag het genoeg aan sy eie kwaad –Mat 6:34.

As dissipels van Jesus weet ons dus dat God ons wysheid en genade sal gee vir die probleme van vandag. Ons word beveel om nie môre se probleme vooruit te dra nie. Ons moet weer daaraan herinner word dat God, nou soos altyd, genade vir vandag sal gee wat groot genoeg is om vrede te midde van die storm te handhaaf, en dit môre ook sal gee as ons lewe. Laat ons ’n les by Petrus en die dissipels leer—om ons op Jesus te rig. Ons moet Jesus vertrou, selfs wanneer dit lyk of Hy in die boot slaap, eerder as om ons aandag op die storm te vestig wat oral om ons woed. Jesus was in beheer, of Hy nou geslaap of wakker was, en is dit steeds. Maar ons kan vra: “Hoe weet ek of ek môre kos of klere sal hê, of my onderneming sal hê?” En weer hoor ons die Heiland sê: “Kyk na die lelies, die voëls van die hemel, en leer ’n les by hulle!” Volgens God se maatstaf kan ons nie eers van die eenvoudigste dinge doen nie, soos om ’n el by ons lengte te voeg; waarom sou ons dan probeer om die moeilike dinge te hanteer, soos om vir ’n môre te voorsien wat buite ons beheer is? Pas hierdie opdragte by die jaar 2020 en die pandemie waarmee ons te kampe het? Ek is seker dat ons in teorie daarmee kan saamstem, maar kan ons hierdie verse ons eie maak en hulle vandag ’n baie prominente plek in ons lewe gee?

God se Woord gee beginsels wat, as ons dit nie aangeneem het nie, ons ook “in ’n warboel sal laat rondmaal” wanneer ons voor dinge te staan kom soos die pandemie, wat heeltemal buite ons beheer is. Een van hierdie beginsels is die duidelike lering dat lyding deel van die lewe van ’n volgeling van Jesus is. En as ons kinders is, dan ook erfgename, erfgename van God en mede-erfgename van Christus, as ons naamlik saam met Hom ly, sodat ons ook saam met Hom verheerlik kan word –Rom 8:17.

Die “gesondheids-en-rykdom”-evangelie wat vandag deur baie predikers verkondig word, is ’n valse leerstelling en kan iemand heeltemal ontredderd laat wanneer hy met gesondheids- of ekonomiese verlies te kampe kry. Ons moet lyding kan aanvaar; ons moet dit omhels; ons moet onsself met dieselfde gesindheid as Christus toerus. Die verlies van ons onderneming, huis en ja, selfs ons eie lewe, as gevolg van ekonomiese rampe, storms of ongelukke, val nie buite die omvang van God se wil vir die Christen nie. Ons weet dat God enige van hierdie rampe kan uit die weg ruim en ons daarteen sal beskerm AS dit sy wil is. Maar of Hy dit doen of nie, is God se prerogatief, en ons is die gelukkigste AS ons ons lewens heeltemal in geloof aan Hom oorgee en Hom vertrou om ons te onderhou, hetsy met min of met baie.

’n Verdere beginsel waarmee ons rekening moet hou, is dat ons geen regte het nie, behalwe die reg op die Boom van die Lewe. Vir ons as Christene maak dit min verskil of ons burgers van die Verenigde State is of nie. Ons het baie voorregte waarvoor ons baie dankbaar is, maar ons moet nie dink dat ons die reg het om iets te besit, te behou of te koop, of dat ons ’n aanspraak in hierdie wêreld het nie. Die Heilige Skrif herinner ons daaraan dat ons hier maar pelgrims en vreemdelinge is (sien Heb 11:13-16). Soos Abraham en die ander aartsvaders het ons hier geen blywende stad nie, maar ons soek ’n stad …waarvan God die boumeester en oprigter is –Heb 11:10.

Daar is baie prokureurs wat aanbied om vir ons regte te veg, maar die waarheid is dat ons burgerskap in die Hemel is en dat ons hier net ambassadeurs is. Die samelewing kan ons wegjaag, en ons moet enige tyd sonder die geringste huiwering alles agterlaat. As dit werklikheid gaan word, moet ons lewe met al ons besittings losweg in ons hande. Ons het nie die reg nie (slegs die voorreg)—om grond te besit, genoeg kos te hê, goeie gesondheid te geniet en sonder lyding te leef—en ons moet ook nie vir hierdie sogenaamde regte veg nie. Ons, God se volk, moet die gesindheid van Christus aanneem, bereid wees om alles ter wille van Christus agter te laat en Hom heeltemal vir ons lewensonderhoud te vertrou. Jesus het gesê dat Hy sien wanneer ’n mossie op die grond val, en herinner ons daaraan dat ons meer werd is as baie mossies. Jesus roep ons om alles wat ons hier op aarde dierbaar is, te haat: As iemand na My toe kom en hy haat nie sy vader en moeder en vrou en kinders en broers en susters, ja, selfs ook sy eie lewe nie, kan hy my dissipel nie wees nie –Luk 14:26.

As Christene beplan ons nie om hier op aarde te bly nie; ons sien uit na die Hemel. Die Skrif verwoord hierdie gedagte wanneer dit nie net sê dat die hele aarde sug om van hierdie dood en verval verlos te word nie, maar ook dat ons self sug om verlos te word. Behoort ons so sterk hierheen aangetrek te word dat ons harte beswyk …van vrees en verwagting oor die dinge wat oor die wêreld kom…? –Luk 21:26. Behoort ons nie eerder uit te roep: “Hoe lank nog, Here Jesus?” en “Kom dan”? Net soos die apostel dit laat blyk terwyl hy worstel met die gedagte dat hy “tussen twee” staan—Want ek word van weerskante gedring: ek het die begeerte om heen te gaan en met Christus te wees, want dit is verreweg die beste; maar om in die vlees te bly, is nodiger om julle ontwil. –Php 1:23-24. Die apostel dui duidelik aan dat “die begeerte om heen te gaan en met Christus te wees, verreweg die beste is,” en dat die enigste ding wat hom hier hou, die feit is dat daar werk is om te doen.

’n Verdere gebied waarop ons bedag moet wees, is ons kwesbaarheid gedurende hierdie tyd sonder kerkbyeenkomste. Ons kan in die versoeking kom om aanlyn te gaan en geestelike voedsel te ontvang van valse profete of mense wat valse leerstellings verkondig. Ons moet “die geeste beproef” en weet aan wie se voete ons sit. Wees kieskeurig oor na wie jy luister, of by wie jy jou gesin geestelike voedsel laat ontvang. Ons, as vaders, is geroep om leiding te gee, en ons móét leiding gee. Die verantwoordelikheid rus op ons skouers om ons gesinne te help om deur hierdie onseker tye te navigeer. As vaders sal ons gedurende hierdie tyd dalk meer proaktief moet wees. Dit is ’n oproep aan ons om op te staan en ons vrouens en kinders te lei. Ons moet nie net waak oor “aan wie se voete ons sit” nie, maar ook ons gesinne met vertroue lei, hulle oproep om op God te vertrou en hulle in geloofsgebede lei. Ons moet vir hulle ’n voorbeeld van geloof en vertroue in God stel wat deur geen mate van teenspoed geskud sal word nie. Hierdie tyd van omwenteling sal ons nie van stryk bring AS ons in Christus gewortel en gegrond is nie.

In ’n tyd soos hierdie moet ons wyse besluite neem, selfs besluite oor die toekoms, maar steeds nie in paniek verval en rondhardloop asof ons geen Hemelse Vader het nie. Ons moet ook ons gesinne lei om versigtig te wees om nie alles te glo wat ’n mens hoor nie, maar om bewus te wees van waar ons nuus vandaan kom en te oorweeg hoe betroubaar dit is. Samesweringsteorieë oor hoe hierdie virus begin het en die politieke agenda wat na bewering daaragter sit, is volop. Vermy dit om tyd daaraan te bestee om hierdie samesweringsteoretici te volg, en volg eerder die opdrag in die Skrif: “neerwerp elke skans.” Die eenvoudige waarheid is dit: ons weet nie, en selfs al het ons geweet, behoort dit steeds nie ons lewenswyse of ons algemene reaksie te verander nie. God het ons nie ’n gees van vreesagtigheid gegee nie, maar van krag en liefde en selfbeheersing. Johannes sê vir ons om nie “elke gees te glo nie, maar die geeste te beproef of hulle uit God is.”

Ek glo dat dit ’n wonderlike geleentheid is om na ons mede-broers en -susters uit te reik deur vir mekaar te bid en met mekaar in verbinding te bly, sodat ons kan “huil saam met die wat huil” en “bly wees saam met die wat bly is”. Sommige van ons het werk en sommige nie. God se Woord sê vir ons dat dié wat het, aan dié wat nie het nie, moet gee, sodat daar gelykheid kan wees. Dit is ’n tyd om uit te reik na die bejaardes in ons kerk of gemeenskap en per pos of telefoon met hulle in verbinding te bly. In hierdie tyd sal eensame mense net nog eensamer word. ’n Opbeurende woord, ’n brief in die pos, of enige ander hulpbron wat jy gepas kan gebruik, is dalk net wat die mense om jou nodig het.

Gedurende die tydperke van verpligte “tuisbly” sal ’n hele groep in ons samelewing voor uitdagings te staan kom wat hulle tot nou toe nie geken het nie. Volgens verskeie nuusbronne het gesinslede meer tyd saam deurgebring as gewoonlik, en het gesinsgeweld toegeneem. Maar laat dit nooit onder ons genoem word nie. Dit is nou die tyd vir ons as God se kinders om ons verhoudings binne die huis ten volle te benut. Die Bybel roep ons om “die tyd uit te koop”, en dit kan ons doen deur ons tyd saam as ’n gesin ten beste te benut. Bring tyd saam deur—lees die Bybel, bid saam, sing saam en doen eenvoudig aangename dinge saam—dinge wat groei en liefde in ons verhoudings sal bevorder. Ons vaders moet kreatief wees om die gesin bymekaar te bring op ’n manier wat ’n atmosfeer van eenheid en samesyn sal voortbring.

Een vraag wat ’n antwoord vereis, is: “Behoort die regering te bepaal of ons kerk hou of nie?” Dit is iets wat ons moet beantwoord, aangesien dit in sommige dele van die land meer as ’n voorstel is en verpligtend geword het. Ek glo dat, aangesien die voorstel/bevel om gedurende hierdie tyd nie bymekaar te kom, daarop gemik is om te voorkom dat ’n hoogs aansteeklike virus versprei, dit dan voldoen aan die Skrifopdrag om “ons naaste lief te hê soos onsself”. Dit is ’n goeie geleentheid om aan die publiek te wys dat ons kies om die regering te eerbiedig as die opdrag ons nie vra om die Skrif te oortree nie. Dit kan binnekort gebeur dat ons gevra word om iets te doen wat ons nie met ’n skoon gewete kan doen nie; dan sal ons moet standpunt inneem en “God meer gehoorsaam wees as die mense”.

Sommige voel ’n sweempie skuld oor die vers: “om nie ons onderlinge byeenkomste na te laat nie”, maar dit lyk asof dit ’n gewoonte of lewenswyse aanspreek. Ek neem aan dit handel oor die lui, traak-my-nie-agterige hart wat nie die nut daarvan insien om bymekaar te kom nie. Ons wil bymekaarkom… Sodra ons weer kan bymekaarkom, sal ons die geleentheid aangryp. Daar is ’n groot verskil tussen dié wat vir ’n kort tydjie nie kan bymekaarkom nie en dié wat kies om dit nie te doen nie omdat hulle nie die waarde daarvan insien nie. Op die oomblik lyk dit na die beste getuienis aan ons wêreld en vir ons openbare betrekkinge om die opdrag te eerbiedig, aangesien hulle nie teen ons geloof en God gekant is nie. Laat ons net sorg dat dit nie ons nuwe normaal word nie. Laat ons ons oog hou op ’n pad vorentoe waarop ons weer prakties as ’n plaaslike liggaam kan funksioneer.

Wat kan ons doen? Bid meer as ooit dat God dit sal gebruik om die verlorenes te red en die kerk te louter. Bestee tyd daaraan om verhoudings op te bou met dié na aan jou saam met wie jy aangemoedig is om tuis te bly. Laat hierdie pandemie ons voorberei op dit wat God vir ons in die toekoms het. Laat ons baie versigtig wees oor hoe ons oor die regering en sommige van die beslissings praat wat gedurende dit alles uitgevaardig is. Greetings of love in the name of Jesus, our Savior, our Redeemer, and our Lord. When our last magazine issue went out, most things in the world seemed to be continuing quite normally. Suddenly, everything started changing with unnerving speed and uncertainty. The next thing we knew a previously unheard-of virus had everyone’s attention. How our lives have changed.

Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2Pe 3:3-4. I had to think of this verse as Covid-19 started upending basically all of life. Where did the church find itself during this all? Surely, we weren’t scoffing… Hopefully we weren’t walking after our own lusts… But where were we? Maybe some of us had become lulled into the belief that things would continue according to what we understood as normal, at least for our indefinite future.

But suddenly what was once normal was gone. Schools closed—forcing many families to oversee their children’s education at home. Businesses closed—forcing many folks to find a way to work from home. Libraries closed—forcing folks to read at home. Daycare centers closed—forcing many parents to find a way for at least one of them to watch their own children at home. All personal care facilities (barber shops, nail parlors, etc.) closed—forcing many families to figure out how to take care of themselves and each other at home. All centers of entertainment closed—forcing families to start entertaining themselves and each other at home.

More and more families were required to stay at home without the opportunity of interacting with others. Many were the negative predictions by professionals, authorities, and the media—Domestic Violence would rise, Child Abuse would escalate, Addictions would increase, and Mental Illness would become a major problem.

As I am writing this, our state of Ohio has started relaxing the “stay at home” order, yet no matter how much someone may wish or worry, the old normal has yet to be willed back into existence. As time has passed, new normals have begun to develop. And yes, some of the negative predictions did come to pass, yet in the middle of it all some surprises have arisen as well.

**************************************

Recently, I came across an interesting article1 published by CNN titled, WHY SOME KIDS ARE HAPPIER RIGHT NOW, AND OTHER UNEXPECTED EFFECTS OF QUARANTINE. Surprisingly, this article didn’t appear to go viral nor did it seem to generate much attention in the media. To me, this type of information should be of interest to parents and children across the whole world, yet for some reason it didn’t seem to be the type of news that the majority of the media wanted to focus on.

Information like this runs counter to the direction the world is going. It would undermine way too much of the accepted system—daycare centers for children of working parents would go out of business; mothers would need to give up their careers and instead be stay-at-home moms; extra-curricular and after school activities for all the children in any given community would no longer be needed; children being raised by the system would instead be raised by their parents; emotional and mental struggles would no longer be treated primarily with therapy and drugs, and the list could go on.

Now on to the news article. In spite of their misgivings and apprehension about all the possible negatives of the whole family being at home together most of the time, hundreds of families from around the United States … shared on social media and in discussion boards a sense of relief and joy regarding the actual outcome after some time had passed. This outcome was unexpected by most, yet according to the research of professionals, it tracks with what we [they] know about the causes of childhood anxiety and depression today. This article states that according to the research one of the most well-supported explanations for this rise of mental health disorders is that children have too much going on and not enough choice over what they do. It’s a function of a whole society that is overworked and time-poor, and our kids are paying the price for it.

This article quoted parents from across the United States, including North Carolina, Tennessee and California. It discussed an interesting phenomenon, which was referred to as a happiness spike, among children during this unexpected disruption of normal hectic schedules. Much to their surprise and appreciation, the outcome of this happiness spike was counter-intuitive to what parents had fully expected would result.

According to one parent, the whole family now eats three unrushed and healthy meals together every day; the children are sleeping more and they are having a chance to get bored and then also having time to find a solution on their own. Finally, since they are going through this time of uncertainty and heightened emotion together, it has given them something to bond over.

Peter Gray, research professor of psychology at Boston College and author of the book FREE TO LEARN, says that “Suddenly kids are being able to [be self-directed]. They have time on a nice spring day to just sit outside and enjoy the sunshine. The things that are the subject of poetry that we have been denying our children are suddenly available to them. He believes that children need to develop healthily and happily—[have] time to play and explore.

A number of things were listed which parents, psychologists, and researchers see as results of this disruption in the normal schedules for many families.

  • They are seeing more of their parents
  • They have become better behaved
  • There is an increased camaraderie among siblings.
  • They are kinder to one another
  • They are playing more alone or with siblings
  • They are less emotionally overwhelmed
  • They are sleeping better

They talked about how children could now be children since they were no longer in the rat race of life. They now had time to explore their world, in their way. They had time to use their imagination and creativity. They were no longer under the pressure of rushing from one adult-scheduled appointment to another. No longer were they under the pressure to achieve a certain level or performance based on their peers. The article says that research shows that all these small acts can give them [children] a much-needed confidence boost.

According to the news article, the sense that they [children] are in control of their own lives and can handle disruptions on their own [is] a crucial element of emotional well-being. And surprise of surprises, emotional struggles and mental disorders started to correct themselves. According to one mother, her 12-year-old daughter who had been diagnosed with ADHD and with Autism Spectrum Disorder, began to see marked improvement after about two weeks. The change was so pronounced that the negative behavior that had been part of this girl’s identity due to her diagnosed disorders, actually began to return to that of a normal 12-year-old girl.

Bottomline… hundreds of families from around the United States are reporting that their children seem happier.

******************************************

While we realize that this is according to secular wisdom, most of it is simple, common sense derived from unbiased observation of the facts. Many of these conclusions are supported by the simple teaching of God’s Word, the Holy Bible. It is interesting to me how so many in the church today want to follow in the footsteps of the world when it comes to family structure, personal development, and child rearing. Some in the church have seemed to get to a point where they feel that God’s teaching is too simple, too old-fashioned, or for some other reason they believe it just doesn’t work to accomplish a successful outcome.

My goal in highlighting this news article is to help us see that the world’s system isn’t all its cracked up to be. It doesn’t produce the kind of fruit that we all are striving for. Let’s get back to believing in the Holy Scriptures, following them in simple obedience, and believing that God’s ways will work even in our times of uncertainty.

I will close with several thoughts that I wish to leave with us all. Within the last several weeks, I heard several thoughts that were shared by two different ministers. Both were regarding this virus issue and the world-wide disruption of normal schedules. First, even though this has seemed like a major obstacle for many of us to overcome, we can be sure that this will not be the last, nor will it be the worst. We can expect to face much more difficult situations as the end of time draws ever closer. Second, is the thought that we should look at this as a wake-up call to our spiritual lives. And that there should be NO person who doesn’t allow this to bring about change in their lives. There is NO human being that is so holy that they have no need of improvement where God is concerned.

Saudações de amor em nome de Jesus, nosso Salvador, nosso Redentor e nosso Senhor. Quando a última edição da nossa revista foi publicada, a maioria das coisas no mundo parecia continuar com bastante normalidade. De repente, tudo começou a mudar com uma velocidade e uma incerteza inquietantes. Quando nos demos conta, um vírus até então desconhecido havia atraído a atenção de todos. Como nossas vidas mudaram.

Sabendo primeiro isto: que nos últimos dias virão escarnecedores, andando segundo as suas próprias concupiscências e dizendo: Onde está a promessa da sua vinda? Porque, desde que os pais dormiram, todas as coisas permanecem como desde o princípio da criação –2Pe 3:3-4. Tive de pensar nesse versículo quando a Covid-19 começou a virar praticamente toda a vida de cabeça para baixo. Onde a igreja se encontrava em meio a tudo isso? Certamente, não estávamos escarnecendo… Esperemos que não estivéssemos andando segundo as nossas próprias concupiscências… Mas onde estávamos? Talvez alguns de nós tivessem sido embalados pela crença de que as coisas continuariam de acordo com o que entendíamos como normal, pelo menos no futuro indefinido.

Mas, de repente, o que antes era normal desapareceu. As escolas fecharam — obrigando muitas famílias a supervisionar a educação dos filhos em casa. As empresas fecharam — obrigando muitas pessoas a encontrar uma maneira de trabalhar em casa. As bibliotecas fecharam — obrigando as pessoas a ler em casa. As creches fecharam — obrigando muitos pais a encontrar uma maneira de pelo menos um deles cuidar dos próprios filhos em casa. Todos os estabelecimentos de cuidados pessoais (barbearias, salões de manicure etc.) fecharam — obrigando muitas famílias a descobrir como cuidar de si mesmas e umas das outras em casa. Todos os centros de entretenimento fecharam — obrigando as famílias a começar a entreter a si mesmas e umas às outras em casa.

Cada vez mais famílias tiveram de ficar em casa, sem a oportunidade de interagir com outras pessoas. Foram muitas as previsões negativas de profissionais, autoridades e da mídia — a violência doméstica aumentaria, os maus-tratos a crianças se agravariam, os vícios aumentariam e os transtornos mentais se tornariam um grande problema.

Enquanto escrevo isto, nosso estado de Ohio começou a flexibilizar a ordem de “ficar em casa”; ainda assim, por mais que alguém deseje ou se preocupe, não é possível fazer com que a antiga normalidade volte a existir. Com o passar do tempo, novas normalidades começaram a se desenvolver. E sim, algumas das previsões negativas se concretizaram, mas, em meio a tudo isso, também surgiram algumas surpresas.

**************************************

Recentemente, deparei-me com um artigo interessante1 publicado pela CNN, intitulado POR QUE ALGUMAS CRIANÇAS ESTÃO MAIS FELIZES AGORA E OUTROS EFEITOS INESPERADOS DA QUARENTENA. Surpreendentemente, esse artigo não pareceu se tornar viral nem gerar muita atenção na mídia. Para mim, esse tipo de informação deveria interessar a pais e filhos do mundo inteiro, mas, por alguma razão, não pareceu ser o tipo de notícia em que a maioria da mídia queria se concentrar.

Informações como essa vão contra a direção que o mundo está tomando. Elas abalariam demais o sistema aceito — creches para filhos de pais que trabalham fechariam as portas; as mães teriam de abandonar suas carreiras e, em vez disso, ficar em casa com os filhos; atividades extracurriculares e depois das aulas para todas as crianças de uma determinada comunidade deixariam de ser necessárias; crianças criadas pelo sistema passariam a ser criadas pelos pais; dificuldades emocionais e mentais deixariam de ser tratadas principalmente com terapia e medicamentos, e a lista poderia continuar.

Agora, passemos à notícia. Apesar das reservas e apreensões quanto a todos os possíveis aspectos negativos de toda a família ficar em casa junta a maior parte do tempo, centenas de famílias de diferentes partes dos Estados Unidos… compartilharam nas redes sociais e em fóruns de discussão uma sensação de alívio e alegria em relação ao resultado efetivo depois de algum tempo. Esse resultado foi inesperado para a maioria, mas, de acordo com as pesquisas de profissionais, está de acordo com o que [eles] sabem hoje sobre as causas da ansiedade e da depressão na infância. Este artigo afirma que, segundo as pesquisas, uma das explicações mais bem fundamentadas para o aumento dos transtornos de saúde mental é que as crianças têm coisas demais acontecendo e pouca liberdade de escolha sobre o que fazem. Isso é consequência de uma sociedade inteira sobrecarregada de trabalho e com pouco tempo, e nossos filhos estão pagando o preço por isso.

O artigo citou pais de diferentes partes dos Estados Unidos, incluindo Carolina do Norte, Tennessee e Califórnia. Falou de um fenômeno interessante, chamado de pico de felicidade, entre as crianças durante essa interrupção inesperada das rotinas agitadas. Para surpresa e satisfação dos pais, o resultado desse pico de felicidade foi o contrário do que eles esperavam plenamente que acontecesse.

Segundo um dos pais, agora toda a família faz três refeições saudáveis e sem pressa, juntos, todos os dias; as crianças estão dormindo mais e têm a oportunidade de ficar entediadas e também tempo para encontrar uma solução por conta própria. Por fim, como estão passando juntos por esse período de incerteza e emoções intensificadas, isso lhes deu algo que os une.

Peter Gray, professor pesquisador de psicologia no Boston College e autor do livro LIVRES PARA APRENDER, diz: “De repente, as crianças estão podendo [dirigir a si mesmas]. Têm tempo, num agradável dia de primavera, para simplesmente sentar do lado de fora e aproveitar o sol. As coisas que são tema de poesia, mas que temos negado às nossas crianças, de repente estão ao alcance delas. Ele acredita que as crianças precisam se desenvolver de forma saudável e feliz —[ter] tempo para brincar e explorar.

Foram enumeradas várias coisas que pais, psicólogos e pesquisadores veem como resultados dessa interrupção das rotinas normais de muitas famílias.

  • Estão vendo mais os pais
  • Passaram a se comportar melhor
  • Há mais companheirismo entre irmãos.
  • Estão sendo mais gentis uns com os outros
  • Estão brincando mais sozinhos ou com os irmãos
  • Estão menos sobrecarregadas emocionalmente
  • Estão dormindo melhor

Falaram sobre como as crianças agora podiam ser crianças, já que não estavam mais na corrida desenfreada da vida. Agora tinham tempo para explorar o mundo à sua maneira. Tinham tempo para usar a imaginação e a criatividade. Já não estavam sob a pressão de correr de um compromisso marcado por adultos para outro. Já não estavam sob a pressão de alcançar determinado nível ou desempenho com base no dos colegas. O artigo diz que as pesquisas mostram que todos esses pequenos atos podem dar a elas [às crianças] um necessário impulso de confiança.

Segundo a notícia, a sensação de que elas [as crianças] estão no controle das próprias vidas e conseguem lidar sozinhas com as interrupções [é] um elemento crucial do bem-estar emocional. E, para surpresa geral, as dificuldades emocionais e os transtornos mentais começaram a se corrigir. Segundo uma mãe, sua filha de 12 anos, diagnosticada com TDAH e transtorno do espectro autista, começou a apresentar uma melhora notável depois de cerca de duas semanas. A mudança foi tão acentuada que o comportamento negativo que fazia parte da identidade dessa menina por causa dos transtornos diagnosticados começou, de fato, a voltar ao de uma menina normal de 12 anos.

Em suma… centenas de famílias de diferentes partes dos Estados Unidos estão relatando que seus filhos parecem mais felizes.

******************************************

Embora reconheçamos que isso se baseia na sabedoria secular, a maior parte é simples bom senso, derivado de uma observação imparcial dos fatos. Muitas dessas conclusões são apoiadas pelo simples ensinamento da Palavra de Deus, a Bíblia Sagrada. Acho interessante que tantas pessoas na igreja hoje queiram seguir os passos do mundo no que diz respeito à estrutura familiar, ao desenvolvimento pessoal e à criação dos filhos. Algumas pessoas na igreja parecem ter chegado a um ponto em que sentem que o ensinamento de Deus é simples demais, antiquado demais ou, por alguma outra razão, acreditam que simplesmente não funciona para alcançar um resultado bem-sucedido.

Meu objetivo ao destacar essa notícia é nos ajudar a perceber que o sistema do mundo não é tudo aquilo que dizem. Ele não produz o tipo de fruto pelo qual todos nos esforçamos. Voltemos a crer nas Sagradas Escrituras, a segui-las em simples obediência e a acreditar que os caminhos de Deus funcionam até mesmo em nossos tempos de incerteza.

Concluirei com algumas reflexões que desejo deixar com todos nós. Nas últimas semanas, ouvi algumas reflexões compartilhadas por dois ministros diferentes. Ambas diziam respeito a essa questão do vírus e à interrupção mundial das rotinas normais. Primeiro, embora isso tenha parecido um grande obstáculo a ser superado por muitos de nós, podemos ter certeza de que não será o último, nem será o pior. Podemos esperar enfrentar situações muito mais difíceis à medida que o fim dos tempos se aproxima cada vez mais. Segundo, devemos encarar isso como um chamado para despertar para nossa vida espiritual. E não deve haver NINGUÉM que deixe de permitir que isso provoque uma mudança em sua vida. NÃO há ser humano tão santo que não precise melhorar no que diz respeito a Deus.

Who would have ever imagined that a little germ which cannot be seen with the human eye, has put the entire globe in a tizzy, a panic, and an economic disruption? I have not seen a pandemic of this magnitude in my lifetime and, when this first emerged, I was one of the gainsayers who could not believe it would cripple our world to this extent. Questions abound, conspiracy theories are propagated, and fear has run rampant throughout the world as the entire globe responds to the pandemic. Will there be a cure, or will this continue to be a scourge in our world? If this little virus trespasses into my physical body, what is the chance of survival? Will it affect any of my loved ones? The questions are innumerable. Where it has come from has been theorized by many, but does anyone really know? Where is God in the whole thing? Did it surprise Him? Is it God’s judgment on humanity? These and many other questions are being asked by many sincere people and the answers that are given often contradict one another.

One of the outfalls of the pandemic is the government invasion into the church and our personal lives in a way that has been unprecedented in my and your lifetime. Suddenly, we are faced with decisions that many of us have not thought through. When, and how much, should the government mandate things in our lives when we clearly believe in separation of Church and state? What are my rights? What will I do if I lose my business? Will I cash in the stimulus check that is supposed to arrive in the mail in the near future?

There is a verse in Peter that reminds me that if anyone should have answers in this time of pandemic, we as Christians should. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: –1Pe 3:15. We may not know the origin of the virus, nor the outcome, but we do know Who knows all things, and that it was not a surprise to Him. It is the right time to turn to the Lord Jesus Christ, the One who holds all things by the power of His Word. If anytime in recent history the Christian has an opportunity to be salt in the earth and light in the world, it is during this time of upheaval. So, what should the response of the Christian be?

Consider this verse in Luke: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth… –Luk 21:26. For the Christian, earthquakes, famines, and pestilence should be no surprise since they have been prophesied to us through the Word of God. And while these things are happening and will happen, God has provided clear scriptural mandates for us as Christians to follow. We are clearly commanded in the scripture to not worry about tomorrow: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Mat 6:34.

So, we as Jesus’ disciples know that God will give us wisdom and grace for the difficulties of today. We are commanded to not borrow tomorrow’s troubles. We need to be reminded once again, in this time, as always, God will provide grace for today that will be great enough to sustain peace in the midst of the storm, and will provide it tomorrow if we live. Let us learn a lesson from Peter and the disciples—to focus on Jesus. We need to trust Jesus even when He seems to be asleep in the boat, rather than focusing on the storm that is raging all around us. Jesus was in control whether he was sleeping or awake and still is. But we might say, “How do I know if I will have food or clothing, or my business tomorrow?” And again, we hear the Savior say, “Look at the lilies, the fowls of the air, and learn a lesson from them!” We cannot even do some of the simplest things by God’s estimation, like add a cubit to our stature, so why would we try to deal with the hard things of providing for a tomorrow that is out of our control? Do these commands fit for the year 2020 and the pandemic that we are facing? I am sure that, in theory, we can agree, but can we internalize these verses and make them a very prominent place in our lives today?

There are principles given in God’s Word that, if we have not embraced them, we will also ‘reel in a tizzy’ when faced with things like the pandemic that is completely out of our control. One of those principles is the clear teaching that suffering is a way of life for the follower of Jesus. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17.

The ‘health and wealth’ gospel that is peddled by many preachers today is a false doctrine and can leave a person reeling when they are faced with health or economic loss. We need to be okay with suffering, we need to embrace it; we need to arm ourselves with the same mind as Christ. The loss of our business, home and yes, even our own lives also, by economic disaster, storms, or accidents is not outside the realm of the will of God for the Christian. We know that God can eliminate any of these calamities and will protect us from them all IF He so wills. But whether He does or not is God’s prerogative and we are the happiest IF we surrender our lives completely to Him in faith, and trust Him to keep us, whether with little or with much.

Another principle we need to reckon with is that we have no rights except the right to the Tree of Life. For us as Christians it makes little difference if we are citizens of the United States or not. We have many privileges for which we are very grateful for, but we should not think we have a right to own, keep, or buy, or that we have a stake to claim in this world. In the Holy Scriptures we are reminded that we are but pilgrims and strangers here (see Heb 11:13-16). As Abraham and the other patriarchs, we have no abiding city here but look for a city …whose builder and maker is God –Heb 11:10.

There are plenty of lawyers offering to fight for our rights, but the truth of the matter is, our citizenship is in Heaven and we are just ambassadors here and can be kicked out by society and need to leave all anytime without a moment’s hesitation. If this will be a reality, we need to live our lives with all our things held with an open hand. We do not have the right (only the privilege)—to own land, to have enough food, to enjoy good health, and to live without suffering—nor should we fight for those so-called rights, but we, God’s people, must put on the mind of Christ and be willing to leave all behind for the sake of Christ and trust Him completely for our sustenance. Jesus said He sees one sparrow fall to the ground and reminds us that we are worth more than many sparrows. Jesus calls us to hate all that we hold dear here on this earth: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple –Luk 14:26.

As Christians, we do not plan to stay here on this earth; we are anticipating Heaven. The scriptures express this sentiment when it not only considers the whole earth groaning to be delivered from this death and decay, but that we ourselves are also groaning to be delivered. Should there be such a strong pull to be here that our hearts fail us …for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth…? –Luk 21:26. Should we much rather cry out “how long Lord Jesus” “so come”? Even as the apostle intimates as he wrestles with being “betwixt two”—For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. –Php 1:23-24. The apostle clearly indicates “having a desire to depart and be with Christ is far better,” and the only thing that holds him here is the fact that there is work to be done.

Another area we should be awake to, is our vulnerability during this time of no church services. We may be tempted to go on-line and be fed spiritually by those who are false prophets or those who teach false doctrine. We need to “try the spirits” and know whose feet we are sitting at. Be selective to whom you might listen, or from whom you might allow your family to take nourishment. We, as fathers, are called to lead and lead we must. The burden is on our shoulders to help our families navigate through these uncertain times. We as fathers may need to be more proactive during this time. It is a call to us to rise up and lead our wives and children. Not only do we have to watch “whose feet we are sitting at”, but we need to lead our families with confidence, calling them to trust in God, and leading them in prayers of faith. We need to provide them with an example of faith and trust in God that no amount of buffeting will shake. This time of upheaval will not knock us off our feet IF we are rooted and grounded in Christ.

At a time like this, we need to make wise decisions, even decisions concerning the future, but still refrain from falling into the panic mode and running around as if we have no Heavenly Father. We also need to lead our families in being careful not to believe everything that one hears, but to be aware of where our news is coming from and to consider how reliable it is. Conspiracy theories abound concerning how this virus started and the political agenda theorized to be behind it. Refrain from spending time following these conspirators and rather follow the scripture mandate, “casting down imaginations.” The simple truth is this, we do not know, and if we did know it still should not change the way we live and our overall response. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, of love and a sound mind. John tells us to not “believe every spirit, but to try the spirits to see whether they be of God.”

I believe that this is an awesome opportunity to reach out to our fellow brothers and sisters by praying for one another and by staying in touch so that we can ‘weep with those that weep’ and ‘rejoice with those that rejoice’. Some of us have jobs and some do not. God’s Word tells us that those who have are to give to those who do not have so that there may be an equality. It is a time to reach out to the elderly in our church or community and stay in touch by mail or phone. This is a time in which the lonely will only get lonelier. A cheery word, or a letter in the mail, and whatever other resources you can appropriately use may be just the thing that those around you need.

During the times of mandatory “stay at home”, there is a whole group of our society that will face challenges that they have not seen up to this time. According to various news sources there has been an increase in domestic violence since family members are spending much more time together than they normally do. But let this not once be named among us. This is the time for us as God’s children to maximize on “in home” relationships. The Bible calls us to “redeem the time” and this can be done by making the most of our time together as a family. Spend time together—reading the Bible, praying together, singing together, and just simply doing enjoyable things together—things that will nurture growth and love in our relationships. We need to be creative as fathers in bringing our family together in a way that will produce an atmosphere of unity and oneness.

One question that begs an answer is this, “Should the government dictate whether we have church or not?” This is something we need to answer since for some areas of the country it is more than a suggestion but has become mandatory. I believe that since the suggestion/order to not meet together during this time is for the purpose of not spreading a virus that is quite contagious, this then fulfills the scripture “to love our neighbor as ourselves.” It is a good opportunity to show the public that if the mandate does not ask us to violate the scripture, then we choose to honor the government. There may come a time soon enough that we will be asked to do something that we cannot do with a clear conscience and then we will need to stand and “obey God rather than men.”

Some feel a twang of guilt because of the verse, “to not forsake the assembling of ourselves together”, however, this seems to be addressing a habit or a way of life. I suppose this is dealing with the lazy, slothful heart that does not see the benefit of getting together. We want to get together… As soon as we can get together again, we will take advantage of it. There is a big difference between those who cannot get together for a short time and those that choose not to since they do not see the value of it. For the present time, it seems the best testimony to our world and public relations to honor the mandate since they are not fighting against our faith and God. Let’s just take care to not let this become our new normal. Let’s keep our eye on a path forward to once again practically function as a local body.

What can we do? Pray more than ever that God would use this to win the lost and refine the church. Spend time building relationships with those you are closest to and have been encouraged to stay home with. Let this pandemic prepare us for what God has for us in the future. Let us be very careful how we talk about the government and some of the rulings that have come out through this all. We are called to honor the king and we need to spend more time thanking God for our freedoms than maximizing on the negative—I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; –1Ti 2:1-3. For the Christian, …we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Rom 8:28.

Siapa yang pernah membayangkan bahwa kuman kecil yang tidak dapat dilihat dengan mata telanjang akan membuat seluruh dunia gempar, panik, dan mengalami kekacauan ekonomi? Saya belum pernah menyaksikan pandemi sebesar ini seumur hidup saya dan, ketika hal ini pertama kali muncul, saya termasuk orang yang meragukannya dan tidak percaya bahwa pandemi ini akan melumpuhkan dunia kita sedemikian rupa. Banyak pertanyaan bermunculan, teori konspirasi tersebar, dan ketakutan merajalela di seluruh dunia sementara semua orang menanggapi pandemi ini. Akankah ada obatnya, ataukah hal ini akan terus menjadi malapetaka di dunia kita? Jika virus kecil ini masuk ke dalam tubuh saya, seberapa besar peluang saya untuk bertahan hidup? Akankah virus ini berdampak pada orang-orang terkasih saya? Pertanyaannya tak terhitung banyaknya. Banyak orang telah mengemukakan teori tentang asal-usulnya, tetapi apakah ada yang benar-benar tahu? Di manakah Allah dalam semua ini? Apakah hal ini mengejutkan-Nya? Apakah ini penghakiman Allah atas umat manusia? Banyak orang tulus mengajukan pertanyaan-pertanyaan ini dan banyak pertanyaan lainnya, dan jawaban yang diberikan sering kali saling bertentangan.

Salah satu dampak pandemi ini adalah campur tangan pemerintah dalam gereja dan kehidupan pribadi kita dengan cara yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya selama hidup saya maupun Anda. Tiba-tiba, kita dihadapkan pada keputusan-keputusan yang belum pernah dipikirkan matang-matang oleh banyak dari kita. Kapan, dan sejauh mana, pemerintah seharusnya mewajibkan hal-hal tertentu dalam kehidupan kita, sementara kita jelas percaya pada pemisahan gereja dan negara? Apa hak-hak saya? Apa yang akan saya lakukan jika kehilangan usaha saya? Akankah saya mencairkan cek bantuan stimulus yang konon akan tiba melalui pos dalam waktu dekat?

Ada ayat dalam surat Petrus yang mengingatkan saya bahwa jika ada yang seharusnya memiliki jawaban pada masa pandemi ini, kita sebagai orang Kristenlah yang seharusnya memilikinya. Tetapi kuduskanlah Tuhan Allah di dalam hatimu: dan hendaklah kamu selalu siap sedia untuk memberi jawaban kepada setiap orang yang meminta pertanggungjawaban tentang pengharapan yang ada padamu, dengan lemah lembut dan hormat: –1Ptr 3:15. Kita mungkin tidak tahu asal-usul virus ini ataupun bagaimana kesudahannya, tetapi kita tahu Siapa yang mengetahui segala sesuatu, dan bahwa hal ini tidak mengejutkan-Nya. Inilah saat yang tepat untuk berpaling kepada Tuhan Yesus Kristus, Dia yang menopang segala sesuatu dengan kuasa Firman-Nya. Jika dalam sejarah belakangan ini orang Kristen pernah memiliki kesempatan untuk menjadi garam di bumi dan terang di dunia, maka kesempatan itu adalah pada masa pergolakan ini. Jadi, bagaimana seharusnya tanggapan orang Kristen?

Pertimbangkan ayat ini dalam Lukas: Orang-orang akan mati ketakutan karena mengkhawatirkan segala sesuatu yang akan menimpa bumi… –Luk 21:26. Bagi orang Kristen, gempa bumi, kelaparan, dan wabah penyakit seharusnya bukanlah hal yang mengejutkan, sebab semuanya telah dinubuatkan kepada kita melalui Firman Allah. Dan sementara hal-hal ini sedang terjadi dan akan terjadi, Allah telah memberikan perintah-perintah yang jelas dalam Kitab Suci untuk kita ikuti sebagai orang Kristen. Dalam Kitab Suci kita dengan jelas diperintahkan untuk tidak khawatir tentang hari esok: Sebab itu janganlah kamu kuatir akan hari besok, karena hari besok mempunyai kesusahannya sendiri. Cukuplah kesusahan sehari untuk sehari –Mat 6:34.

Jadi, kita sebagai murid-murid Yesus tahu bahwa Allah akan memberi kita hikmat dan anugerah untuk menghadapi kesulitan hari ini. Kita diperintahkan agar tidak memikul kesusahan hari esok. Kita perlu diingatkan sekali lagi bahwa pada masa ini, seperti biasanya, Allah akan menyediakan anugerah untuk hari ini yang cukup besar untuk memelihara damai sejahtera di tengah badai, dan akan menyediakannya juga esok hari jika kita masih hidup. Marilah kita belajar dari Petrus dan murid-murid lainnya—memusatkan perhatian kepada Yesus. Kita perlu memercayai Yesus bahkan ketika tampaknya Ia tertidur di dalam perahu, alih-alih memusatkan perhatian pada badai yang mengamuk di sekeliling kita. Yesus tetap berkuasa, baik ketika Ia tidur maupun terjaga, dan sampai sekarang pun demikian. Namun, mungkin kita berkata, “Bagaimana saya tahu apakah besok saya akan punya makanan atau pakaian, atau apakah usaha saya akan tetap ada?” Sekali lagi, kita mendengar Sang Juruselamat berkata, “Lihatlah bunga bakung dan burung-burung di udara, dan belajarlah dari mereka!” Menurut penilaian Allah, kita bahkan tidak mampu melakukan beberapa hal yang paling sederhana, seperti menambah sehasta pada tinggi badan kita. Jadi, mengapa kita mencoba menangani perkara-perkara sulit, yaitu menyediakan kebutuhan untuk hari esok yang berada di luar kendali kita? Apakah perintah-perintah ini berlaku untuk tahun 2020 dan pandemi yang sedang kita hadapi? Saya yakin secara teori kita dapat menyetujuinya, tetapi dapatkah kita meresapi ayat-ayat ini dan menjadikannya bagian yang sangat menonjol dalam kehidupan kita saat ini?

Ada prinsip-prinsip yang diberikan dalam Firman Allah, dan jika kita belum menerimanya, kita juga akan “limbung dalam kegemparan” ketika menghadapi hal-hal seperti pandemi yang sepenuhnya berada di luar kendali kita. Salah satu prinsip itu adalah ajaran yang jelas bahwa penderitaan merupakan bagian dari kehidupan pengikut Yesus. Dan jika kita adalah anak-anak, maka kita juga ahli waris, yakni ahli waris Allah dan ahli waris bersama Kristus; yaitu jika kita menderita bersama-sama dengan Dia, supaya kita juga dipermuliakan bersama-sama dengan Dia –Rm 8:17.

Injil “kesehatan dan kemakmuran” yang disebarkan banyak pengkhotbah masa kini adalah ajaran palsu dan dapat membuat seseorang limbung ketika menghadapi kehilangan kesehatan atau kerugian ekonomi. Kita perlu menerima penderitaan; kita perlu merangkulnya; kita perlu memperlengkapi diri dengan pikiran yang sama seperti Kristus. Kehilangan usaha, rumah, dan bahkan nyawa kita sendiri akibat bencana ekonomi, badai, atau kecelakaan, juga tidak berada di luar lingkup kehendak Allah bagi orang Kristen. Kita tahu bahwa Allah dapat meniadakan semua malapetaka ini dan akan melindungi kita darinya jika memang demikian kehendak-Nya. Namun, apakah Ia melakukannya atau tidak merupakan hak Allah, dan kita paling berbahagia JIKA kita menyerahkan hidup kita sepenuhnya kepada-Nya dalam iman, serta memercayai-Nya untuk memelihara kita, baik dalam kekurangan maupun kelimpahan.

Prinsip lain yang perlu kita pahami ialah bahwa kita tidak memiliki hak apa pun selain hak atas Pohon Kehidupan. Bagi kita sebagai orang Kristen, tidak banyak bedanya apakah kita warga negara Amerika Serikat atau bukan. Kita memiliki banyak hak istimewa yang sangat kita syukuri, tetapi kita tidak seharusnya berpikir bahwa kita berhak memiliki, mempertahankan, atau membeli sesuatu, atau bahwa kita memiliki bagian yang dapat kita tuntut di dunia ini. Dalam Kitab Suci kita diingatkan bahwa kita hanyalah pendatang dan orang asing di sini (lihat Ibr 11:13-16). Seperti Abraham dan para bapa leluhur lainnya, kita tidak mempunyai kota yang tetap di sini, tetapi menantikan sebuah kota …yang direncanakan dan dibangun oleh Allah –Ibr 11:10.

Banyak pengacara menawarkan diri untuk memperjuangkan hak-hak kita, tetapi kenyataannya, kewargaan kita adalah di Surga dan kita hanyalah duta-duta di sini; masyarakat dapat mengusir kita dan kita harus meninggalkan semuanya kapan saja tanpa ragu sedikit pun. Jika hal ini akan menjadi kenyataan, kita perlu menjalani hidup dengan memegang segala sesuatu secara terbuka, tanpa menggenggamnya erat-erat. Kita tidak berhak (kita hanya memiliki hak istimewa)—untuk memiliki tanah, memperoleh cukup makanan, menikmati kesehatan yang baik, dan hidup tanpa penderitaan—dan kita juga tidak seharusnya memperjuangkan apa yang disebut hak-hak itu. Sebaliknya, kita, umat Allah, harus mengenakan pikiran Kristus dan bersedia meninggalkan semuanya demi Kristus serta memercayai-Nya sepenuhnya untuk mencukupi kebutuhan kita. Yesus berkata bahwa Ia melihat seekor burung pipit jatuh ke tanah dan mengingatkan kita bahwa kita lebih berharga daripada banyak burung pipit. Yesus memanggil kita untuk membenci semua yang kita sayangi di bumi ini: Jikalau seorang datang kepada-Ku dan ia tidak membenci bapanya, ibunya, isterinya, anak-anaknya, saudara-saudaranya laki-laki atau perempuan, bahkan nyawanya sendiri, ia tidak dapat menjadi murid-Ku –Luk 14:26.

Sebagai orang Kristen, kita tidak berencana untuk menetap di bumi ini; kita menantikan Surga. Kitab Suci mengungkapkan perasaan ini dengan menyatakan bukan hanya bahwa seluruh bumi mengeluh sambil menantikan pembebasan dari kematian dan kebinasaan ini, tetapi juga bahwa kita sendiri mengeluh sambil menantikan pembebasan. Apakah tarikan untuk tetap tinggal di sini seharusnya begitu kuat sehingga hati kita menjadi lemah …karena ketakutan dan karena mengkhawatirkan segala sesuatu yang akan menimpa bumi…? –Luk 21:26. Bukankah seharusnya kita justru berseru, “berapa lama lagi, Tuhan Yesus,” “datanglah”? Demikianlah yang tersirat dalam perkataan rasul itu ketika ia bergumul karena “di antara dua pilihan”—Karena aku terdesak oleh dua pilihan: aku ingin pergi dan diam bersama-sama dengan Kristus—itu memang jauh lebih baik; tetapi lebih perlu untuk tinggal di dunia ini karena kamu. –Flp 1:23-24. Rasul itu dengan jelas menyatakan bahwa “ingin pergi dan diam bersama Kristus memang jauh lebih baik,” dan satu-satunya hal yang menahannya di sini adalah kenyataan bahwa masih ada pekerjaan yang harus dilakukan.

Bidang lain yang perlu kita waspadai adalah kerentanan kita selama masa tanpa ibadah gereja. Kita mungkin tergoda untuk membuka internet dan menerima makanan rohani dari nabi-nabi palsu atau mereka yang mengajarkan ajaran palsu. Kita perlu “menguji roh-roh” dan mengetahui di kaki siapa kita duduk. Pilihlah dengan cermat siapa yang akan Anda dengarkan, atau dari siapa Anda mengizinkan keluarga Anda menerima asupan rohani. Kita sebagai para ayah dipanggil untuk memimpin, dan kita harus memimpin. Tanggung jawab untuk membantu keluarga kita melewati masa-masa yang tidak pasti ini berada di pundak kita. Pada masa ini, kita sebagai ayah mungkin perlu lebih proaktif. Ini adalah panggilan bagi kita untuk bangkit dan memimpin istri serta anak-anak kita. Kita bukan hanya harus memperhatikan “di kaki siapa kita duduk”, tetapi juga perlu memimpin keluarga kita dengan keyakinan, mengajak mereka untuk percaya kepada Allah, dan memimpin mereka dalam doa-doa iman. Kita perlu menjadi teladan iman dan kepercayaan kepada Allah yang tidak tergoyahkan oleh tekanan sebesar apa pun. Masa pergolakan ini tidak akan membuat kita jatuh JIKA kita berakar dan berlandaskan di dalam Kristus.

Pada saat seperti ini, kita perlu mengambil keputusan-keputusan bijaksana, bahkan keputusan mengenai masa depan, tetapi tetap menahan diri agar tidak panik dan berlarian seolah-olah kita tidak mempunyai Bapa di Surga. Kita juga perlu memimpin keluarga kita agar berhati-hati dan tidak memercayai segala sesuatu yang didengar, melainkan menyadari dari mana berita yang kita peroleh berasal dan mempertimbangkan seberapa dapat diandalkannya berita itu. Teori konspirasi berlimpah mengenai bagaimana virus ini bermula dan agenda politik yang konon berada di baliknya. Jangan habiskan waktu mengikuti para penganut teori konspirasi ini; sebaliknya, ikutilah perintah Kitab Suci, “meruntuhkan khayalan-khayalan.” Kebenaran sederhananya adalah bahwa kita tidak tahu, dan sekalipun kita tahu, hal itu tetap tidak seharusnya mengubah cara hidup dan tanggapan kita secara keseluruhan. Allah tidak memberikan kepada kita roh ketakutan, melainkan roh yang membangkitkan kekuatan, kasih, dan pikiran yang sehat. Yohanes mengatakan kepada kita untuk tidak “percaya kepada setiap roh, tetapi menguji roh-roh itu untuk mengetahui apakah mereka berasal dari Allah.”

Saya percaya bahwa ini adalah kesempatan luar biasa untuk menjangkau saudara-saudari kita dengan saling mendoakan dan tetap berhubungan, supaya kita dapat “menangis dengan orang yang menangis” dan “bersukacita dengan orang yang bersukacita”. Sebagian dari kita memiliki pekerjaan dan sebagian lagi tidak. Firman Allah mengatakan bahwa mereka yang memiliki harus memberi kepada mereka yang tidak memiliki, supaya ada kesetaraan. Inilah saatnya menjangkau para lanjut usia di gereja atau masyarakat kita dan tetap berhubungan melalui surat atau telepon. Pada masa ini, mereka yang kesepian akan semakin kesepian. Sepatah kata yang menghibur, surat yang dikirim lewat pos, dan apa pun sumber daya lain yang dapat Anda gunakan dengan tepat mungkin merupakan hal yang dibutuhkan orang-orang di sekitar Anda.

Selama masa “wajib tinggal di rumah”, ada sekelompok besar masyarakat kita yang akan menghadapi tantangan-tantangan yang belum pernah mereka alami sebelumnya. Menurut berbagai sumber berita, kekerasan dalam rumah tangga meningkat karena anggota keluarga menghabiskan waktu bersama jauh lebih banyak daripada biasanya. Namun, jangan sampai hal seperti ini sekalipun disebut di antara kita. Inilah saatnya bagi kita sebagai anak-anak Allah untuk memaksimalkan hubungan “di dalam rumah”. Alkitab memanggil kita untuk “mempergunakan waktu yang ada”, dan hal ini dapat dilakukan dengan memanfaatkan sebaik-baiknya waktu yang kita habiskan bersama sebagai keluarga. Luangkan waktu bersama—membaca Alkitab, berdoa bersama, bernyanyi bersama, dan sekadar melakukan hal-hal menyenangkan bersama—hal-hal yang akan memupuk pertumbuhan dan kasih dalam hubungan kita. Sebagai ayah, kita perlu kreatif dalam menyatukan keluarga dengan cara yang akan menciptakan suasana persatuan dan kebersamaan.

Satu pertanyaan yang menuntut jawaban ialah, “Haruskah pemerintah menentukan apakah kita boleh beribadah bersama atau tidak?” Ini perlu kita jawab karena di beberapa wilayah negara ini, hal tersebut bukan sekadar imbauan, melainkan sudah diwajibkan. Saya percaya bahwa karena imbauan/perintah untuk tidak berkumpul selama masa ini bertujuan agar virus yang sangat menular tidak menyebar, hal ini memenuhi perintah Kitab Suci untuk “mengasihi sesamamu seperti dirimu sendiri.” Ini kesempatan yang baik untuk menunjukkan kepada masyarakat bahwa jika perintah itu tidak meminta kita melanggar Kitab Suci, kita memilih untuk menghormati pemerintah. Tidak lama lagi mungkin akan tiba saatnya kita diminta melakukan sesuatu yang tidak dapat kita lakukan dengan hati nurani yang bersih, dan saat itu kita perlu berdiri teguh dan “lebih taat kepada Allah daripada kepada manusia.”

Beberapa orang merasa sedikit bersalah karena ayat yang mengatakan, “janganlah kita menjauhkan diri dari pertemuan-pertemuan ibadah kita,” tetapi tampaknya ayat ini membahas suatu kebiasaan atau cara hidup. Saya kira ayat ini membahas hati yang malas dan lalai, yang tidak melihat manfaat berkumpul. Kita ingin berkumpul… Segera setelah kita dapat berkumpul lagi, kita akan memanfaatkannya. Ada perbedaan besar antara mereka yang tidak dapat berkumpul untuk sementara waktu dan mereka yang memilih untuk tidak berkumpul karena tidak melihat nilainya. Untuk saat ini, tampaknya kesaksian terbaik bagi dunia dan hubungan baik dengan masyarakat dapat ditunjukkan dengan menghormati perintah tersebut, karena mereka tidak sedang menentang iman dan Allah kita. Marilah kita berhati-hati agar hal ini tidak menjadi kebiasaan baru kita. Marilah kita tetap mengarahkan pandangan pada jalan ke depan agar kita dapat kembali menjalankan fungsi sebagai tubuh setempat secara nyata.

Apa yang dapat kita lakukan? Berdoalah lebih sungguh-sungguh daripada sebelumnya agar Allah memakai hal ini untuk memenangkan orang-orang yang terhilang dan memurnikan gereja. Luangkan waktu untuk membangun hubungan dengan orang-orang terdekat yang telah dianjurkan kepada Anda untuk tinggal di rumah bersama mereka. Biarlah pandemi ini mempersiapkan kita menghadapi apa yang Allah sediakan bagi kita di masa depan. Marilah kita sangat berhati-hati dalam berbicara tentang pemerintah dan beberapa peraturan yang dikeluarkan selama masa ini. Kita dipanggil untuk menghormati raja, dan kita perlu meluangkan lebih banyak waktu untuk bersyukur kepada Allah atas kebebasan kita daripada berfokus pada hal-hal negatif—Karena itu aku menasihatkan: pertama-tama, naikkanlah permohonan, doa syafaat, dan ucapan syukur untuk semua orang, untuk raja-raja dan semua pembesar, agar kita dapat hidup tenang dan tenteram dalam segala kesalehan dan kehormatan. Itulah yang baik dan berkenan kepada Allah, Juruselamat kita; –1Tim 2:1-3. Bagi orang Kristen, …kita tahu bahwa Allah turut bekerja dalam segala sesuatu untuk mendatangkan kebaikan bagi mereka yang mengasihi Allah, yaitu bagi mereka yang terpanggil sesuai dengan rencana-Nya –Rm 8:28.
