Joel had a serious problem of taking things which did not belong to him. Sometimes he would sneak mother’s freshly baked cookies from the cookie jar, or he would take Nathan’s magic markers without asking to use them. To make matters worse, Joel would lie or make excuses when he was caught. Mother and Father had to punish Joel many times. They told him that if he continued to take small things without asking for permission, it could lead to stealing bigger things as he grew older.

And God hates stealing!

One day Mother took Joel and Nathan to Weaver’s Country Store to buy shoes. “Look Mother,” Joel said excitedly, pointing to the shiny pocketknives on the counter. “Will you please buy one for me?”

“No, Joel,” Mother replied. “You must wait until you are older for a pocketknife.”

“O.K.,” Joel answered rather disappointedly.

Later, while Mother was fitting shoes on Nathan, Joel wandered front to the pocketknives again. He looked at them longingly. “That white one is a beauty,” he thought to himself. “Oh, if only I could have it! Mother just does not understand that I am old enough to have one. All the other boys my age have pocketknives.” Just then another ugly thought entered his head. “I think I will just take that white one. No one will ever know.” Joel glanced toward the back of the store where Mr. Weaver was helping fit shoes on Nathan. No one was looking, so he quickly reached up, took the white pocketknife from the box on the counter, and stuck it into his pocket.

Turning nervously, Joel walked back up the aisle. His head started to pound, and his heart was thumping so hard he was afraid everyone could hear it. He hoped Mother would take more time fitting shoes on Nathan. Then maybe she would not notice how hot and red his face was getting. Mother always seemed to notice when something was wrong.

But Mother did not notice this time, and soon they were on their way home. After several days, Joel discovered that it was not fun having a stolen pocketknife. He could hardly ever use it for fear of getting caught. He had to keep it well hidden most of the time!

Several weeks passed. Then one evening, Nathan came into the kitchen where Joel and Mother were doing the supper dishes. “Look, Mother! I found this pocketknife under the couch cushion. I wonder where it came from?”

Joel’s heart began to thump wildly as he watched Mother examine the pocketknife. He wished he could dash outside and disappear. He had just slipped the pocketknife under the couch cushion that evening when Mother had walked into the parlor unexpectedly as she announced that supper was ready. He never thought someone would find it there.

Suddenly he realized Mother was looking at him. “Joel, do you know where this comes from?” she asked.

“Oh! Err – well – ah – I think Cousin Mike has a white one like that,” Joel stammered. “It – ah – it probably slipped out of his pocket the other evening when they were here visiting.”

“I see… Well, I will need to ask Aunt Eva about this,” Mother replied calmly as she placed the pocketknife on the window shelf.

Joel felt miserable. It seemed as if Mother’s sad eyes were watching every move he made. Oh, how he wished he had never stolen that pocketknife! Every time he looked at it, sitting there on the shelf, it seemed to grow larger in size! He decided to go to bed early, but when he closed his eyes, all he saw was that ugly, white pocketknife, leering at him from the window shelf!

The next day, Mother called Joel to her. She was holding the white pocketknife. “I called Aunt Eva today, and she said that Mike does not have a pocketknife. Now Joel, tell me… where did you get this pocketknife? And remember, it does not pay to lie,” Mother said firmly as she placed her hand under his chin and raised his drooping head to look into his eyes.

“I – ah – took it from Weaver’s Store,” Joel stammered.

“Do you realize that was stealing?” Mother asked.

“Yes, I do, and I – I am sorry I lied about it too. I will never do anything like that again. I – ah – I felt so awful ever since I stole it,” choked Joel as his body shook with sobs.

“I am glad to hear you say that Joel,” Mother said. “Father and I have been asking God to help you with this problem of lying and stealing. This evening when Father comes home, you will need to tell him all about it, then Father and I will decide what your punishment should be. After that, we will take you back to the store and you can give the pocketknife to Mr. Weaver. Also, since you used the knife, you will need to pay for it with your own money.”

How Joel dreaded facing Father and Mr. Weaver, but later when it was all over, he felt so much better. That day Joel learned a lesson he never forgot.

Ο Τζόελ είχε ένα σοβαρό πρόβλημα: έπαιρνε πράγματα που δεν του ανήκαν. Μερικές φορές τρύπωνε κρυφά και έπαιρνε τα φρεσκοψημένα μπισκότα της μητέρας του από το κουτί, ή έπαιρνε τους μαρκαδόρους του Νέιθαν χωρίς να ζητήσει την άδειά του. Και σαν να μην έφτανε αυτό, ο Τζόελ έλεγε ψέματα ή έβρισκε δικαιολογίες όταν τον έπιαναν. Η μητέρα και ο πατέρας έπρεπε να τον τιμωρήσουν πολλές φορές. Του έλεγαν πως, αν συνέχιζε να παίρνει μικροπράγματα χωρίς να ζητά άδεια, μεγαλώνοντας θα μπορούσε να φτάσει να κλέβει μεγαλύτερα πράγματα.

Και ο Θεός μισεί την κλοπή!

Μια μέρα η μητέρα πήρε τον Τζόελ και τον Νέιθαν στο επαρχιακό κατάστημα του Γουίβερ για να αγοράσουν παπούτσια. «Κοίτα, μαμά», είπε ενθουσιασμένος ο Τζόελ, δείχνοντας τα γυαλιστερά σουγιαδάκια στον πάγκο. «Σε παρακαλώ, θα μου αγοράσεις ένα;»

«Όχι, Τζόελ», απάντησε η μητέρα. «Πρέπει να περιμένεις μέχρι να μεγαλώσεις για να αποκτήσεις σουγιαδάκι.»

«Εντάξει», απάντησε ο Τζόελ κάπως απογοητευμένος.

Αργότερα, ενώ η μητέρα δοκίμαζε παπούτσια στον Νέιθαν, ο Τζόελ περιπλανήθηκε ξανά προς το μπροστινό μέρος του καταστήματος, εκεί όπου βρίσκονταν τα σουγιαδάκια. Τα κοίταζε με λαχτάρα. «Εκείνο το άσπρο είναι πανέμορφο», σκέφτηκε. «Αχ, και να μπορούσα να το έχω! Η μαμά απλώς δεν καταλαβαίνει ότι είμαι αρκετά μεγάλος για να έχω ένα. Όλα τα άλλα αγόρια της ηλικίας μου έχουν σουγιαδάκια». Εκείνη τη στιγμή τού ήρθε στο μυαλό άλλη μια άσχημη σκέψη. «Λέω να πάρω αυτό το άσπρο. Κανείς δεν θα το μάθει ποτέ». Ο Τζόελ κοίταξε προς το πίσω μέρος του καταστήματος, όπου ο κύριος Γουίβερ βοηθούσε τον Νέιθαν να δοκιμάσει παπούτσια. Κανείς δεν τον κοιτούσε, κι έτσι άπλωσε γρήγορα το χέρι, πήρε το άσπρο σουγιαδάκι από το κουτί στον πάγκο και το έχωσε στην τσέπη του.

Γυρίζοντας νευρικά, ο Τζόελ περπάτησε πίσω στον διάδρομο. Το κεφάλι του άρχισε να χτυπάει και η καρδιά του χτυπούσε τόσο δυνατά, που φοβόταν πως θα την άκουγαν όλοι. Ήλπιζε η μητέρα να χρειαστεί περισσότερη ώρα για να δοκιμάσει παπούτσια στον Νέιθαν. Τότε ίσως να μην πρόσεχε πόσο ζεστό και κόκκινο γινόταν το πρόσωπό του. Η μητέρα πάντα φαινόταν να καταλαβαίνει πότε κάτι δεν πήγαινε καλά.

Όμως αυτή τη φορά η μητέρα δεν το πρόσεξε και σύντομα πήραν τον δρόμο για το σπίτι. Ύστερα από μερικές μέρες, ο Τζόελ κατάλαβε πως δεν ήταν καθόλου διασκεδαστικό να έχει ένα κλεμμένο σουγιαδάκι. Σχεδόν ποτέ δεν μπορούσε να το χρησιμοποιήσει, από φόβο μήπως τον πιάσουν. Τις περισσότερες φορές έπρεπε να το κρατά καλά κρυμμένο!

Πέρασαν αρκετές εβδομάδες. Ένα βράδυ, ο Νέιθαν μπήκε στην κουζίνα, όπου ο Τζόελ και η μητέρα έπλεναν τα πιάτα του βραδινού. «Κοίτα, μαμά! Βρήκα αυτό το σουγιαδάκι κάτω από το μαξιλάρι του καναπέ. Αναρωτιέμαι από πού να ήρθε;»

Η καρδιά του Τζόελ άρχισε να χτυπάει τρελά καθώς έβλεπε τη μητέρα να εξετάζει το σουγιαδάκι. Μακάρι να μπορούσε να πεταχτεί έξω και να εξαφανιστεί. Μόλις εκείνο το βράδυ είχε χώσει το σουγιαδάκι κάτω από το μαξιλάρι του καναπέ, όταν η μητέρα είχε μπει ξαφνικά στο καθιστικό ανακοινώνοντας πως το βραδινό ήταν έτοιμο. Δεν είχε σκεφτεί ποτέ ότι κάποιος θα το έβρισκε εκεί.

Ξαφνικά κατάλαβε πως η μητέρα τον κοιτούσε. «Τζόελ, ξέρεις από πού είναι αυτό;» τον ρώτησε.

«Α! Εεε… λοιπόν… α… νομίζω πως ο ξάδελφος Μάικ έχει ένα άσπρο σαν κι αυτό», τραύλισε ο Τζόελ. «Μπορεί… α… μάλλον του έπεσε από την τσέπη το άλλο βράδυ, όταν είχαν έρθει για επίσκεψη.»

«Μάλιστα… Λοιπόν, θα πρέπει να ρωτήσω τη θεία Εύα γι’ αυτό», απάντησε ήρεμα η μητέρα, καθώς άφηνε το σουγιαδάκι στο περβάζι του παραθύρου.

Ο Τζόελ ένιωθε απαίσια. Του φαινόταν πως τα λυπημένα μάτια της μητέρας τον παρακολουθούσαν σε κάθε του κίνηση. Αχ, πόσο ευχόταν να μην είχε κλέψει ποτέ εκείνο το σουγιαδάκι! Κάθε φορά που το κοιτούσε, εκεί, πάνω στο περβάζι, του φαινόταν πως μεγάλωνε όλο και περισσότερο! Αποφάσισε να πάει νωρίς για ύπνο, μα όταν έκλεισε τα μάτια, το μόνο που έβλεπε ήταν εκείνο το άσχημο, άσπρο σουγιαδάκι να τον κοιτάζει απειλητικά από το περβάζι!

Την επόμενη μέρα, η μητέρα φώναξε τον Τζόελ κοντά της. Κρατούσε το άσπρο σουγιαδάκι. «Τηλεφώνησα σήμερα στη θεία Εύα και μου είπε πως ο Μάικ δεν έχει σουγιαδάκι. Τώρα, Τζόελ, πες μου… από πού πήρες αυτό το σουγιαδάκι; Και να θυμάσαι, δεν σε συμφέρει να λες ψέματα», είπε σταθερά η μητέρα, καθώς έβαλε το χέρι της κάτω από το πηγούνι του και του σήκωσε το σκυμμένο κεφάλι για να τον κοιτάξει στα μάτια.

«Εγώ… α… το πήρα από το κατάστημα του Γουίβερ», τραύλισε ο Τζόελ.

«Καταλαβαίνεις ότι αυτό ήταν κλοπή;» ρώτησε η μητέρα.

«Ναι, το καταλαβαίνω, και… και λυπάμαι που είπα και ψέματα γι’ αυτό. Δεν θα ξανακάνω ποτέ κάτι τέτοιο. Εγώ… α… ένιωθα τόσο απαίσια από τότε που το έκλεψα», είπε με δυσκολία ο Τζόελ, ενώ το σώμα του τρανταζόταν από τους λυγμούς.

«Χαίρομαι που το λες αυτό, Τζόελ», είπε η μητέρα. «Ο πατέρας σου κι εγώ ζητούσαμε από τον Θεό να σε βοηθήσει με αυτό το πρόβλημα του ψέματος και της κλοπής. Απόψε, όταν γυρίσει ο πατέρας σου, θα πρέπει να του τα πεις όλα. Έπειτα, ο πατέρας σου κι εγώ θα αποφασίσουμε ποια θα είναι η τιμωρία σου. Μετά, θα σε πάμε πίσω στο κατάστημα για να δώσεις το σουγιαδάκι στον κύριο Γουίβερ. Επίσης, αφού χρησιμοποίησες το σουγιαδάκι, θα πρέπει να το πληρώσεις με τα δικά σου χρήματα.»

One fruit of the spirit is a word we all know.
Joy is a blessing for us believers below.
Man can’t produce the Joy that I speak,
It comes from God, given to the meek.
It allows you to suffer, having peace within.
It only leaves at the presence of sin.
Joy brings you through the trials of living.
A peace in your heart that keeps on forgiving.
It doesn’t forsake us; through the struggles we face.
But rather gives courage and keeps us in grace.
Joy is something this world does not know.
It comes not from pleasure, nor feelings that grow;
But comes from the peace that only God gives.
It’s for the redeemed, and the life that he lives.
So why do so many reject this great gift?
That is known for healing and burdens to lift.
If you find yourself lacking the Joy from above,
Turn to the Saviour and His redeeming love!

– Barry Grant

Un fruto del Espíritu es una palabra que todos conocemos.
La alegría es una bendición para los creyentes aquí en la tierra.
El ser humano no puede producir la alegría de la que hablo,
viene de Dios, dada a los humildes.
Te permite sufrir con paz en tu interior.
Solo se va cuando el pecado está presente.
La alegría te ayuda a superar las pruebas de la vida.
Una paz en tu corazón que sigue perdonando.
No nos abandona en las luchas que afrontamos.
Más bien nos da valor y nos mantiene en la gracia.
La alegría es algo que este mundo no conoce.
No viene del placer ni de sentimientos que crecen;
sino de la paz que solo Dios da.
Es para los redimidos y para la vida que él vive.
Entonces, ¿por qué tantos rechazan este gran don?
Que es conocido por sanar y aliviar las cargas.
Si te encuentras sin la alegría que viene de lo alto,
¡acude al Salvador y a su amor redentor!

– Barry Grant

The early church in olden days
Had a desire to tell
The sinner about Jesus Christ,
About Heaven and hell.

Indeed, they were not perfect souls,
But yet they loved their Lord;
And strove to follow this command
In spite of peril and sword.

The more people they converted,
The more the tension grew.
The wicked rulers of the land
Did not know what to do.

A lot of folks were burned at stake,
Some put in dungeons cold,
Because they spread the Gospel word
With faith and courage bold.

These brave soldiers who suffered much
Were such bright lights indeed,
But to tell others about God
They still did see a need.

Now many years since then have passed;
We Christians tend to say
“Be an example to the world;
You need not tell the way.”

But if this point of view were true,
Then I would like to know:
As did the church in olden days,
Why doesn’t our church grow?

Is it that in America,
The fire has grown cold?
Since faith is good, why don’t we share
As did the saints of old?

In other lands this very day,
The fire is burning bright;
Because Christians are zealous there
And vigorous in fight.

While we thank God for freedom here,
They praise their Lord on high.
And thank Him that for Jesus’ sake
They suffer and they die.

So as martyrs in other lands
Are shedding blood for God,
If we would also spread God’s Word,
Our blood would stain our sod.

Is it a blessing from our God
That our country is free?
Or is it ‘cause we aren’t a “threat”
To the society?

Are we ashamed or have no time?
Dear friends, the time is nigh.
If we don’t bring the folks to God,
The populace will die.

So, in conclusion, friends, let’s take
The path that Jesus trod,
Showing lost souls, the narrow way,
That leads men home to God.

– Darren Brubaker

Den första kyrkan i forna dar
ville gärna berätta
för syndaren om Jesus Kristus,
om himmel och helvete.

Visst var de inte fullkomliga,
men ändå älskade de sin Herre
och strävade att följa denna befallning
trots faror och svärd.

Ju fler människor de omvände,
desto större blev spänningen.
Landets onda härskare
visste inte vad de skulle göra.

Många brändes på bål,
några sattes i kalla fängelsehålor,
för att de spred evangeliets ord
med djärv tro och mod.

Dessa tappra soldater som led så mycket
var verkligen lysande ljus,
men de såg fortfarande behovet
av att berätta för andra om Gud.

Nu har många år gått sedan dess;
vi kristna brukar säga:
”Var ett föredöme för världen;
du behöver inte visa vägen.”

Men om den här synen vore sann,
då skulle jag vilja veta:
liksom kyrkan i forna dar,
varför växer inte vår kyrka?

Har elden falnat
här i Amerika?
Om tron är god, varför delar vi den då inte
som helgonen förr?

I andra länder just i dag
brinner elden klart,
för där är de kristna ivriga
och strider med kraft.

Medan vi tackar Gud för friheten här,
prisar de sin Herre i höjden.
Och tackar Honom för att de för Jesu skull
lider och dör.

Så medan martyrer i andra länder
utgjuter sitt blod för Gud,
skulle vårt blod också fläcka jorden
om vi spred Guds ord.

Är det en välsignelse från vår Gud
att vårt land är fritt?
Eller är det för att vi inte är ett ”hot”
mot samhället?

Skäms vi, eller har vi ingen tid?
Kära vänner, tiden är nära.
Om vi inte för människorna till Gud,
kommer folket att gå under.

Så låt oss till sist, vänner, välja
den väg som Jesus gick,
visa vilsna själar den smala vägen
som leder människan hem till Gud.

– Darren Brubaker

Who would have ever imagined that a little germ which cannot be seen with the human eye, has put the entire globe in a tizzy, a panic, and an economic disruption? I have not seen a pandemic of this magnitude in my lifetime and, when this first emerged, I was one of the gainsayers who could not believe it would cripple our world to this extent. Questions abound, conspiracy theories are propagated, and fear has run rampant throughout the world as the entire globe responds to the pandemic. Will there be a cure, or will this continue to be a scourge in our world? If this little virus trespasses into my physical body, what is the chance of survival? Will it affect any of my loved ones? The questions are innumerable. Where it has come from has been theorized by many, but does anyone really know? Where is God in the whole thing? Did it surprise Him? Is it God’s judgment on humanity? These and many other questions are being asked by many sincere people and the answers that are given often contradict one another.

One of the outfalls of the pandemic is the government invasion into the church and our personal lives in a way that has been unprecedented in my and your lifetime. Suddenly, we are faced with decisions that many of us have not thought through. When, and how much, should the government mandate things in our lives when we clearly believe in separation of Church and state? What are my rights? What will I do if I lose my business? Will I cash in the stimulus check that is supposed to arrive in the mail in the near future?

There is a verse in Peter that reminds me that if anyone should have answers in this time of pandemic, we as Christians should. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: –1Pe 3:15. We may not know the origin of the virus, nor the outcome, but we do know Who knows all things, and that it was not a surprise to Him. It is the right time to turn to the Lord Jesus Christ, the One who holds all things by the power of His Word. If anytime in recent history the Christian has an opportunity to be salt in the earth and light in the world, it is during this time of upheaval. So, what should the response of the Christian be?

Consider this verse in Luke: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth… –Luk 21:26. For the Christian, earthquakes, famines, and pestilence should be no surprise since they have been prophesied to us through the Word of God. And while these things are happening and will happen, God has provided clear scriptural mandates for us as Christians to follow. We are clearly commanded in the scripture to not worry about tomorrow: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Mat 6:34.

So, we as Jesus’ disciples know that God will give us wisdom and grace for the difficulties of today. We are commanded to not borrow tomorrow’s troubles. We need to be reminded once again, in this time, as always, God will provide grace for today that will be great enough to sustain peace in the midst of the storm, and will provide it tomorrow if we live. Let us learn a lesson from Peter and the disciples—to focus on Jesus. We need to trust Jesus even when He seems to be asleep in the boat, rather than focusing on the storm that is raging all around us. Jesus was in control whether he was sleeping or awake and still is. But we might say, “How do I know if I will have food or clothing, or my business tomorrow?” And again, we hear the Savior say, “Look at the lilies, the fowls of the air, and learn a lesson from them!” We cannot even do some of the simplest things by God’s estimation, like add a cubit to our stature, so why would we try to deal with the hard things of providing for a tomorrow that is out of our control? Do these commands fit for the year 2020 and the pandemic that we are facing? I am sure that, in theory, we can agree, but can we internalize these verses and make them a very prominent place in our lives today?

There are principles given in God’s Word that, if we have not embraced them, we will also ‘reel in a tizzy’ when faced with things like the pandemic that is completely out of our control. One of those principles is the clear teaching that suffering is a way of life for the follower of Jesus. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17.

The ‘health and wealth’ gospel that is peddled by many preachers today is a false doctrine and can leave a person reeling when they are faced with health or economic loss. We need to be okay with suffering, we need to embrace it; we need to arm ourselves with the same mind as Christ. The loss of our business, home and yes, even our own lives also, by economic disaster, storms, or accidents is not outside the realm of the will of God for the Christian. We know that God can eliminate any of these calamities and will protect us from them all IF He so wills. But whether He does or not is God’s prerogative and we are the happiest IF we surrender our lives completely to Him in faith, and trust Him to keep us, whether with little or with much.

Another principle we need to reckon with is that we have no rights except the right to the Tree of Life. For us as Christians it makes little difference if we are citizens of the United States or not. We have many privileges for which we are very grateful for, but we should not think we have a right to own, keep, or buy, or that we have a stake to claim in this world. In the Holy Scriptures we are reminded that we are but pilgrims and strangers here (see Heb 11:13-16). As Abraham and the other patriarchs, we have no abiding city here but look for a city …whose builder and maker is God –Heb 11:10.

There are plenty of lawyers offering to fight for our rights, but the truth of the matter is, our citizenship is in Heaven and we are just ambassadors here and can be kicked out by society and need to leave all anytime without a moment’s hesitation. If this will be a reality, we need to live our lives with all our things held with an open hand. We do not have the right (only the privilege)—to own land, to have enough food, to enjoy good health, and to live without suffering—nor should we fight for those so-called rights, but we, God’s people, must put on the mind of Christ and be willing to leave all behind for the sake of Christ and trust Him completely for our sustenance. Jesus said He sees one sparrow fall to the ground and reminds us that we are worth more than many sparrows. Jesus calls us to hate all that we hold dear here on this earth: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple –Luk 14:26.

As Christians, we do not plan to stay here on this earth; we are anticipating Heaven. The scriptures express this sentiment when it not only considers the whole earth groaning to be delivered from this death and decay, but that we ourselves are also groaning to be delivered. Should there be such a strong pull to be here that our hearts fail us …for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth…? –Luk 21:26. Should we much rather cry out “how long Lord Jesus” “so come”? Even as the apostle intimates as he wrestles with being “betwixt two”—For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. –Php 1:23-24. The apostle clearly indicates “having a desire to depart and be with Christ is far better,” and the only thing that holds him here is the fact that there is work to be done.

Another area we should be awake to, is our vulnerability during this time of no church services. We may be tempted to go on-line and be fed spiritually by those who are false prophets or those who teach false doctrine. We need to “try the spirits” and know whose feet we are sitting at. Be selective to whom you might listen, or from whom you might allow your family to take nourishment. We, as fathers, are called to lead and lead we must. The burden is on our shoulders to help our families navigate through these uncertain times. We as fathers may need to be more proactive during this time. It is a call to us to rise up and lead our wives and children. Not only do we have to watch “whose feet we are sitting at”, but we need to lead our families with confidence, calling them to trust in God, and leading them in prayers of faith. We need to provide them with an example of faith and trust in God that no amount of buffeting will shake. This time of upheaval will not knock us off our feet IF we are rooted and grounded in Christ.

At a time like this, we need to make wise decisions, even decisions concerning the future, but still refrain from falling into the panic mode and running around as if we have no Heavenly Father. We also need to lead our families in being careful not to believe everything that one hears, but to be aware of where our news is coming from and to consider how reliable it is. Conspiracy theories abound concerning how this virus started and the political agenda theorized to be behind it. Refrain from spending time following these conspirators and rather follow the scripture mandate, “casting down imaginations.” The simple truth is this, we do not know, and if we did know it still should not change the way we live and our overall response. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, of love and a sound mind. John tells us to not “believe every spirit, but to try the spirits to see whether they be of God.”

I believe that this is an awesome opportunity to reach out to our fellow brothers and sisters by praying for one another and by staying in touch so that we can ‘weep with those that weep’ and ‘rejoice with those that rejoice’. Some of us have jobs and some do not. God’s Word tells us that those who have are to give to those who do not have so that there may be an equality. It is a time to reach out to the elderly in our church or community and stay in touch by mail or phone. This is a time in which the lonely will only get lonelier. A cheery word, or a letter in the mail, and whatever other resources you can appropriately use may be just the thing that those around you need.

During the times of mandatory “stay at home”, there is a whole group of our society that will face challenges that they have not seen up to this time. According to various news sources there has been an increase in domestic violence since family members are spending much more time together than they normally do. But let this not once be named among us. This is the time for us as God’s children to maximize on “in home” relationships. The Bible calls us to “redeem the time” and this can be done by making the most of our time together as a family. Spend time together—reading the Bible, praying together, singing together, and just simply doing enjoyable things together—things that will nurture growth and love in our relationships. We need to be creative as fathers in bringing our family together in a way that will produce an atmosphere of unity and oneness.

One question that begs an answer is this, “Should the government dictate whether we have church or not?” This is something we need to answer since for some areas of the country it is more than a suggestion but has become mandatory. I believe that since the suggestion/order to not meet together during this time is for the purpose of not spreading a virus that is quite contagious, this then fulfills the scripture “to love our neighbor as ourselves.” It is a good opportunity to show the public that if the mandate does not ask us to violate the scripture, then we choose to honor the government. There may come a time soon enough that we will be asked to do something that we cannot do with a clear conscience and then we will need to stand and “obey God rather than men.”

Some feel a twang of guilt because of the verse, “to not forsake the assembling of ourselves together”, however, this seems to be addressing a habit or a way of life. I suppose this is dealing with the lazy, slothful heart that does not see the benefit of getting together. We want to get together… As soon as we can get together again, we will take advantage of it. There is a big difference between those who cannot get together for a short time and those that choose not to since they do not see the value of it. For the present time, it seems the best testimony to our world and public relations to honor the mandate since they are not fighting against our faith and God. Let’s just take care to not let this become our new normal. Let’s keep our eye on a path forward to once again practically function as a local body.

What can we do? Pray more than ever that God would use this to win the lost and refine the church. Spend time building relationships with those you are closest to and have been encouraged to stay home with. Let this pandemic prepare us for what God has for us in the future. Let us be very careful how we talk about the government and some of the rulings that have come out through this all. We are called to honor the king and we need to spend more time thanking God for our freedoms than maximizing on the negative—I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; –1Ti 2:1-3. For the Christian, …we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Rom 8:28.

Chi avrebbe mai immaginato che un piccolo germe, invisibile all’occhio umano, avrebbe gettato l’intero pianeta nello scompiglio, nel panico e in una crisi economica? Nella mia vita non ho mai visto una pandemia di questa portata e, quando è comparsa per la prima volta, ero tra coloro che non credevano che avrebbe paralizzato il nostro mondo fino a questo punto. Le domande si moltiplicano, si diffondono teorie del complotto e la paura dilaga in tutto il mondo mentre l’intero pianeta reagisce alla pandemia. Si troverà una cura o questa piaga continuerà a incombere sul nostro mondo? Se questo piccolo virus si introduce nel mio corpo, quali sono le probabilità di sopravvivere? Colpirà qualcuno dei miei cari? Le domande sono innumerevoli. Molti hanno avanzato teorie sulla sua provenienza, ma qualcuno la conosce davvero? Dov’è Dio in tutto questo? È stato colto di sorpresa? È il giudizio di Dio sull’umanità? Molte persone sincere si pongono queste e tante altre domande, e le risposte che vengono date spesso si contraddicono a vicenda.

Una delle conseguenze della pandemia è l’ingerenza del governo nella chiesa e nelle nostre vite personali, in misura senza precedenti nella mia e nella vostra vita. Improvvisamente ci troviamo di fronte a decisioni su cui molti di noi non hanno riflettuto a fondo. Quando e fino a che punto il governo dovrebbe imporre regole nelle nostre vite, se crediamo chiaramente nella separazione tra Chiesa e Stato? Quali sono i miei diritti? Che cosa farò se perdo la mia attività? Incasserò l’assegno di sostegno economico che dovrebbe arrivare per posta nel prossimo futuro?

C’è un versetto nella lettera di Pietro che mi ricorda che, se qualcuno dovrebbe avere risposte in questo tempo di pandemia, dovremmo essere noi cristiani. Ma santificate il Signore Dio nei vostri cuori: e siate sempre pronti a dare una risposta a chiunque vi chieda ragione della speranza che è in voi, con mansuetudine e timore: –1 Pietro 3:15. Forse non conosciamo l’origine del virus né come andrà a finire, ma sappiamo Chi conosce ogni cosa e che per Lui non è stata una sorpresa. È il momento giusto per rivolgerci al Signore Gesù Cristo, Colui che sostiene ogni cosa con la potenza della Sua Parola. Se nella storia recente il cristiano ha avuto un’occasione per essere sale sulla terra e luce nel mondo, è proprio in questo tempo di sconvolgimenti. Dunque, quale dovrebbe essere la reazione del cristiano?

Considerate questo versetto di Luca: Gli uomini verranno meno per la paura e per l’attesa delle cose che stanno per accadere sulla terra… –Luca 21:26. Per il cristiano, terremoti, carestie e pestilenze non dovrebbero essere una sorpresa, poiché ci sono stati profetizzati nella Parola di Dio. E, mentre queste cose accadono e accadranno, Dio ci ha dato chiare istruzioni scritturali da seguire come cristiani. La Scrittura ci comanda chiaramente di non preoccuparci del domani: Non siate dunque in ansia per il domani, perché il domani avrà già le sue inquietudini. Basta a ciascun giorno il suo affanno. –Matteo 6:34.

Noi, discepoli di Gesù, sappiamo dunque che Dio ci darà sapienza e grazia per le difficoltà di oggi. Ci è comandato di non caricarci dei problemi di domani. In questo tempo, come sempre, dobbiamo ricordare ancora una volta che Dio provvederà oggi una grazia sufficiente a mantenere la pace in mezzo alla tempesta, e la provvederà anche domani, se saremo ancora in vita. Impariamo una lezione da Pietro e dai discepoli: concentriamoci su Gesù. Dobbiamo confidare in Gesù anche quando sembra dormire nella barca, invece di concentrarci sulla tempesta che infuria tutt’intorno a noi. Gesù era al controllo, che dormisse o fosse sveglio, e lo è ancora. Ma potremmo dire: «Come faccio a sapere se domani avrò da mangiare, da vestire o se la mia attività ci sarà ancora?». E ancora una volta sentiamo il Salvatore dire: «Guardate i gigli, gli uccelli del cielo e imparate da loro!». Secondo la valutazione di Dio, non siamo neppure capaci di fare alcune delle cose più semplici, come aggiungere un cubito alla nostra statura; perché allora dovremmo cercare di affrontare le difficoltà di provvedere a un domani che non è sotto il nostro controllo? Questi comandamenti sono adatti al 2020 e alla pandemia che stiamo affrontando? Sono certo che, in teoria, possiamo essere d’accordo, ma riusciamo a interiorizzare questi versetti e a farne un principio centrale della nostra vita oggi?

Nella Parola di Dio ci sono principi che, se non li abbiamo fatti nostri, ci faranno anche noi «perdere la testa» quando ci troveremo davanti a cose come la pandemia, che è del tutto fuori dal nostro controllo. Uno di questi principi è il chiaro insegnamento che la sofferenza fa parte della vita di chi segue Gesù. E se siamo figli, siamo anche eredi: eredi di Dio e coeredi di Cristo, se davvero soffriamo con lui, per essere anche glorificati con lui. –Romani 8:17.

Il vangelo della «salute e della prosperità», predicato oggi da molti pastori, è una falsa dottrina e può lasciare una persona sconvolta quando si trova ad affrontare una perdita economica o di salute. Dobbiamo accettare la sofferenza, anzi, farla nostra; dobbiamo armarci dello stesso sentimento di Cristo. La perdita della nostra attività, della nostra casa e sì, persino della nostra stessa vita, a causa di una crisi economica, di tempeste o di incidenti, non è estranea alla volontà di Dio per il cristiano. Sappiamo che Dio può eliminare ciascuna di queste calamità e ci proteggerà da tutte SE questa è la Sua volontà. Ma che lo faccia o no è prerogativa di Dio, e noi siamo più felici SE gli affidiamo completamente la nostra vita con fede e confidiamo in Lui perché si prenda cura di noi, sia che abbiamo poco o molto.

Un altro principio con cui dobbiamo fare i conti è che non abbiamo alcun diritto, se non il diritto all’albero della vita. Per noi cristiani fa poca differenza essere o non essere cittadini degli Stati Uniti. Abbiamo molti privilegi di cui siamo profondamente grati, ma non dobbiamo pensare di avere il diritto di possedere, conservare o comprare, né di poter rivendicare una parte in questo mondo. Nelle Sacre Scritture ci viene ricordato che qui siamo soltanto pellegrini e stranieri (vedi Ebrei 11:13-16). Come Abramo e gli altri patriarchi, qui non abbiamo una città permanente, ma ne cerchiamo una …il cui architetto e costruttore è Dio. –Ebrei 11:10.

Non mancano avvocati disposti a lottare per i nostri diritti, ma la verità è che la nostra cittadinanza è in cielo e qui siamo soltanto ambasciatori: la società può cacciarci e dobbiamo lasciare ogni cosa in qualsiasi momento, senza la minima esitazione. Se questa eventualità diventerà realtà, dobbiamo vivere tenendo ogni nostro bene con mano aperta. Non abbiamo il diritto (ma soltanto il privilegio) di possedere terreni, avere cibo a sufficienza, godere di buona salute e vivere senza sofferenze; né dobbiamo lottare per questi cosiddetti diritti. Noi, popolo di Dio, dobbiamo invece rivestirci del sentimento di Cristo ed essere disposti a lasciare tutto per amore di Cristo, confidando completamente in Lui per il nostro sostentamento. Gesù dice di vedere un passero cadere a terra e ci ricorda che valiamo più di molti passeri. Gesù ci chiama a odiare tutto ciò che abbiamo caro qui sulla terra: Se uno viene a me e non odia suo padre, sua madre, sua moglie, i figli, i fratelli, le sorelle e persino la propria vita, non può essere mio discepolo. –Luca 14:26.

Come cristiani, non abbiamo intenzione di restare qui sulla terra: attendiamo il cielo. Le Scritture esprimono questo sentimento considerando non soltanto che tutta la terra geme per essere liberata da questa morte e da questo decadimento, ma anche che noi stessi gemiamo per essere liberati. Dovremmo essere così fortemente attaccati a questa vita da venire meno …per la paura e per l’attesa delle cose che stanno per accadere sulla terra…? –Luca 21:26. Non dovremmo piuttosto gridare «fino a quando, Signore Gesù?» e «vieni dunque»? È ciò che lascia intendere l’apostolo mentre si dibatte tra «due cose»: Infatti sono messo alle strette dalle due cose: da una parte ho il desiderio di partire e di essere con Cristo, perché è cosa di gran lunga migliore; ma, dall’altra, il mio rimanere nel corpo è più necessario per voi. –Filippesi 1:23-24. L’apostolo afferma chiaramente che «il desiderio di partire e di essere con Cristo è cosa di gran lunga migliore», e che l’unica cosa che lo trattiene qui è il fatto che c’è del lavoro da compiere.

Un altro ambito a cui dobbiamo prestare attenzione è la nostra vulnerabilità in questo periodo in cui non si tengono funzioni religiose. Potremmo essere tentati di collegarci online e ricevere nutrimento spirituale da falsi profeti o da chi insegna false dottrine. Dobbiamo «mettere alla prova gli spiriti» e sapere ai piedi di chi ci sediamo. Siate selettivi riguardo a chi ascoltate e a chi permettete di nutrire spiritualmente la vostra famiglia. Noi padri siamo chiamati a guidare, e dobbiamo farlo. È sulle nostre spalle che grava il compito di aiutare le nostre famiglie a orientarsi in questi tempi incerti. In questo periodo noi padri potremmo dover essere più proattivi. È un appello a levarci e guidare le nostre mogli e i nostri figli. Non dobbiamo soltanto badare a «chi ascoltiamo», ma anche guidare con sicurezza le nostre famiglie, chiamandole a confidare in Dio e conducendole in preghiere di fede. Dobbiamo offrire loro un esempio di fede e fiducia in Dio che nessuna avversità possa scuotere. Questo periodo di sconvolgimenti non ci farà cadere SE siamo radicati e fondati in Cristo.

In un momento come questo dobbiamo prendere decisioni sagge, anche riguardo al futuro, ma senza cedere al panico e correre qua e là come se non avessimo un Padre celeste. Dobbiamo anche guidare le nostre famiglie a non credere a tutto ciò che si sente, ma a prestare attenzione alla provenienza delle notizie e a valutarne l’affidabilità. Circolano molte teorie del complotto su come è iniziato questo virus e sul presunto programma politico che vi sarebbe dietro. Evitiamo di passare il tempo a seguire questi complottisti e seguiamo invece l’ingiunzione delle Scritture: «facendo cadere i ragionamenti». La semplice verità è questa: non lo sappiamo e, anche se lo sapessimo, ciò non dovrebbe comunque cambiare il nostro modo di vivere né la nostra reazione complessiva. Dio non ci ha dato uno spirito di paura, ma di forza, di amore e di saggezza. Giovanni ci dice di non «credere a ogni spirito, ma di mettere alla prova gli spiriti per sapere se sono da Dio».

Credo che questa sia una straordinaria opportunità per farci vicini ai nostri fratelli e sorelle, pregando gli uni per gli altri e restando in contatto, così da poter «piangere con quelli che piangono» e «rallegrarci con quelli che si rallegrano». Alcuni di noi hanno un lavoro, altri no. La Parola di Dio ci dice che chi ha deve dare a chi non ha, affinché vi sia uguaglianza. È il momento di farci vicini agli anziani della nostra chiesa o comunità e di restare in contatto per posta o per telefono. In questo periodo chi si sente solo rischia di sentirsi ancora più solo. Una parola gentile, una lettera per posta e qualunque altra risorsa possiate usare nel modo opportuno possono essere proprio ciò di cui hanno bisogno le persone intorno a voi.

Durante i periodi di «obbligo di restare a casa», un’intera fascia della nostra società dovrà affrontare difficoltà che finora non aveva mai incontrato. Secondo diverse fonti di notizie, la violenza domestica è aumentata, poiché i familiari trascorrono insieme molto più tempo del solito. Ma che questo non sia mai nominato tra noi. Questo è il momento per noi, figli di Dio, di valorizzare al massimo le relazioni «in famiglia». La Bibbia ci chiama a «riscattare il tempo» e possiamo farlo sfruttando al meglio il tempo trascorso insieme come famiglia. Passiamo del tempo insieme: leggiamo la Bibbia, preghiamo, cantiamo e semplicemente facciamo insieme cose piacevoli, cose che alimentino la crescita e l’amore nelle nostre relazioni. Noi padri dobbiamo essere creativi nel riunire la famiglia, creando un’atmosfera di unità e di unione.

Una domanda a cui occorre rispondere è questa: «Il governo dovrebbe decidere se possiamo riunirci in chiesa oppure no?». Dobbiamo rispondere, perché in alcune zone del Paese non si tratta più di un suggerimento, ma è diventato un obbligo. Credo che, poiché il suggerimento o l’ordine di non riunirci in questo periodo ha lo scopo di impedire la diffusione di un virus molto contagioso, esso soddisfi il precetto scritturale di «amare il nostro prossimo come noi stessi». È una buona opportunità per dimostrare al pubblico che, se il provvedimento non ci chiede di trasgredire la Scrittura, scegliamo di rispettare il governo. Potrebbe arrivare presto il momento in cui ci verrà chiesto di fare qualcosa che non possiamo fare a coscienza tranquilla; allora dovremo prendere posizione e «ubbidire a Dio anziché agli uomini».

Alcuni provano un certo senso di colpa per il versetto «non abbandonando la nostra comune adunanza», eppure sembra riferirsi a un’abitudine o a uno stile di vita. Immagino che si riferisca al cuore pigro e indolente, che non riconosce il beneficio del riunirsi. Noi vogliamo riunirci… Non appena potremo farlo di nuovo, ne approfitteremo. C’è una grande differenza tra chi non può riunirsi per un breve periodo e chi sceglie di non farlo perché non ne vede il valore. Per il momento, sembra che la testimonianza migliore per il nostro mondo e le buone relazioni con il pubblico consistano nel rispettare il provvedimento, dato che non è in contrasto con la nostra fede e con Dio. Facciamo attenzione a non lasciare che questa diventi la nostra nuova normalità. Teniamo lo sguardo fisso sul cammino da seguire per tornare a operare concretamente come corpo locale.

Che cosa possiamo fare? Pregare più che mai affinché Dio si serva di questa situazione per salvare i perduti e raffinare la chiesa. Dedichiamo del tempo a coltivare i rapporti con le persone a noi più vicine, con le quali ci è stato raccomandato di restare a casa. Lasciamo che questa pandemia ci prepari a ciò che Dio ha in serbo per noi in futuro. Facciamo molta attenzione a come parliamo del governo e di alcuni dei provvedimenti emanati in tutto questo periodo. Siamo chiamati a onorare il re e dobbiamo dedicare più tempo a ringraziare Dio per le nostre libertà che a insistere sugli aspetti negativi: Esorto dunque, prima di ogni altra cosa, a fare suppliche, preghiere, intercessioni e ringraziamenti per tutti gli uomini, per i re e per tutti quelli che sono costituiti in autorità, affinché possiamo condurre una vita tranquilla e pacifica, in ogni pietà e dignità. Questo è buono e gradito agli occhi di Dio, nostro Salvatore. –1 Timoteo 2:1-3. Per il cristiano, …sappiamo che tutte le cose cooperano al bene di quelli che amano Dio, i quali sono chiamati secondo il suo disegno. –Romani 8:28.

Joel had a serious problem of taking things which did not belong to him. Sometimes he would sneak mother’s freshly baked cookies from the cookie jar, or he would take Nathan’s magic markers without asking to use them. To make matters worse, Joel would lie or make excuses when he was caught. Mother and Father had to punish Joel many times. They told him that if he continued to take small things without asking for permission, it could lead to stealing bigger things as he grew older.

And God hates stealing!

One day Mother took Joel and Nathan to Weaver’s Country Store to buy shoes. “Look Mother,” Joel said excitedly, pointing to the shiny pocketknives on the counter. “Will you please buy one for me?”

“No, Joel,” Mother replied. “You must wait until you are older for a pocketknife.”

“O.K.,” Joel answered rather disappointedly.

Later, while Mother was fitting shoes on Nathan, Joel wandered front to the pocketknives again. He looked at them longingly. “That white one is a beauty,” he thought to himself. “Oh, if only I could have it! Mother just does not understand that I am old enough to have one. All the other boys my age have pocketknives.” Just then another ugly thought entered his head. “I think I will just take that white one. No one will ever know.” Joel glanced toward the back of the store where Mr. Weaver was helping fit shoes on Nathan. No one was looking, so he quickly reached up, took the white pocketknife from the box on the counter, and stuck it into his pocket.

Turning nervously, Joel walked back up the aisle. His head started to pound, and his heart was thumping so hard he was afraid everyone could hear it. He hoped Mother would take more time fitting shoes on Nathan. Then maybe she would not notice how hot and red his face was getting. Mother always seemed to notice when something was wrong.

But Mother did not notice this time, and soon they were on their way home. After several days, Joel discovered that it was not fun having a stolen pocketknife. He could hardly ever use it for fear of getting caught. He had to keep it well hidden most of the time!

Several weeks passed. Then one evening, Nathan came into the kitchen where Joel and Mother were doing the supper dishes. “Look, Mother! I found this pocketknife under the couch cushion. I wonder where it came from?”

Joel’s heart began to thump wildly as he watched Mother examine the pocketknife. He wished he could dash outside and disappear. He had just slipped the pocketknife under the couch cushion that evening when Mother had walked into the parlor unexpectedly as she announced that supper was ready. He never thought someone would find it there.

Suddenly he realized Mother was looking at him. “Joel, do you know where this comes from?” she asked.

“Oh! Err – well – ah – I think Cousin Mike has a white one like that,” Joel stammered. “It – ah – it probably slipped out of his pocket the other evening when they were here visiting.”

“I see… Well, I will need to ask Aunt Eva about this,” Mother replied calmly as she placed the pocketknife on the window shelf.

Joel felt miserable. It seemed as if Mother’s sad eyes were watching every move he made. Oh, how he wished he had never stolen that pocketknife! Every time he looked at it, sitting there on the shelf, it seemed to grow larger in size! He decided to go to bed early, but when he closed his eyes, all he saw was that ugly, white pocketknife, leering at him from the window shelf!

The next day, Mother called Joel to her. She was holding the white pocketknife. “I called Aunt Eva today, and she said that Mike does not have a pocketknife. Now Joel, tell me… where did you get this pocketknife? And remember, it does not pay to lie,” Mother said firmly as she placed her hand under his chin and raised his drooping head to look into his eyes.

“I – ah – took it from Weaver’s Store,” Joel stammered.

“Do you realize that was stealing?” Mother asked.

“Yes, I do, and I – I am sorry I lied about it too. I will never do anything like that again. I – ah – I felt so awful ever since I stole it,” choked Joel as his body shook with sobs.

“I am glad to hear you say that Joel,” Mother said. “Father and I have been asking God to help you with this problem of lying and stealing. This evening when Father comes home, you will need to tell him all about it, then Father and I will decide what your punishment should be. After that, we will take you back to the store and you can give the pocketknife to Mr. Weaver. Also, since you used the knife, you will need to pay for it with your own money.”

How Joel dreaded facing Father and Mr. Weaver, but later when it was all over, he felt so much better. That day Joel learned a lesson he never forgot.

Joel tenía un grave problema: tomaba cosas que no le pertenecían. A veces se escabullía para sacar del tarro unas galletas recién horneadas por su madre, o tomaba los marcadores mágicos de Nathan sin pedirle permiso para usarlos. Para empeorar las cosas, Joel mentía o inventaba excusas cuando lo descubrían. Su madre y su padre tuvieron que castigarlo muchas veces. Le dijeron que, si seguía tomando cosas pequeñas sin pedir permiso, podría llegar a robar cosas más grandes al hacerse mayor.

¡Y Dios aborrece el robo!

Un día, la madre llevó a Joel y Nathan a la tienda rural de Weaver para comprar zapatos. «¡Mira, mamá!», dijo Joel emocionado, señalando las brillantes navajas de bolsillo sobre el mostrador. «¿Me comprarías una, por favor?»

«No, Joel», respondió su madre. «Tendrás que esperar a ser mayor para tener una navaja de bolsillo».

«Está bien», contestó Joel, algo decepcionado.

Más tarde, mientras su madre le probaba zapatos a Nathan, Joel volvió a acercarse a las navajas de bolsillo. Las miró con anhelo. «Esa blanca es preciosa», pensó. «¡Ay, si tan solo pudiera tenerla! Mamá simplemente no entiende que ya tengo edad para tener una. Todos los demás chicos de mi edad tienen navajas de bolsillo». En ese mismo momento se le ocurrió otra idea desagradable. «Creo que simplemente me llevaré esa blanca. Nadie se enterará». Joel miró hacia el fondo de la tienda, donde el señor Weaver ayudaba a Nathan a probarse los zapatos. Nadie lo miraba, así que estiró rápidamente el brazo, sacó de la caja sobre el mostrador la navaja de bolsillo blanca y se la metió en el bolsillo.

Se dio la vuelta nerviosamente y caminó de regreso por el pasillo. Le empezó a latir la cabeza y el corazón le palpitaba tan fuerte que temía que todos pudieran oírlo. Esperaba que su madre tardara más en probarle los zapatos a Nathan. Así quizá no se daría cuenta de lo acalorado y rojo que se le estaba poniendo el rostro. A su madre siempre parecía darse cuenta cuando algo andaba mal.

Pero esta vez su madre no se dio cuenta, y pronto iban de camino a casa. Después de varios días, Joel descubrió que no era divertido tener una navaja de bolsillo robada. Casi nunca podía usarla por miedo a que lo descubrieran. ¡La mayor parte del tiempo tenía que mantenerla bien escondida!

Pasaron varias semanas. Una tarde, Nathan entró en la cocina, donde Joel y su madre lavaban los platos de la cena. «¡Mira, mamá! Encontré esta navaja de bolsillo debajo del cojín del sofá. ¿De dónde habrá salido?»

El corazón de Joel empezó a latir con fuerza mientras veía a su madre examinar la navaja. Deseó poder salir corriendo y desaparecer. Esa misma tarde había deslizado la navaja debajo del cojín del sofá cuando su madre entró inesperadamente en la sala y anunció que la cena estaba lista. Nunca pensó que alguien la encontraría allí.

De pronto se dio cuenta de que su madre lo miraba. «Joel, ¿sabes de dónde salió esto?», preguntó.

«¡Ah! Eeeh… bueno… pues… creo que el primo Mike tiene una blanca como esa», tartamudeó Joel. «Se… eh… probablemente se le salió del bolsillo la otra tarde, cuando vinieron de visita».

«Ya veo… Bueno, tendré que preguntarle a la tía Eva», respondió su madre con calma mientras ponía la navaja de bolsillo en el estante de la ventana.

Joel se sentía desdichado. Le parecía que los ojos tristes de su madre seguían cada movimiento que hacía. ¡Ay, cómo deseaba no haber robado nunca esa navaja de bolsillo! Cada vez que la miraba allí, sobre el estante, ¡le parecía que crecía y crecía! Decidió acostarse temprano, pero al cerrar los ojos, lo único que veía era aquella desagradable navaja de bolsillo blanca, que lo miraba con aire amenazador desde el estante de la ventana.

Al día siguiente, su madre llamó a Joel. Sostenía la navaja de bolsillo blanca. «Hoy llamé a la tía Eva y me dijo que Mike no tiene una navaja de bolsillo. Ahora, Joel, dime… ¿de dónde sacaste esta navaja? Y recuerda: mentir no te conviene», dijo su madre con firmeza mientras le ponía la mano bajo la barbilla y le levantaba la cabeza inclinada para que la mirara a los ojos.

«Yo… eh… la tomé de la tienda de Weaver», tartamudeó Joel.

«¿Te das cuenta de que eso fue robar?», preguntó su madre.

«Sí, lo sé, y yo… yo también siento haber mentido. Nunca volveré a hacer algo así. Yo… eh… me he sentido muy mal desde que la robé», dijo Joel entre sollozos, con el cuerpo sacudido por el llanto.

«Me alegra oírte decir eso, Joel», dijo su madre. «Tu padre y yo le hemos estado pidiendo a Dios que te ayude con este problema de mentir y robar. Esta tarde, cuando tu padre vuelva a casa, tendrás que contárselo todo; después, tu padre y yo decidiremos cuál debe ser tu castigo. Luego te llevaremos de vuelta a la tienda para que le devuelvas la navaja al señor Weaver. Además, como la usaste, tendrás que pagarla con tu propio dinero».

¡Cuánto temía Joel tener que enfrentarse a su padre y al señor Weaver! Pero después, cuando todo terminó, se sintió mucho mejor. Ese día, Joel aprendió una lección que nunca olvidó.

Is it only in the heartbreak,
When confusion ‘round me churns,
That I truly seek my Savior’s arms
And my will toward Him turns?

Is it only in the darkness,
When I cannot see my way;
Or when asked of something I do not know
That I think to stop and pray?

Is it only when I feel
The force of evil ‘round me gathered,
That I seek for His protection;
To in His arms be sheltered?

Oh, foolish heart of mine!
How can you call Him your best friend
When it’s only in your trials
That on Him you will depend?

In good times too, you need Him,
Perhaps more desperately;
Since it’s easier to forget to seek
When the way you think you see.

Even when you fail to hear Him,
When by His side you fail to stay,
He will hear you when you cry to Him
And on Him your troubles lay.

But how much better it would be
To earnestly seek His face
As much in the smoother times of life
As in the rougher place!

To seek and to search, to stay by His side,
To share the joy and the sorrow,
The unknowns in His hands, He’ll be at your side
For whatever may come in tomorrow.

–by Katie Good

أطلب حقًا ذراعي مخلّصي،

أفقط في الظلام،

أفقط حين أشعر

I have heard many Christians say they are not satisfied with their relationship with God. They wonder why God does not speak to them like He spoke with people in the Bible, or even in the early church. I have often thought of this, and at times have felt the same way. I have come to realize that God is still speaking with His children today, just as He always has. The problem is that we are not always listening.

Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: –Joh 16:7-8.

I have excellent hearing. However, I had to consider whether I listen to only the things and people I desire and unknowingly block out what I do not want to hear?

Today the god of this world has filled people’s lives with distractions, and while not all are bad, he (Satan) wants our attention and focus to be on other things, then when God speaks to us, we do not hear. So, what happens when we stop listening to God? He stops speaking, and we eventually drift away from truth. God gave everyone a conscience. It is a wonderful thing that keeps us on the strait and narrow way. But God’s word says that if we continue to ignore the prodding of the Spirit, our conscience will stop working properly. Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; –1Ti 4:1-2. In other words, we do wrong, but since our conscience doesn’t work any longer, there is no feeling there. We begin to justify our actions; we are always right.

I remember years ago as I was driving to work, I noticed a police car coming in my direction. I then realized I was not wearing my seat belt, so I slyly slipped it on, hoping he had not noticed. To my disappointment, he turned around and pulled me over. He asked me a very straightforward question. “Sir, did you just put your seat belt on when you saw me?”

I smiled and told him with an apology that I did. He went back to his car and several minutes later he returned. He told me that he sees many people do the same thing. They see him and quickly put their seat belt on, but he has never had anyone admit to it. They all argue with him that their seat belt was already on. He gave me a warning and thanked me for being honest.

It is sad that today, so many people no longer listen to their conscience, which is telling them to do right. Instead, even when they know they are wrong they argue, trying to deny or justify their wrong. We expect this from the world, but is this a practice that we are seeing more and more in the church today? I have even heard many people use the Bible to try to justify their wrongdoing. Have we stopped listening to God? Have we pampered ‘self ’ to the point that we no longer can admit when we are wrong? Would we rather look ‘right’ and have a guilty conscience? Or humble ourselves, admit our failure and rejoice with a clear conscience. Friends, do we value a clear conscience? Can we say with the apostle Paul that we …have lived in all good conscience before God until this day … to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men –Act 23:1-24:16.

Let’s look at the account of David and Bathsheba. David was a man after God’s own heart, so why did this happen? The account is in II Samuel chapter 11. It was the time when kings went forth to battle, and they had a battle going with the children of Ammon. But David tarried still at Jerusalem. When we begin to do things the way we want and ignore the call of God in our lives, we hinder the Spirit. So, David is just hanging around; it says that David was laying on his bed. Was he seeking God? It doesn’t seem like it. An ancient proverb says that ‘idleness is the devil’s workshop’. David decides to take a stroll on the roof. Was David innocent even at this time? Maybe David already knew he could see this woman from his rooftop? Maybe he had been tempted before, ‘at even tide’, to look over toward Bathsheba’s home. Either way, he now found himself in an awkward situation. What amazes me is there was no thinking—David does not seem to give his conscience any time at all to work. He simply sent messengers to go and bring her to him, and then he laid with her. Again, it seems that David’s conscience is not working. But rather he goes right into coverup mode. He calls for Bathsheba’s husband and eventually has him killed… and then marries Bathsheba. But God was not done with David. In II Samuel chapter 12 it says that God sent Nathan to David. Often before God gives us over, He sends a messenger. Maybe it’s a brother in the church, maybe it’s a church leader. Are we aware of, and listening to, the messengers God sends to us?

Nathan went to David and told him a story…

There were two men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor. The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds. But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.

And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him. And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity. And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man… –2Sa 12:4-7.

David now came face to face with his sin; there was still time. David repented with genuine godly sorrow and was forgiven (read Psalm 51).

David could have become angry with Nathan and had him killed. Or what if Nathan would have refused to go talk to David because he feared him? When we want a clear conscience, I believe people around us will know that and it will be easy for them to come and talk to us about sin in our lives. But too often the opposite happens; we would rather live the way we want and shield ourselves from the counsel of others, and when a brother or sister comes to talk to us, we get angry and they don’t come talk to us again.

The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise –Pro 12:15.

If Nathan would have refused to talk to David, maybe David would never have seen his sin. It is our responsibility to talk to one another and it leads to a clear conscience. It often doesn’t feel good when our conscience is pricked, but that is the way God designed it, so we act upon a guilty conscience. Unfortunately, there are many other accounts in God’s word where someone refused to repent, and God’s judgement was poured out.

When our conscience is pricked, we have two choices: either to get angry and deny, or to humble ourselves and repent. It is really that simple. What do we find ourselves doing when God speaks to us through our conscience? Are we broken?

In the book of Acts, we have a few accounts of how people responded to their conscience being pricked. The first account is in chapter 2, the day of Pentecost. Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit, lifted up his voice and spoke some very hard things to the large crowd that had gathered. It says that after Peter was finished preaching, the people were pricked in their heart. So how did these people respond? They …said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do? Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost –Act 2:37-38. And about 3,000 souls were added to the Kingdom.

When we respond to that pricking of the heart, or the voice of God to our conscience, God hears us and will forgive us! However, if we turn just a few pages in our Bibles we see another response to the pricking of God in our conscience.

In Acts chapter 5 we see that the apostles went about preaching and healing the sick, and the high priest and those that were with him put them in prison. But God opened the doors and released them. Notice that this group of more than likely very young men, and new in the faith, rose up early the next morning and went into the temple to teach. They were sold out. That day the high priest wanted to talk with the disciples, so he sent someone to the prison, but they were not there. Then came one and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people –Act 5:25. So, they went to the temple and brought them to the high priest. Peter then again began to speak boldly, telling them that they should obey God rather than man: …we are his witnesses of these things; and so is also the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to them that obey him. When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel to slay them –Act 5: 32-33.

Again, we see God speaking, convicting the conscience, but notice their reaction to the voice of God: ‘They took counsel to slay them’. Even though we are believers, we still tend to give a similar response when our conscience is pricked. We want to neutralize whatever it was that was spoken to us. In similar manner as David had Uriah killed, the Sadducees sought to slay the disciples, Herod beheaded John the Baptist, and the World killed our Lord, we avoid people that speak truth and say the hard things that God wants us to hear. The Lord is hated by the world because he testifies …of it, that the works thereof are evil –Joh 7:7.

Maybe we begin to have itching ears, hearing only what we want. We rid ourselves of the presence of people who love us and desire to speak into our lives. We often forget that our conscience is a gift from God and a very important part of a believer’s life. When it stops working, we are in big trouble.

A guilty conscience has proven to be a very difficult thing to deal with. It has caused many to turn to drugs and alcohol. It has also caused many like Judas to take their own life. Many people do not understand that a troubled conscience is God’s way of calling someone to himself. There is great hope for a bad conscience. It is not pills, or classes, or drugs, or entertainment. It is the Lord Jesus Christ and only Him. It is impossible to drown away a bad conscience.

What is worse than a bad conscience is a seared conscience. This occurs when someone has ignored God’s calling to repent and turn from their wrong for so long that He gives them over to their sin. He allows them to think that what they are doing is okay. This is a position that is very dangerous, and few find their way back to truth.

One hundred years ago it was common for a town or village to only have one sheriff to control its crime. Forty years ago, someone asked one of these then-retired sheriffs how they were able to control all the crime by themselves. He said that it was easy; back then, men’s consciences still worked. He went on to say that most criminals would eventually turn themselves in. They would rather face prison than continue living with a guilty conscience.

Today there are many criminals on the run, and men everywhere comfortably living in sin. It seems that their conscience is no longer working, being seared with a hot iron. That is not my concern today, but rather my concern is for the church of Jesus Christ. Do we have a clear conscience before God? Are we really looking forward to the return of the Lord? Do we have joy in our lives, relationships, and marriages? Are we actively pursuing the Kingdom of God, or are we trying to ease our conscience with the ways of the world, money, entertainment, pleasure, and the likes?

My children wanted a dog for some time, so I finally decided it was time and brought a puppy home. The children fell in love with it over the next months. Then someone stole it. The children were devastated, and they prayed every night that God would bring the puppy back. One day as we walked home from the Sunday service a puppy came running from a small house, jumping and yipping. We quickly realized it was our puppy. I walked over to the house and asked the man if this was his dog. He said that it was, so I asked him where he had gotten it. The man claimed he had purchased the dog. I then asked him if he was a Christian; guiltily he said he was. I smiled and told him that he should know that God knows the truth, that God sees everything. I patted him on the back, and we walked home.

Then we waited… sure enough, there was a knock at the door. Opening the door, I saw the man holding our puppy. He said he was sorry and gave the puppy back. I shook his hand and told him that God was pleased with his response to his conscience. The man walked away with no puppy, but with something far greater, a clear conscience before God.

When we choose to ignore our conscience, we eventually become bitter; we believe everyone is out to get us. We have a problem with the sermons we hear, we have a problem with our spouse and children. We shut ourselves off, we separate ourselves from God and his people.

If you find yourself in this state, remember, a clear heaven is only a prayer away.

The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise –Psa 51:17.

我听过许多基督徒说，他们对自己与神的关系并不满意。他们不明白，为什么神不像在圣经时代，甚至不像在早期教会时那样对人说话。我常常想到这件事，有时也有同样的感受。我渐渐明白，神今天仍在对祂的儿女说话，一如既往。问题是，我们并不总是在聆听。

然而，我将真情告诉你们：我去是与你们有益的；我若不去，保惠师就不到你们这里来；我若去，就差祂来。祂来了，就要叫世人为罪、为义、为审判，自己责备自己。–约翰福音 16:7-8。

我的听力很好。然而，我不得不想一想：我是不是只听自己想听的事和想听的人，却在不知不觉中屏蔽了自己不愿听的内容？

今天，这世界的神让人们的生活充满了各种分心的事物；这些事物并非全都不好，但他（撒但）想要我们的注意力和专注都放在别的事情上，于是神对我们说话时，我们就听不见了。那么，我们不再听神的话，会发生什么事呢？祂就不再说话，而我们最终会渐渐偏离真理。神赐给每个人良心。这是美好的恩赐，使我们走在正直狭窄的道路上。但神的话说，如果我们继续无视圣灵的催促，我们的良心就会停止正常运作。圣灵明说，在后来的时候，必有人离弃真道，听从那引诱人的邪灵和鬼魔的道理；这是因为说谎之人的假冒；这等人的良心如同被热铁烙惯了一般；–提摩太前书 4:1-2。换句话说，我们做了错事，但由于良心不再起作用，心里便毫无感觉。我们开始为自己的行为辩解；我们总认为自己是对的。

多年前，我开车去上班时，记得自己看见一辆警车迎面驶来。接着我意识到自己没有系安全带，便悄悄地把安全带系上，希望警察没有注意到。令我失望的是，他掉头把我拦了下来。他问了我一个非常直接的问题：“先生，你刚才看见我时才系上安全带的吗？”

我笑了笑，向他道歉并告诉他确实如此。他回到车里，几分钟后又走了回来。他告诉我，他见过很多人做同样的事。他们看见他就赶紧系上安全带，但从来没有人承认过。每个人都跟他争辩，说自己早就系好了。他给了我口头警告，并感谢我诚实以对。

可悲的是，今天有那么多人不再听从良心的提醒，尽管良心在告诉他们要行正事。相反，即使他们知道自己错了，仍然争辩，试图否认或为自己的过错辩解。我们会对世人有这样的表现并不意外，但今天我们在教会里是否越来越常看到这种做法？我甚至听过许多人引用圣经，试图为自己的过错辩解。我们是否已经不再听神的话？我们是否把“自我”娇纵到一个地步，以至于再也无法承认自己的错误？我们宁愿看起来“正确”，心里却有罪疚吗？还是愿意谦卑自己，承认自己的失败，并因良心无亏而欢喜？朋友们，我们看重无亏的良心吗？我们能否像使徒保罗那样说，我们……直到今日，在神面前行事为人都是凭着良心……对神对人，常存无亏的良心——使徒行传 23:1-24:16。

让我们看看大卫和拔示巴的故事。大卫是合神心意的人，那么这件事为什么会发生呢？记载在《撒母耳记下》第十一章。当时正是列王出战的时候，他们正与亚扪人交战。但大卫仍留在耶路撒冷。当我们开始随心所欲行事，忽视神对我们生命的呼召时，就会拦阻圣灵。因此，大卫只是闲荡着；经文说大卫躺在床上。他是在寻求神吗？看起来不像。古谚说：“懒惰是魔鬼的工场。”大卫决定到屋顶上走走。大卫在那时真的毫无所知吗？也许大卫早就知道，从屋顶上可以看见这个女人？也许他以前在“黄昏的时候”就受过试探，朝拔示巴的家那边张望。不管怎样，他此刻发现自己陷入了尴尬的处境。令我惊讶的是，他完全没有思量——大卫似乎根本没给良心任何时间发挥作用。他只是派使者去把她带来，然后与她同寝。再一次，大卫的良心似乎没有起作用。他反而马上开始掩盖。他叫拔示巴的丈夫来，最后还使他被杀……然后娶了拔示巴。但神并没有就此放过大卫。《撒母耳记下》第十二章说，神差遣拿单去见大卫。神把我们交给罪之前，常会先差遣一位使者。也许是教会里的弟兄，也许是教会领袖。我们是否留意并聆听神差来找我们的使者？

拿单去见大卫，给他讲了一个故事……

一座城里有两个人：一个富户，一个穷人。富户有许多牛群羊群；穷人除了所买来养活的一只小母羊羔之外，什么也没有。羊羔在他和他的儿女身边长大，吃他所吃的，喝他所喝的，睡在他怀里，在他看来就像女儿一样。

有一客人来到这富户家里；富户舍不得从自己的牛群羊群中取一只来预备给客人吃，却取了那穷人的羊羔，预备给来到他家里的客人吃。大卫就甚恼怒那人，对拿单说：“我指着永生的耶和华起誓，行这事的人该死！他必偿还羊羔四倍，因为他行这事，没有怜恤的心。”拿单对大卫说：“你就是那人！”……–撒母耳记下 12:4-7。

大卫此刻直面自己的罪；事情仍有挽回的余地。大卫真心悔改，怀着属神的忧伤，并得到了赦免（请读诗篇第51篇）。

大卫本可以对拿单大发雷霆，把他杀了。或者，假如拿单因为害怕大卫而不肯去找他谈，会怎么样呢？我相信，当我们渴望良心无亏时，周围的人会知道这一点，他们也就容易来和我们谈论生命中的罪。但太多时候，情况恰恰相反；我们宁愿照自己的意思生活，隔绝别人的劝告；当弟兄或姊妹来和我们谈时，我们却发怒，于是他们再也不来找我们谈了。

愚妄人所行的，在自己眼中看为正直；惟智慧人肯听人的劝教。–箴言 12:15。

假如拿单拒绝和大卫说话，大卫或许永远也不会看见自己的罪。彼此交谈是我们的责任，这会使人良心无亏。良心受到责备时，往往让人感觉不好；但神就是这样设计的，好叫我们因良心有亏而采取行动。遗憾的是，神的话中还有许多其他记载，讲到有人拒绝悔改，结果神的审判就倾倒下来。

良心受到责备时，我们有两个选择：要么发怒并否认，要么谦卑自己并悔改。事情就是这么简单。神借着我们的良心对我们说话时，我们发现自己会怎么做？我们心里破碎了吗？

《使徒行传》中有几段记载，讲到人们在良心受到责备时如何回应。第一段记载在第二章，也就是五旬节那一天。彼得被圣灵充满，放声向聚集的大群人讲了一些非常严厉的话。经文说，彼得讲完后，众人觉得扎心。那么这些人怎么回应呢？他们……就对彼得和其余的使徒说：“弟兄们，我们当怎样行？”彼得说：“你们各人要悔改，奉耶稣基督的名受洗，叫你们的罪得赦，就必领受所赐的圣灵；”——使徒行传 2:37-38。于是约有三千人归入神的国。

当我们回应心里的责备，或神对我们良心所说的话时，神就垂听我们，也会赦免我们！然而，只要在圣经里再翻几页，就会看到人们对神在良心中的责备作出了另一种回应。

在《使徒行传》第五章，我们看到使徒们到处传道、医治病人，大祭司和那些与他一伙的人就把他们下在监里。但神打开了监门，释放了他们。请留意，这一群人很可能都非常年轻，而且信主不久，第二天一早就起来进殿教训人。他们全心投入。那天大祭司想和门徒谈话，就派人到监里去找他们，但他们已经不在那里了。有一个人来禀报说：“你们收在监里的人，现今站在殿里教训百姓。”——使徒行传 5:25。于是他们到殿里把使徒带到大祭司面前。彼得又开始大胆发言，告诉他们应当顺从神，不顺从人：……我们为这事作见证；神赐给顺从之人的圣灵也为这事作见证。公会的人听见就极其恼怒，想要杀他们。——使徒行传 5:32-33。

我们再一次看到神在说话，责备人的良心；但请留意他们对神声音的反应：“他们商议要杀他们。”即使我们是信徒，良心受到责备时，我们仍常常会作出类似的回应。我们想要消除别人对我们所说的话所带来的影响。正如大卫杀了乌利亚，撒都该人想杀门徒，希律斩了施洗约翰的头，世人杀了我们的主一样，我们会躲避那些讲真话、说出神要我们听见的严厉话语的人。主被世人憎恨，因为祂指着世人作见证，说他们的行为是恶的。……因为我指证世人所做的事是恶的。——约翰福音 7:7。

也许我们开始耳朵发痒，只听自己想听的话。我们把爱我们、盼望对我们的生命说些话的人赶走。我们常忘记，良心是神所赐的恩典，也是信徒生命中非常重要的一部分。良心一旦停止运作，我们就麻烦大了。

事实证明，受责备的良心极难应对。它使许多人转向毒品和酒精，也使许多人像犹大一样自尽。许多人不明白，良心不安是神呼召人归向祂的方式。良心有亏并非没有盼望。解决之道不是药片、课程、毒品或娱乐，而是主耶稣基督，唯有祂。良心有亏，不可能靠麻痹自己来摆脱。

比良心有亏更糟糕的，是被烙坏的良心。这种情况发生在有人长期无视神要他悔改、离弃过错的呼召，以至于神把他交给罪的时候。神任凭他以为自己所做的是对的。这是非常危险的光景，能回到真理的人寥寥无几。

一百年前，一个镇或村通常只有一名警长负责控制犯罪。四十年前，有人问其中一位当时已经退休的警长，他们过去怎么能独自控制所有犯罪。他说这很容易；那时候，男人的良心还起作用。他接着说，大多数罪犯最后都会自首。他们宁愿面对监禁，也不愿继续带着有罪的良心生活。

如今有许多罪犯在逃，各地都有男人安然地活在罪中。他们的良心似乎不再起作用，仿佛被热铁烙坏了一样。这不是我今天所关注的；我关心的是耶稣基督的教会。我们在神面前有无亏的良心吗？我们真的盼望主再来吗？我们的生活、人际关系和婚姻中有喜乐吗？我们积极追求神的国吗？还是在试图用世界的方式、金钱、娱乐、享乐等等来减轻良心的不安？

我的孩子们想要一只狗已经有一段时间了，所以我终于决定，是时候带一只小狗回家了。接下来的几个月里，孩子们爱上了它。后来有人把它偷走了。孩子们伤心欲绝，每晚都祷告求神让小狗回来。一天，我们从主日聚会走回家时，一只小狗从一间小房子里跑出来，跳着、叫着。我们很快认出那就是我们的狗。我走到那户人家门口，问那个人这是不是他的狗。他说是，于是我问他是从哪里得到的。那人声称自己买了这只狗。接着我问他是不是基督徒；他羞愧地承认是。我微笑着告诉他，他应该知道神知道真相，神看见一切。我拍了拍他的背，我们就回家了。

然后我们等着……果然，门被敲响了。我打开门，看见那人抱着我们的小狗。他说对不起，把小狗还给了我们。我握着他的手，告诉他，神喜悦他对良心责备的回应。那人离开时没有带走小狗，却得到了远比小狗宝贵的东西：在神面前无亏的良心。

我们选择忽视良心，最终就会变得苦毒；我们会认为人人都在跟我们作对。我们对听到的讲道有意见，对配偶和孩子也有意见。我们封闭自己，把自己与神和祂的子民隔绝开来。

如果你发现自己正处于这样的光景，请记住，只要一祷告，与神之间的天际就能重归晴朗。

神所要的祭就是忧伤的灵；神啊，忧伤痛悔的心，你必不轻看。——诗篇 51:17。

The early church in olden days
Had a desire to tell
The sinner about Jesus Christ,
About Heaven and hell.

Indeed, they were not perfect souls,
But yet they loved their Lord;
And strove to follow this command
In spite of peril and sword.

The more people they converted,
The more the tension grew.
The wicked rulers of the land
Did not know what to do.

A lot of folks were burned at stake,
Some put in dungeons cold,
Because they spread the Gospel word
With faith and courage bold.

These brave soldiers who suffered much
Were such bright lights indeed,
But to tell others about God
They still did see a need.

Now many years since then have passed;
We Christians tend to say
“Be an example to the world;
You need not tell the way.”

But if this point of view were true,
Then I would like to know:
As did the church in olden days,
Why doesn’t our church grow?

Is it that in America,
The fire has grown cold?
Since faith is good, why don’t we share
As did the saints of old?

In other lands this very day,
The fire is burning bright;
Because Christians are zealous there
And vigorous in fight.

While we thank God for freedom here,
They praise their Lord on high.
And thank Him that for Jesus’ sake
They suffer and they die.

So as martyrs in other lands
Are shedding blood for God,
If we would also spread God’s Word,
Our blood would stain our sod.

Is it a blessing from our God
That our country is free?
Or is it ‘cause we aren’t a “threat”
To the society?

Are we ashamed or have no time?
Dear friends, the time is nigh.
If we don’t bring the folks to God,
The populace will die.

So, in conclusion, friends, let’s take
The path that Jesus trod,
Showing lost souls, the narrow way,
That leads men home to God.

– Darren Brubaker

पुराने दिनों की आरंभिक कलीसिया की
यह चाह थी कि बताए
पापी को यीशु मसीह के बारे में,
स्वर्ग और नरक के बारे में।

निस्संदेह, वे सिद्ध आत्माएँ नहीं थीं,
फिर भी वे अपने प्रभु से प्रेम करती थीं;
और इस आज्ञा का पालन करने का प्रयास करती थीं
संकट और तलवार के बावजूद।

जितने अधिक लोगों को उन्होंने परिवर्तित किया,
उतना ही अधिक तनाव बढ़ा।
देश के दुष्ट शासक
समझ नहीं पा रहे थे कि क्या करें।

बहुत-से लोगों को खंभे से बाँधकर जला दिया गया,
कुछ को ठंडी कालकोठरियों में डाल दिया गया,
क्योंकि उन्होंने सुसमाचार का संदेश फैलाया
अटल विश्वास और साहस के साथ।

बहुत दुःख सहने वाले ये बहादुर सैनिक
सचमुच उज्ज्वल दीपक थे,
फिर भी वे परमेश्वर के बारे में दूसरों को बताने की
आवश्यकता देखते थे।

तब से अब तक बहुत वर्ष बीत गए हैं;
हम मसीही अक्सर कहते हैं,
“संसार के सामने एक उदाहरण बनो;
तुम्हें मार्ग बताने की ज़रूरत नहीं।”

पर यदि यह दृष्टिकोण सही होता,
तो मैं जानना चाहूँगा:
पुराने दिनों की कलीसिया की तरह,
हमारी कलीसिया क्यों नहीं बढ़ती?

क्या अमेरिका में
आग ठंडी पड़ गई है?
विश्वास अच्छा है, तो हम बाँटते क्यों नहीं,
जैसे पुराने संतों ने बाँटा था?

आज भी दूसरे देशों में
आग तेज़ी से जल रही है;
क्योंकि वहाँ मसीही जोशीले हैं
और संघर्ष में सक्रिय हैं।

यहाँ की आज़ादी के लिए हम परमेश्वर का धन्यवाद करते हैं,
वे अपने प्रभु की महिमा करते हैं।
और उसका धन्यवाद करते हैं कि यीशु के लिए
वे दुःख सहते और मरते हैं।

इसलिए, जब दूसरे देशों में शहीद
परमेश्वर के लिए अपना लहू बहा रहे हैं,
यदि हम भी परमेश्वर का वचन फैलाएँ,
तो हमारा लहू हमारी धरती को रंग देगा।

क्या हमारे परमेश्वर की ओर से यह आशीष है
कि हमारा देश स्वतंत्र है?
या इसलिए कि हम समाज के लिए
कोई “खतरा” नहीं हैं?

क्या हमें लज्जा आती है या हमारे पास समय नहीं?
प्यारे मित्रो, समय निकट है।
यदि हम लोगों को परमेश्वर के पास नहीं लाएँगे,
तो जनसमुदाय मर जाएगा।

तो अंत में, मित्रो, आइए अपनाएँ
वह मार्ग जिस पर यीशु चले,
खोई हुई आत्माओं को वह संकरा मार्ग दिखाएँ,
जो मनुष्यों को परमेश्वर के घर ले जाता है।

– Darren Brubaker

One fruit of the spirit is a word we all know.
Joy is a blessing for us believers below.
Man can’t produce the Joy that I speak,
It comes from God, given to the meek.
It allows you to suffer, having peace within.
It only leaves at the presence of sin.
Joy brings you through the trials of living.
A peace in your heart that keeps on forgiving.
It doesn’t forsake us; through the struggles we face.
But rather gives courage and keeps us in grace.
Joy is something this world does not know.
It comes not from pleasure, nor feelings that grow;
But comes from the peace that only God gives.
It’s for the redeemed, and the life that he lives.
So why do so many reject this great gift?
That is known for healing and burdens to lift.
If you find yourself lacking the Joy from above,
Turn to the Saviour and His redeeming love!

– Barry Grant
