De formative årene

Se, jeg sender dere profeten Elia før Herrens store og fryktinngytende dag kommer. Han skal vende fedrenes hjerter til barna og barnas hjerter til fedrene, så jeg ikke skal komme og slå jorden med bann –Mal 4:5-6.

Gudfryktige foreldres visjon er å opprettholde et nært og berikende forhold til barna sine. Familieforhold er byggesteinene i menighetene våre og selve veven i samfunnet vårt. Hvis du vokste opp i en tett sammensveiset familie der man delte tanker åpent og på en konstruktiv måte, kan du anta at dette er et vanlig og «normalt» familieliv. Dessverre er det ikke alltid slik.

I denne artikkelen vil vi se på måter å forholde seg til hverandre på som knytter foreldre nærmere barna sine og barn nærmere foreldrene sine. Vi vil rette oppmerksomheten mot de formative årene, det vil si barndomsårene fra fødselen til ungdomstiden. Først skal vi se på hva foreldre kan gjøre for å «holde fast ved» (vinne og beholde) barnas hjerter, og deretter på tiltak for å rette opp dysfunksjonelle forhold.

Den beste måten å følge kvaliteten på forholdet mellom foreldre og barn på er å begynne ved fødselen og følge forholdet etter hvert som barnet utvikler seg. Barn blir født med grunnleggende behov. Når disse behovene blir møtt, skjer det en sunn utvikling. Når de ikke blir møtt, vil barnet streve med å utvikle seg til sitt fulle potensial.

Det første året

Aksept

Studier har vist at et barn kan merke avvisning, noen ganger til og med i mors liv. Hvis et barn er uønsket, vil barnet naturlig speile det det opplever. Derfor har de en tendens til å utvikle en følelse av å være avvist og knytter seg da ikke ordentlig til forelderen. I et normalt forhold mellom foreldre og barn er barnet naturlig knyttet til foreldrene, og foreldrene trenger bare å pleie og styrke båndet som allerede finnes.

Fysisk berøring

Det var en tid da babyer ble skyndet bort til barselavdelingen for «profesjonell» pleie straks de var født. Denne praksisen og andre lignende «overgrep», som at fedre ble nektet adgang til fødestuen, banet vei for hjemmefødsler. Heldigvis har også legevitenskapen blitt «opplyst» om at det oppstår en sterk tilknytning i løpet av de første timene og dagene av et spedbarns liv.

De fleste mødre og fedre trenger ikke å bli fortalt at de skal kose og kysse babyene sine. Til dem som ikke naturlig søker fysisk nærhet til spedbarnet sitt, vil vi si at fysisk avstand i spedbarnsalderen fører til følelsesmessig avstand senere i livet. Vi trenger bare å se på Jesus, som ifølge Skriften viser oss vår himmelske Far, for å lære hvordan foreldre bør bruke fysisk berøring i forholdet til barna sine—Jesus la hendene på barna i Matteus 19:13-15; Jesus tok barna i armene sine i Markus 10:13-16; og gjennom hele Det nye testamentet brukte Jesus hendene sine til å gi helbredende berøring til de mange ulike plagene hos dem han møtte.

God omsorg

Et spedbarns grunnleggende behov er ganske enkle og åpenbare: mat, bleieskift og rikelig med søvn. De fleste foreldre vil naturlig sørge for disse nødvendighetene. I de sjeldne tilfellene der barn blir forsømt på dette stadiet av livet, vil det oppstå varige vansker som følger dem livet ut.

Fra to til fem år

På en eller annen måte har det andre leveåret blitt kjent som «de forferdelige toårene». I virkeligheten er det en fantastisk og nødvendig tid for læring og utforskning for et barn. Det finnes sannsynligvis ingen annen livsfase der et barn er mer formbart. Hjernen utvikler seg svært raskt, noe som gir foreldre en stor mulighet til å påvirke barnet.

Her er noen av disse mulighetene…

…Lære å be

Familiefilosofien vår har vært «Kan et barn snakke, kan barnet be». Selv om barnet kanskje ikke forstår så mye om hvem Gud er, gjør bønn inntrykk på barnets sinn av at «Gud finnes». Denne enkle bevisstheten om at Gud finnes vil følge og velsigne barnet gjennom hele livet.

De første bønnene deres vil helt sikkert være enkle, for eksempel «Takk for maten. Amen». En forelder kan lære barnet å be med en enkel bønn der barnet gjentar etter den voksne. Et barn som utvikler en vane med å be, legger grunnlaget for et disiplinert bønneliv.

…Lære bibelhistorier

Barn elsker å bli lest for. Når en forelder leser for et barn, tror barnet på det som blir lest fordi mamma eller pappa «har sagt det». Før de fyller fem år, er barn ikke i stand til å skjelne mellom sannhet og fantasi. I deres sinn er alt virkelig.

Denne livsfasen er en ideell tid for å introdusere barnet for Bibelens fantastiske fortellinger. Det finnes mange bøker med bibelhistorier. Sørg for at de er bibelsk korrekte og ikke en slags glorifisert fantasi. Bibelhistorier som blir innprentet i barnets sinn, vil følge dem livet ut.

…Utvikling av empati

Nyere studier har vist at empati—barnets evne til å føle det en annen føler—utvikles mellom to- og femårsalderen. Den samme studien har vist at barn som får underholdes med elektroniske medier i denne fasen av livet, ikke utvikler empati. Det raske visuelle inntrykket fra filmer og dataspill overstimulerer hjernen og hemmer utviklingen av de mer subtile evnene til omsorg og innlevelse. Dessuten er mye av denne underholdningen voldelig og selvsentrert. Studien er svært alarmerende når vi tenker på at de fleste barn i dag vokser opp med denne typen surrogatoppdragelse.

Apostelen Paulus profeterte at i de siste dager skal …mennesker være egenkjærlige… –2Ti 3:2. Denne profetien blir oppfylt i livet til barn som ikke utvikler empati.

…Utvikling av lydighet

I alderen to til fem år er et barns vilje mest formbar—det vil si at den kan formes. Foreldre gjør klokt i å se på dette som den beste tiden for å trene viljen. Prøven på om lydighetstreningen virker, er om barnet reagerer på muntlige beskjeder. Barn som ikke tar foreldrenes beskjeder til følge, har ikke lært lydighet og vil vokse opp med å gå sin egen vei i livet. Et barn som lærer å leve med en vilje som er underordnet foreldrenes, vil en dag mye lettere kunne vandre i ubetinget lydighet mot Gud.

Bibelen gir tydelige direktiver om bruk av riset. Ris og refselse gir visdom, men et barn som får gå sin egen vei, fører skam over sin mor –Ordsp 29:15. Det mest effektive middelet mot opprør er riset. Dette må gjøres med omtanke og måtehold, aldri i sinne og aldri i overmål. Så lenge smerten ved ulydighet ikke er større enn «smerten» ved lydighet, vil barnet fortsette å være ulydig.

Kjærlig og omsorgsfull disiplin har den virkningen at barnets hjerte trekkes mot forelderen. Disiplin, HVIS den utøves på riktig måte, virker frigjørende på barnets ånd, ved å befri den fra skyld og gjenopprette barnets forhold til forelderen. Vi har erfart at barnet trekkes mot forelderen som utøver disiplinen. Disiplin har en måte å bringe barnet i samsvar med sin egen samvittighet på, slik at barnet nå kan finne ro—følelsesmessig og åndelig fred og ro. I denne tilstanden av indre fred kan barnet igjen forholde seg til foreldrene sine.

Fra seks år til ungdomstiden

Disse årene er avgjørende for utviklingen av forholdet mellom foreldre og barn. I løpet av disse årene utvikler barna forhold til andre som noen ganger konkurrerer med forholdet til foreldrene. Etter hvert som barna blir mindre avhengige av oss, er det en tendens til at vi ikke føler oss like forpliktet til å investere like mye tid og energi i å opprettholde forholdet.

Tenåringsopprør begynner før barnet når tenårene. Hvis forholdet ikke blir pleiet gjennom disse årene før ungdomstiden, vender barnets hjerte seg andre steder.

La oss se på noen av barnas behov i denne livsfasen…

…Et personlig forhold til Gud

Barn som vokser opp i et kristent hjem og regelmessig sitter under forkynnelsen av evangeliet, vil komme til et punkt der de må velge om de vil gjøre sin jordiske fars Gud til sin personlige Gud. Noen ganger omtaler vi dette som «ansvarsalderen». Nøyaktig når dette skjer, varierer fra barn til barn, men hvis foreldrenes opplæring og forkynnelsen av evangeliet har noen virkning, vil den på et tidspunkt føre til syndserkjennelse og omvendelse, som oftest i ungdomstiden.

Dette påvirker forholdet mellom foreldre og barn ved at et barn som gjør motstand mot Guds autoritet, også vil gjøre motstand mot foreldrenes autoritet, og omvendt. Et barn som kjenner syndserkjennelse, er noen ganger mutt, tilbaketrukket og lite samarbeidsvillig. En klok forelder vil være oppmerksom på dette og hjelpe barnet sitt inn i Guds rike. Selv om vi ikke fremmer barneevangelisering, må vi være klar over om Gud taler til barnets hjerte, og være tilgjengelige når tiden for den åndelige fødselen er kommet.

…En følelse av egenverdi

Denne livsfasen er en tid for læring og handling. Barn lærer ved å gjøre ting, og bør oppmuntres til å oppdage sine skapende evner. Prosessen med å «lære ved å gjøre» innebærer ofte at barnet mislykkes mens det lærer gjennom «prøving og feiling». Barn bør ikke kritiseres hvis det de prøver på, ikke lykkes med en gang. Etter hundrevis av mislykkede forsøk fant Tom Edison til slutt opp en fungerende lyspære.

En følelse av egenverdi oppstår når et barn oppdager at «jeg kan gjøre ting» og «jeg kan bidra til familien min og lokalsamfunnet mitt». Et barn som er tilfreds med seg selv og sine medfødte evner, vil også være tilfreds med forholdet til venner og familie.

Et barn som har blitt trykket ned og fått følelsen av å være inkompetent, vil trekke seg bort fra nære forhold og lete andre steder etter bekreftelse. Manglende bekreftelse fra foreldrene i et barns liv kan påvirke barnets forhold til andre resten av livet. Dette kan bare løses gjennom forståelse av Guds betingelsesløse kjærlighet og aksept.

…Personlig ansvar

I denne fasen av et barns liv må barnet lære personlig ansvar. Enkle ting som å re opp sengen, rydde rommet og hjelpe til med husarbeidet lærer dem å bli ansvarlige medlemmer av husholdningen. Denne disiplinen blir et livsmønster som gjør at de etter hvert kan bli bidragsytende medlemmer av den lokale menigheten og samfunnet.

Å lære personlig ansvar tidlig i livet flytter barnets fokus bort fra å tilfredsstille seg selv og over på å leve i harmoni med andre. Mange som strever med forhold til andre som voksne, hadde en barndom der de var opptatt av å tilfredsstille seg selv eller var selvfokuserte. Foreldre kan forberede barna sine på voksenlivet ved å lære dem å ta personlig ansvar tidlig i livet.

…Gode studievaner

Et førungdommelig sinn er som en støvsuger: Det tar lett til seg kunnskap og husker godt. En omsorgsfull forelder vil sørge for rikelig med godt lesestoff til barnet sitt. I en verden full av bøker kan det være utfordrende å skjelne mellom det som er av god kvalitet og det som ikke er det.

Det er svært viktig at vi gir barna bøker som fremmer sunne kristne verdier i tråd med vårt perspektiv på Guds rike. Mange slike bøker er tilgjengelige fra de anabaptistiske forlagene våre. Kjenn barnets interesser, og oppmuntre det til å utvide kunnskapsverdenen sin gjennom omfattende lesning.

Oppmuntre barna til å lese «over» sitt eget nivå, det vil si bøker som ligger litt over det de fullt ut forstår. De bør også lese «utover», det vil si om emner de ikke naturlig trekkes mot eller er interessert i. Barn lærer ved å lese «over» og «utover». De lærer nye ord, nye fakta og nye begreper mens de leser.

Hva har dette med forholdet til foreldrene å gjøre? Foreldre bør engasjere seg i barnas utdanning, enten de underviser dem hjemme eller ikke. Spør dem om hva de leser. Del dine perspektiver og din innsikt om emnet de holder på med. Vinn respekten deres ved å vise kunnskapen din og meningene dine.

…Ettertenksomhet versus underholdning

Vi oppdrar barn til å bli voksne, og denne prosessen må innebære at vi lar dem utvikle seg til kritisk tenkende mennesker og gir dem et bibelsk grunnlag for å vurdere det brede spekteret av ideer de vil møte i livet.

Å «grunne» betyr å tenke. Å «underholde» betyr å ikke tenke. Mye av underholdningen for barn som er tilgjengelig i dag, er laget for å «underholde». Dette gjelder særlig dataspill og filmer. Disse underholdningsformene oppmuntrer barnet til å åpne sinnet for forhåndsbestemte verdier.

Det er utrolig hva noen kristne foreldre lar barna sine se på. Mange dataspill inneholder vold. De fleste filmer har scener med tvilsom moral. Denne påvirkningen går rett til hjertet av barnet og bidrar til å forme samvittigheten deres—følelsen av hva som er rett og galt.

…Kommunikasjon på hjertenivå

Barn før ungdomstiden bør oppmuntres til å snakke om de indre følelsene sine. Forhold bygges gjennom åpenhjertig kommunikasjon. Det var en tid da man lærte at barn skulle «ses, men ikke høres». I nyere tid har pendelen svingt til det motsatte ytterpunktet, der barnet blir «midtpunktet», og barnets følelser blir sett på som det viktigste.

Begge disse ytterpunktene skaper et usunt og unaturlig forhold mellom foreldre og barn. Når vi i stedet følger Guds ledelse, må forelderen beholde rollen som veileder, beholde overtaket og gi barnet sunn veiledning. Barnets følelser skal ikke dominere forholdet, men barnet skal heller ikke undertrykkes så sterkt at det får følelsen av at følelsene det har, ikke er gyldige.

Barnet som tvinges til å undertrykke følelsene sine, vil ha en tendens til å bli sint, og hjertet vil vende seg mot den første personen som viser omsorg. Barnet som får følelsene sine overdrevent pleiet, vil ha en tendens til å bli svært selvopptatt og vil streve i nære forhold.

Oppsummering

Barn er naturlig knyttet til foreldrene sine. Ordspråkene 17:6 sier: …barnas ære er deres fedre. De fleste barn vil gjerne kunne rose seg av foreldrene sine. Identiteten vår er knyttet til foreldrene våre, og vi måler ofte vår egen verdi ut fra forholdet til dem. Dette forholdet blir rammen for framtidige forhold. Mange voksne strever med vansker i mellommenneskelige forhold som noen ganger kan spores tilbake til forsømmelse eller direkte mishandling fra foreldrenes side. Hvis dette er din situasjon, er det to ting du bør være klar over.

For det første finnes helbredelse bare i et personlig forhold til Jesus Kristus. Ingen av oss har hatt perfekte foreldre, men Jesus er en fullkommen venn. Å kjenne ham nært fyller tomrommet som ufullkomne menneskelige forhold etterlater.

For det andre: Hvis du ikke hadde et godt forhold til foreldrene dine, må du finne Guds helbredelse for dette, ellers vil du sannsynligvis gjenta forsømmelsen og/eller mishandlingen med dine egne barn. Vi har en tendens til å etterligne foreldrenes oppdragerstil hvis vi ikke bevisst velger å gjøre noe annet.

Barn som er glade, tilfredse og sosialt tilpasningsdyktige, er barn som har vokst opp i et kjærlig miljø der deres grunnleggende behov er blitt møtt. Det er et stort ansvar å være forelder, men det gir også den største tilfredsstillelsen, med evige belønninger i tillegg.

And there followed him a great company of people, and of women, which also bewailed and lamented him. But Jesus turning unto them said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children –Luk 23:27-28.

Our Lord began his preaching ministry in a rather usual fashion: in a church, reading from a passage of scripture, …And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luk 4:21. Many sermons from parables to prophecies flowed from the lips of the Lord’s Anointed over the next three years, but never would we guess that His final message would end in such an abnormal fashion. The bruised, beaten, and bleeding Christ, upon being thoroughly molested and mocked, began the painstaking journey up the Via Dolorosa pathway to Golgotha. Tradition would tell us that He fell beneath His cross, but scripture does not confirm this. It is here that Jesus slows His pace to offer His last public address to the women at the side of the road bewailing His plight.

Luke is the only evangelist whose insight records this, as he often takes greater notice of the ministry of women in the life of Christ. It is from him alone that we learn of …Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance –Luk 8:3. It is from him that we learn of Gabriel’s visit to Mary and her inner thoughts concerning the virgin birth and her visit to Elizabeth; Anna the prophetess; the widow of Nain; the Lord’s anointing by the woman who was a sinner; and Mary and Martha’s sibling rivalry at Bethany. So it is little wonder that notice is made of the fulfillment of prophecy by the female gender—…they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn. In that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem … And the land shall mourn, every family apart; the family of the house of David apart, and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … and their wives apart; … every family apart, and their wives apart –Zec 12:10-14.

These wives apart being of the gentler nature are traditionally more capable of offering sympathy and tears than their male counterparts. Thus, who in time of sorrow could refuse their gentle touch, their passionate condolences, and their empathetic pity? Our Lord! He whom we oft find bestowing great compassion on the multitudes, certainly can be touched with the feeling of our infirmities. Yet herein is found the resisting and rebuking of the offerings of lamentation from His female encouragers. Has He become insensitive in His last hour? Since He is God’s own Son, the Lamb without blemish, we must not reckon it so.

Though their tears would seem rather to be chosen than the rabble cry for crucifixion, Christ pronounced their offering defective. We must distinguish this crowd of women to be a different sort than the …many women [who] were there beholding afar off… –Mat 27:55. I would suggest that these are Jerusalem sympathizers: professional weepers who would forget tomorrow that they had wept today. These fickle ladies, adept at making loud wailing, found their way to the house of Jairus before Christ’s arrival. When He pronounced that the dead was not dead, but [that she] sleepeth –Mar 5:39, they immediately ceased their weeping ado; And they laughed him to scorn… –Mar 5:40. This, of course, is but personal surmising, but the prophetic injunction consummating this discourse concerning the impending destruction of Jerusalem, and the evil days to come, were not directed to His followers (they were instructed to flee) but to the resistant Jews.

And so, He deftly rebukes them—Weep Not!

One will not decry their natural empathy. Our emotions are as fleeting as the environment that creates them. We can feel so tender at a given moment without an ounce of the Holy Ghost. We may assume that our passionate tears are flowing from a heart of flesh, but moisture may as well be condensed upon a cold heart of stone. Jesus admonishes them soundly for their weeping. This is not just a gentle reminder, “You shouldn’t worry about me, I’ll be OK.” We see here a forceful rebuke commanding them to weep not. Their well-meant tears were falling on unfruitful soil and Christ will not have it so. Jesus does not condemn sentimental expressions, and certainly does not denounce sympathy and weeping with and for others in their time of suffering. But the tears of these women were only muddying up the path, for they were shed for the injustice, personal loss, and pain they felt. They liked this man. He went about doing good deeds. They hoped that He would free them from Roman tyranny.

“A moment to give a loose to grief,
Let grateful sorrows rise,
And wash the bloody stains away
With torrents from your eyes.
Oh, come and mourn with me awhile;
Oh, come to the Savior’s side.
Oh come, together let us mourn:
Jesus, our Lord, is crucified.
Have we no tears to shed for Him,
While soldiers scoff and Jews deride?
Ah! Look how patiently He hangs;
Jesus, our Lord, is crucified.”

While these shortsighted ancient words call us to weep over our Lord, He himself does not. So oft we find ourselves in parallel situations and refuse to see our own renegade tears. We cry from the depths of pain wrought by emotional, physical, spiritual, and mental anguish. This is but natural. A Hollywood film or a frivolous novel may move us to the same condition of heart. Emotional sympathy excites no sin, but the farewell address of our Lord bids us to look elsewhere to plant our tears and so he beckons us to “weep not for me.”

When we behold the suffering of our Lord, we must look to something else—The Cross!

In His suffering for us, we must see that He is doing exactly what He voluntarily came to do—I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep … Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again –Joh 10: 11-17. While the band of women wailed and grieved, God looked down and smiled—Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand. He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied… –Isa 53:10-11. This current scene had long ago been instated …by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, ye have taken, and by wicked hands have crucified and slain: –Act 2:23. Though Peter’s quick feelings rejected the mention of it, …but for this cause came I unto this hour –Joh 12:27. Like Peter, we weep and resist Christ carrying the timber for fear that we should have to shoulder it as well. Here is the God-ordained apex of human salvation and it was being met with regret. The Son had ‘set His face as a flint’ to conquer the sin of the world. Shall we dilute it with our tears? Herein we are called to a major paradigm shift.

Weep not over the crucifixion but consider our transgressions that nailed Him there. Weep not over the dying Savior but bewail the sinner. Shed no tears upon the surgeon’s knife but grieve the spreading tumor which that knife must cut away. Bewail not the remedy for sin but mourn for the root of it. Cherish not the old rugged cross but lament the old ribald cause. Christ willingly endured the cross for the joy set before Him. Spiritual wisdom will demand that we fling our intuitions to the wind and shout for joy. The cross in not an emblem demanding our sympathy but is the divine expression of His love for us. Jesus chose the cross, came for the cross, prayed for the cross, then ultimately conquered sin by personally experiencing the cross. This is no cause for weeping. Nowhere are we instructed to feel sorry for our Lord.

Our dying Lord exhorts us, Weep not for me, but weep for...

…Yourselves

We are the cause for such a livid scene, and every honest heart will lament and feel the sting for the pain that we have caused. Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani (Mar 15:34), is resting upon our own heads. His God forsook Him because of our transgressions. Our pride-stained relationships, presumption, and rebellion drove Him to such a plight.

‘Twas you, my sins, my cruel sins,
His chief tormentors were.
Each of my crimes became a nail,
And unbelief the spear.
‘Twas you that pulled the vengeance down
Upon His guiltless head:
Break, break, my heart, oh burst my eyes!
And let my sorrows bleed.
Strike, mighty grace, my flinty soul,
Till melting waters flow,
And deep repentance drowns
My eyes in sorrow and in woe.” –Watts

Funerals are a traditional cause for weeping. Each of us shall slowly pass by the bier and numbly stare into the corpse of our own sinful nature staring back at us. All the vain things that have charmed us most lay mortified within the vault. Our final tear-stained farewell must be said to self-love, self-interest, self-centeredness, self-confidence, and self-pity as we stretch to entertain the final words of our Lord.

Thus, might I hide my blushing face,
While His dear cross appears.
Dissolve my heart in thankfulness,
And melt my eyes to tears. –Watts

…Your Children

Not only are we accountable for the Roman spear that pierced His side, but we must consider the Jews who spoke on our behalf that notable day—…His blood be on us, and on our children –Mat 27:25. How little we have considered the thundercloud of divine wrath that we have evoked upon our children. Many parents will pass off the neglected responsibility that they have toward the spiritual wellbeing of their offspring. None of us can change the mistakes that we have made in the training of our children, but the least we can do is spend our days weeping over the poor example we have been and difficulty we have created for their conversion. As the environment around us continues to decay and crumble, we should carefully and tearfully consider their future at every turn. Job did. How much more should we? …when the land sinneth against me by trespassing grievously, then will I stretch out mine hand upon it, and will break the staff of the bread thereof … Though Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, as I live, saith the Lord GOD, they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness –Eze 14: 13-20.

…The Sin of the Nation

For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck. Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry? –Luk 23: 29-31.

In the remnant portion of His message, Christ prophesies of the coming national destruction of Jerusalem. This abomination brought Jerusalem to desolation in 70 A.D. and no atrocity has surpassed it since. Our own nation stands on the brink of the judgment of God and what shall our portion be? Shall we spend our hours lobbying for better leaders, religious perseverance, and anti-abortion/anti-gay agendas? We would better spend our time alongside Daniel, Nehemiah, Ezra, and countless others confessing our sin and the sin of our people Israel, and presenting our supplication before the LORD our God. (see Daniel 9:4-20)

…Fellow Believers

Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people –Jer 9:1. We need not look far to be disappointed by the lives of our fellow believers, for some are already turned aside after Satan –1Ti 5:15. It takes no spiritual mind to judge and label such folly. It is perfectly natural to become sarcastic, shake the head, and proclaim their error unto others. It takes love and concern to shed the penitential tear on their behalf. King Saul had turned back from following the Lord and …it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night –1Sa 15:11.

…Impenitent Sinners

Those of us who can find tears for the dying Saviour should indeed reserve them for the souls to whom death is but the beginning of evils. These souls carry in their bosom the instrument of their own destruction. Sin is the cross to which the soul will be fastened, and habits and depravities are the nails! The soul is bearing its sin, and loving to bear it! Look, it is going to execution, but at each step it laughs! Every step it takes is bearing it towards hell, and yet it makes mirth! Lo, the infatuated one scoffs at the voice that warns him, and every scoff he utters is increasing his guilt! Look forward to its end, its never-ending end; look forward to it steadily, with calm and tearful gaze – is it not an awful spectacle? But what if you should be beholding yourselves as in a vision, or seeing your child in the glass of prophecy? If it is your case, I beseech you repent of your sins, bewail your condition, and fly to Christ for shelter! And if it is your child, give heaven no rest; plead continually at the throne of grace till you have brought down a blessing from God upon your offspring! Never cease to pray until your sons and your daughters are safely landed on the Rock of Ages, and so secured there that they will need no other rock to hide them in the day when Christ shall come. –unknown

…Eternal Tears

Several years ago, hordes of humanity flocked the theaters and wept at Mel Gibson’s motion picture—The Passion of Christ—but few wept over their own sin. Many will say, “Lord, Lord, did I not weep at the scene? Did I not bewail your pathetic condition?” Jesus wept in Gethsemane, over Jerusalem, and at the tomb of Lazarus. But Christ’s tears were eternal and void of every wrongful motive and selfish intent. How natural to soak our couch with tears when our feelings are hurt. We fight pangs of pity at the loss of a loved one or our reputation. These are earthly tears. If God were to …put thou my tears into thy bottle… –Psa 56:8, what would He label it? For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death –2Co 7:10.

E lo seguiva una grande moltitudine di popolo e di donne, che si lamentavano e facevano cordoglio per lui. Ma Gesù, voltandosi verso di loro, disse: Figlie di Gerusalemme, non piangete per me, ma piangete per voi stesse e per i vostri figli –Luca 23:27-28.

Il nostro Signore iniziò il suo ministero di predicazione in modo piuttosto consueto: in una chiesa, leggendo un passo della Scrittura: …E cominciò a dire loro: Oggi questa Scrittura si è adempiuta nei vostri orecchi –Luca 4:21. Nei tre anni successivi, dalle parabole alle profezie, molte predicazioni sgorgarono dalle labbra dell’Unto del Signore; eppure non avremmo mai immaginato che il suo messaggio finale si sarebbe concluso in modo così anomalo. Dopo essere stato brutalmente maltrattato e schernito, il Cristo livido, percosso e sanguinante intraprese la dolorosa salita lungo la Via Dolorosa verso il Golgota. La tradizione ci dice che cadde sotto la croce, ma la Scrittura non lo conferma. È qui che Gesù rallenta il passo per rivolgere il suo ultimo discorso pubblico alle donne sul ciglio della strada, che si lamentano della sua sorte.

Luca è l’unico evangelista a registrare questo episodio, poiché spesso presta maggiore attenzione al ministero delle donne nella vita di Cristo. Solo da lui apprendiamo di …Giovanna, moglie di Cuza, amministratore di Erode, e Susanna, e molte altre, che lo assistevano con i loro beni –Luca 8:3. Da lui apprendiamo della visita di Gabriele a Maria, dei suoi pensieri intimi riguardo alla nascita verginale e della sua visita a Elisabetta; di Anna la profetessa; della vedova di Nain; dell’unzione del Signore da parte della donna che era peccatrice; e della rivalità tra sorelle di Maria e Marta a Betania. Non sorprende dunque che si sottolinei l’adempimento della profezia da parte delle donne: …guarderanno a me, a colui che hanno trafitto, e faranno cordoglio per lui, come si fa cordoglio per un figlio unico, e saranno amareggiati per lui, come si è amareggiati per un primogenito. In quel giorno vi sarà un grande cordoglio in Gerusalemme… E il paese farà cordoglio, ogni famiglia da sola; la famiglia della casa di Davide da sola, e le loro mogli da sole; … e le loro mogli da sole; … e le loro mogli da sole; … e le loro mogli da sole; … ogni famiglia da sola, e le loro mogli da sole –Zaccaria 12:10-14.

Queste mogli da sole, essendo di natura più mite, sono tradizionalmente più inclini a offrire compassione e lacrime dei loro corrispettivi maschili. Chi, dunque, in un momento di dolore potrebbe rifiutare il loro tocco gentile, le loro appassionate condoglianze e la loro pietà partecipata? Il nostro Signore! Colui che spesso troviamo prodigo di grande compassione verso le folle può certamente essere toccato dal sentimento delle nostre infermità. Eppure qui vediamo che Egli resiste e rimprovera le offerte di cordoglio delle donne che lo incoraggiano. È diventato insensibile nella sua ultima ora? Poiché è il Figlio stesso di Dio, l’Agnello senza difetto, non dobbiamo pensarlo.

Benché le loro lacrime sembrassero preferibili alle grida della folla che chiedeva la crocifissione, Cristo dichiarò inadeguato il loro gesto. Dobbiamo distinguere questo gruppo di donne da un altro: le …molte donne [che] erano là a guardare da lontano… –Matteo 27:55. Suggerirei che queste siano donne solidali di Gerusalemme: piangitrici professioniste che il giorno dopo avrebbero dimenticato di aver pianto quel giorno. Queste donne volubili, esperte nel levare alte grida di lamento, giunsero alla casa di Iairo prima dell’arrivo di Cristo. Quando Egli dichiarò che la defunta non è morta, ma [che] dorme –Marco 5:39, smisero subito di fare cordoglio; E lo deridevano… –Marco 5:40. Naturalmente, questa è solo una mia congettura personale; tuttavia, l’esortazione profetica che conclude questo discorso sulla distruzione imminente di Gerusalemme e sui giorni malvagi a venire non era rivolta ai suoi seguaci (ai quali era stato detto di fuggire), bensì ai Giudei che opponevano resistenza.

E così, li rimprovera con fermezza: non piangete!

Nessuno disprezza la loro naturale empatia. Le nostre emozioni sono fugaci quanto l’ambiente che le suscita. In un dato momento possiamo sentirci molto teneri senza avere neppure un grammo di Spirito Santo. Possiamo supporre che le nostre lacrime appassionate sgorghino da un cuore di carne, ma l’umidità può anche condensarsi su un freddo cuore di pietra. Gesù le ammonisce con fermezza per il loro pianto. Non si tratta di un semplice gentile promemoria: «Non dovete preoccuparvi per me, starò bene». Qui vediamo un rimprovero energico, che ordina loro di non piangere. Le loro lacrime ben intenzionate cadevano su un terreno infruttuoso, e Cristo non vuole che sia così. Gesù non condanna le espressioni sentimentali e certamente non denuncia la compassione né il piangere con e per gli altri nel momento della sofferenza. Ma le lacrime di queste donne non facevano che infangare il cammino, perché erano versate per l’ingiustizia, la perdita personale e il dolore che sentivano. Quest’uomo piaceva loro. Andava attorno facendo del bene. Speravano che le avrebbe liberate dalla tirannia romana.

«Un momento per dar libero sfogo al dolore,
sorgano riconoscenti i nostri affanni,
e lavino via le macchie di sangue
con torrenti dai vostri occhi.
Oh, venite e piangete con me per un poco;
oh, venite al fianco del Salvatore.
Oh, venite, piangiamo insieme:
Gesù, il nostro Signore, è crocifisso.
Non abbiamo lacrime da versare per lui,
mentre i soldati scherniscono e i Giudei deridono?
Ah! Guardate con quanta pazienza pende;
Gesù, il nostro Signore, è crocifisso».

Benché queste parole antiche e miope ci invitino a piangere per il nostro Signore, Egli stesso non lo fa. Così spesso ci troviamo in situazioni analoghe e rifiutiamo di riconoscere le nostre lacrime ribelli. Piangiamo dal profondo del dolore provocato dall’angoscia emotiva, fisica, spirituale e mentale. È naturale. Un film hollywoodiano o un romanzo frivolo può commuoverci allo stesso modo. La compassione emotiva non suscita peccato, ma il discorso d’addio del nostro Signore ci invita a piantare le nostre lacrime altrove, e così Egli ci esorta: «non piangete per me».

Quando contempliamo la sofferenza del nostro Signore, dobbiamo guardare a qualcos’altro: la croce!

Nella sua sofferenza per noi, dobbiamo vedere che Egli sta facendo esattamente ciò per cui è venuto volontariamente: Io sono il buon pastore; il buon pastore dà la sua vita per le pecore… Per questo il Padre mi ama: perché io depongo la mia vita, per riprenderla poi –Giovanni 10:11-17. Mentre il gruppo di donne piangeva e si disperava, Dio guardava dall’alto e sorrideva: Eppure piacque al SIGNORE di fiaccarlo; egli lo fece soffrire: quando avrà fatto della sua anima un’offerta per il peccato, vedrà la sua discendenza, prolungherà i suoi giorni, e il piacere del SIGNORE prospererà nelle sue mani. Egli vedrà il frutto dell’affanno della sua anima e ne sarà soddisfatto… –Isaia 53:10-11. Questa scena era stata stabilita da tempo …secondo il determinato consiglio e la prescienza di Dio, voi lo prendeste e, per mano d’iniqui, lo crocifiggeste e lo uccideste –Atti 2:23. Benché i sentimenti impulsivi di Pietro ne avessero respinto il menzionarla, …ma per questo sono giunto a quest’ora –Giovanni 12:27. Come Pietro, piangiamo e ci opponiamo a Cristo che porta il legno, temendo che anche noi dovremo portarlo sulle spalle. Ecco il culmine della salvezza umana voluto da Dio, e veniva accolto con rammarico. Il Figlio aveva «reso la sua faccia dura come la pietra» per conquistare il peccato del mondo. Dovremmo sminuire tutto questo con le nostre lacrime? Qui siamo chiamati a un radicale cambiamento di prospettiva.

Non piangere per la crocifissione, ma considera le nostre trasgressioni che lo inchiodarono là. Non piangere per il Salvatore morente, ma fai cordoglio per il peccatore. Non versare lacrime sul bisturi del chirurgo, ma piangi per il tumore in espansione che quel bisturi deve asportare. Non lamentarti del rimedio contro il peccato, ma piangi per la sua radice. Non venerare la vecchia, ruvida croce, ma lamenta la vecchia causa dissoluta. Cristo sopportò volentieri la croce per la gioia che gli era posta dinanzi. La sapienza spirituale richiederà che gettiamo al vento il nostro intuito ed esultiamo. La croce non è un emblema che richiede la nostra compassione, ma l’espressione divina del suo amore per noi. Gesù scelse la croce, venne per la croce, pregò per la croce, e infine conquistò il peccato sperimentando personalmente la croce. Non c’è motivo di piangere. In nessun luogo ci viene detto di provare pena per il nostro Signore.

Il nostro Signore morente ci esorta: non piangete per me, ma piangete per…

…voi stessi

Siamo noi la causa di una scena tanto cruenta, e ogni cuore sincero farà cordoglio e sentirà il pungiglione del dolore che abbiamo provocato. Eloì, Eloì, lamà sabactàni (Marco 15:34) ricade sulle nostre teste. Dio lo abbandonò a causa delle nostre trasgressioni. Le nostre relazioni macchiate dall’orgoglio, la presunzione e la ribellione lo condussero a una simile sorte.

Foste voi, peccati miei, peccati crudeli,
i suoi principali tormentatori.
Ognuno dei miei misfatti fu un chiodo,
e l’incredulità la lancia.
Foste voi a far scendere la vendetta
sul suo capo innocente:
Spezzati, spezzati, cuore mio; oh, scoppino i miei occhi!
E lascino sanguinare il mio dolore.
Colpisci, o potente grazia, la mia anima di pietra,
finché fluiscano acque che la sciolgano,
e il profondo pentimento sommerga
i miei occhi nel dolore e nell’afflizione». –Watts

I funerali sono tradizionalmente occasione di pianto. Ognuno di noi passerà lentamente accanto al feretro e fisserà intontito il cadavere della propria natura peccaminosa che ci guarda a sua volta. Tutte le cose vane che più ci avevano sedotto giacciono esanimi nella tomba. Il nostro ultimo addio, bagnato di lacrime, va detto all’amore di sé, all’interesse personale, all’egocentrismo, alla fiducia in sé e all’autocommiserazione, mentre ci sforziamo di accogliere le ultime parole del nostro Signore.

Così, potrei nascondere il mio volto arrossito,
mentre appare la sua cara croce.
Sciogli il mio cuore nella riconoscenza,
e riempi i miei occhi di lacrime. –Watts

…i vostri figli

Non solo siamo responsabili della lancia romana che gli trafisse il fianco, ma dobbiamo considerare anche i Giudei che quel giorno memorabile parlarono a nostro nome: …Il suo sangue ricada su di noi e sui nostri figli –Matteo 27:25. Quanto poco abbiamo considerato la nube minacciosa dell’ira divina che abbiamo attirato sui nostri figli. Molti genitori si sottraggono alla responsabilità trascurata che hanno nei confronti del benessere spirituale della loro prole. Nessuno di noi può cambiare gli errori commessi nell’educare i propri figli, ma il minimo che possiamo fare è trascorrere i nostri giorni piangendo per il cattivo esempio che siamo stati e per le difficoltà che abbiamo creato alla loro conversione. Mentre l’ambiente intorno a noi continua a deteriorarsi e a crollare, dovremmo considerare con attenzione e con le lacrime agli occhi il loro futuro, a ogni svolta. Giobbe lo fece. Quanto più dovremmo farlo noi? …quando il paese peccherà contro di me, commettendo una grave infedeltà, allora stenderò la mia mano contro di esso e gli spezzerò il sostegno del pane… Anche se Noè, Daniele e Giobbe fossero in mezzo a esso, com’è vero che io vivo, dice il Signore, l’Eterno, essi non salverebbero né figli né figlie; soltanto essi salverebbero la loro anima per la loro giustizia –Ezechiele 14:13-20.

…il peccato della nazione

Ecco, i giorni vengono nei quali si dirà: Beate le sterili, i grembi che non hanno partorito e le mammelle che non hanno allattato. Allora cominceranno a dire ai monti: Cadeteci addosso! e ai colli: Copriteci! Perché, se fanno tali cose al legno verde, che avverrà quando sarà secco? –Luca 23:29-31.

Nella parte conclusiva del suo messaggio, Cristo profetizza la futura distruzione nazionale di Gerusalemme. Questa abominazione portò Gerusalemme alla desolazione nel 70 d.C., e da allora nessuna atrocità l’ha superata. La nostra nazione è sull’orlo del giudizio di Dio: quale sarà la nostra sorte? Dovremmo trascorrere le nostre ore facendo pressioni per avere leader migliori, perseveranza religiosa e programmi contro l’aborto e i gay? Faremmo meglio a trascorrere il nostro tempo al fianco di Daniele, Neemia, Esdra e innumerevoli altri, confessando il nostro peccato e il peccato del nostro popolo Israele, e presentando la nostra supplica davanti al SIGNORE, nostro Dio. (vedi Daniele 9:4-20)

…i compagni di fede

Oh, fosse la mia testa un’acqua e i miei occhi una fonte di lacrime, per piangere giorno e notte gli uccisi della figlia del mio popolo! –Geremia 9:1. Non dobbiamo guardare lontano per restare delusi dalla vita dei nostri compagni di fede, poiché alcuni si sono già sviati per seguire Satana –1 Timoteo 5:15. Non occorre una mente spirituale per giudicare e bollare simili follie. È del tutto naturale diventare sarcastici, scuotere la testa e proclamare ad altri il loro errore. Ci vogliono amore e premura per versare in loro favore una lacrima di pentimento. Il re Saul si era allontanato dal seguire il Signore e …Samuele ne fu addolorato e gridò al SIGNORE tutta la notte –1 Samuele 15:11.

…i peccatori impenitenti

Quelli di noi che riescono a trovare lacrime per il Salvatore morente dovrebbero davvero serbarle per le anime per le quali la morte è solo l’inizio dei mali. Queste anime portano in seno lo strumento della propria distruzione. Il peccato è la croce a cui l’anima sarà inchiodata, e le abitudini e le depravazioni sono i chiodi! L’anima porta il proprio peccato e ama portarlo! Guardate, va verso l’esecuzione, ma a ogni passo ride! Ogni passo la conduce verso l’inferno, eppure si diverte! Ecco, l’infatuato schernisce la voce che lo avverte, e ogni scherno che pronuncia accresce la sua colpa! Guardate al suo esito, al suo esito senza fine; guardatelo con fermezza, con sguardo calmo e lacrimoso: non è uno spettacolo terribile? Ma che dire se contemplaste voi stessi come in una visione, o vedeste vostro figlio nello specchio della profezia? Se è il vostro caso, vi supplico: pentitevi dei vostri peccati, fate cordoglio per la vostra condizione e volate a Cristo per trovare rifugio! E se si tratta di vostro figlio, non date tregua al cielo; supplicate continuamente presso il trono della grazia, finché non avrete fatto scendere su di lui una benedizione da Dio! Non cessate mai di pregare finché i vostri figli e le vostre figlie non saranno approdati sani e salvi alla Rocca dei secoli, e non saranno così al sicuro da non aver bisogno di un’altra roccia che li nasconda nel giorno in cui Cristo verrà. –sconosciuto

…le lacrime eterne

Alcuni anni fa, folle di persone si riversarono nei cinema e piansero guardando il film di Mel Gibson, The Passion of Christ: ma pochi piansero per il proprio peccato. Molti diranno: «Signore, Signore, non ho forse pianto durante quella scena? Non ho forse fatto cordoglio per la tua condizione penosa?». Gesù pianse nel Getsemani, su Gerusalemme e presso la tomba di Lazzaro. Ma le lacrime di Cristo erano eterne ed esenti da ogni motivo illecito e intento egoistico. Com’è naturale inzuppare il divano di lacrime quando i nostri sentimenti sono feriti! Lottiamo contro fitte di compassione per la perdita di una persona cara o della nostra reputazione. Queste sono lacrime terrene. Se Dio dovesse …mettere le mie lacrime nel tuo otre… –Salmo 56:8, quale etichetta vi apporrebbe? Poiché la tristezza secondo Dio produce un ravvedimento che porta alla salvezza e del quale non ci si pente; ma la tristezza del mondo produce la morte –2 Corinzi 7:10.

The Formative years

Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse –Mal 4:5-6.

The vision of godly parents is to maintain an intimate and enriching relationship with our children. Family relationships are the building blocks of our churches and the fabric of our society. If you grew up in a close-knit family where there was constructive, open-hearted sharing you may assume that that is a common and “normal” family life. Unfortunately, this is not always the case.

In this article we intend to consider methods of relating that draw parents to their children and children to their parents. We will be focusing on the formative years which are the childhood years from birth to adolescence. We will look first at what parents can do to “hold” (get and keep) the hearts of their children, then we will consider remedial efforts for dysfunctional relationships.

The best way to trace the quality of a parent/child relationship is to begin at birth and follow the relationship through as the child develops. Children are born with basic fundamental needs. Where these needs are met, healthy development takes place. When these needs are not met, a child will struggle developing to their full potential.

The First Year

Acceptance

Studies have shown that a child can sense rejection, even at times, in the womb. If a child is unwanted, that child will naturally mirror what they are experiencing. Thus, they tend to develop a sense of that rejection and then not bond properly with the parent. In a normal parent/child relationship the child is naturally bonded to the parents, and parents need only to nurture and strengthen the bond that already exists.

Physical Touch

There was a day when babies were whisked away to the nursery for “professional” care the moment they were born. This practice and other similar ‘abuses’, such as fathers being barred from the delivery room, paved the way for home deliveries. Fortunately, even the medical profession has become ‘enlightened’ to the fact that there is powerful bonding that takes place in those first few hours and days of an infant’s life.

Most mothers and fathers do not need to be told to cuddle and kiss their babies. For those who are not inclined to be physically close to their infant, be advised that physical distance in infancy leads to emotional detachment later in life. We need only to consider Jesus, the representation of our Heavenly Father as detailed in the Scriptures to learn how parents should use physical touch when relating to their children—Jesus laid His hands on the children in Matthew 19:13-15; Jesus took the children in His arms in Mark 10:13-16; and throughout the New Testament Jesus used His hands to offer a healing touch to the many, varied ailments of those with whom He came in contact.

Proper Care

The essential needs of an infant are quite simple and obvious: food, diapering, and plenty of sleep. Most parents will naturally provide for these essentials. In rare cases where children are neglected at this stage of their lives, permanent, lifelong struggles will develop.

Ages two to five

Somehow, the second year of life has become known as the “terrible twos”. Instead it is actually a wonderful and necessary time of learning and exploring for a child. There is probably no season of life in which a child is more impressionable. Their brain is developing very rapidly which provides great opportunity for parental input.

Here are a few of those opportunities…

…Learn to pray

Our family philosophy has been “if a child can talk, a child can pray”. While they may not understand much about who God is, praying impresses into the mind of the child the fact that “God is”. This simple awareness of the existence of God will follow and bless that child all throughout his/her life.

Their initial prayers are sure to be simple such as “Thank you for the food, Amen”. A parent can train their child to pray with a simple ‘repeat after me’ type of prayer. A child that develops the habit of praying is laying the foundation for a disciplined life of prayer.

…Learn Bible stories

Children love to be read to. When a parent reads to a child, the child believes what is being read because mom or dad “said so”. Before the age of five, children are unable to discern between truth and fiction. In their mind everything is real.

This season of life is an ideal time to introduce your child to the wonderful stories of the Bible. There are many Bible story books available. Make certain that they are Biblically accurate and not some glorified fantasy. Bible stories impressed upon the mind of a child will go with them for life.

…Development of empathy

Recent studies have shown that empathy—the ability of a child to feel what another is feeling—is developed between the ages of two and five. This same study has shown that children who are allowed to be entertained with electronic media at this season of their lives fail to develop empathy. The fast-paced visual input of movies and computer games over-stimulates the brain and inhibits the development of more subtle influences of caring and feeling. Additionally, much of this entertainment is violent and self-serving in its nature. This study is very alarming when you consider that most children today are growing up with this sort of surrogate parenting.

The Apostle Paul prophesied that in the last days …men shall be lovers of their own selves… –2Ti 3:2. This prophesy is being fulfilled in the lives of children who are failing to develop empathy.

…Development of obedience

In the years of two to five a child’s will is most malleable—that is, able to be conditioned. Parents do well to regard this as the prime season for training the will. The litmus test for obedience training is whether or not a child responds to voice commands. Children who disregard parental commands have not learned obedience and will grow up taking their own way in life. A child who learns to live with a surrendered will to their parents will one day much more easily walk in unquestioning obedience to God.

The Bible gives clear directives on the use of the rod. The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame –Pro 29:15. The most effective remedy for rebellion is the rod. This must be done discreetly and moderately, never in anger and never in excess. Until the pain of disobedience exceeds the “pain” of obedience, a child will continue to disobey.

Loving and caring discipline has the effect of drawing the heart of the child to the parent. Discipline, IF done properly, has the effect of freeing the spirit of the child from guilt and restoring the child’s relationship to the parent. We have found that the child is drawn to the parent who administers the discipline. Discipline has a way of bringing the child into compliance with his own conscience so that he is now at rest—emotional and spiritual peace and tranquility. In this state of inner peace, the child is now free to once more relate with his parents.

Ages six to adolescence

These years are critical years in the development of parent/child relationships. During these years, children are developing relationships with others that sometimes compete with parental relationships. As our children become less dependent on us there is a tendency to not feel compelled to invest as much time and energy in maintaining that relationship.

Teenage rebellion begins before a child reaches the teen years. If the relationship is not nurtured throughout these pre-adolescent years, the heart of the child turns elsewhere.

Let’s look at some of the needs of children at this season of their lives…

…A Personal Relationship with God

Children who are raised in a Christian home and who sit regularly under gospel preaching will come to a point of decision where they must choose to make their earthly father’s God, their personal God. We sometimes refer to this as the ‘age of accountability’. Exactly at what age this happens will vary from child to child, but if parental training and gospel preaching is at all effective it will bring about conviction of sin and repentance at some point, most commonly during adolescence.

This impacts parent/child relationships in that a child who is resisting God’s authority will also resist parental authority and vice versa. A child who is under conviction is sometimes sullen, withdrawn, and not very cooperative. A wise parent will be sensitive to this and will help his/her child to be birthed into the Kingdom. While we do not promote child evangelism, we must be aware whether God is speaking to the heart of our child and be available when the time of spiritual birth has come.

…A sense of personal worth

This season of a child’s life is a time of learning and doing. Children learn by doing and should be encouraged to discover their creative gifts. The process of ‘learning by doing’ many times involves failure as the child learns by ‘trial and error’. Children should not be criticized if their efforts do not work out immediately. After hundreds of failed attempts Tom Edison finally invented a functional light bulb.

A sense of personal worth results when a child discovers that “I can do things” and “I can contribute to my family and my community”. A child who is okay with themselves and their natural abilities will feel okay with their relationships with friends and family.

A child who has been put down and made to feel incompetent will withdraw from intimate relationships and will be looking elsewhere for their affirmation. The absence of parental affirmation in a child’s life can impact their relationships for the rest of their life. Only through understanding God’s unconditional love and acceptance can this be resolved.

…Personal Responsibility

In this season of a child’s life the child must learn personal responsibility. Simple things like making their bed, cleaning their room, and helping with household chores teaches them to become responsible members of the household. This discipline becomes a pattern of life that will allow them to eventually become contributing members of the local church and of society.

Learning personal responsibility early in life shifts a child’s focus away from pleasing self to living in harmony with others. Many people who struggle with relationships as adults have had a childhood of self-pleasing or self-focus. Parents can prepare their children for adulthood by training them to embrace personal responsibility early in life.

…Good study habits

The pre-adolescent mind is like a vacuum in that it absorbs well and has good retention. A caring parent will provide plenty of good quality reading material for their child. In a world of many books it can be a challenge to discern what is good quality and what is not.

It is of primary importance that we provide books that promote sound Christian values that align with our Kingdom perspective. There are many such books available from our Anabaptist publishing houses. Know the interests of your child and encourage them to expand their world of knowledge through extensive reading.

Encourage your children to be reading “up”, that is, slightly above their level of comprehension. They should also be reading “out”, that is, outside of the topics that they are naturally drawn to or are interested in. Children learn by reading “up” and “out”. They learn new words, new facts, and new concepts as they read.

What does this have to do with parental relationships? Parents should be involved in their children’s education whether they are homeschooling or not. Ask them about what they are reading. Offer your perspective and insight on the subject at hand. Win their respect by demonstrating your knowledge and opinions.

…Musing vs. amusing

We are training children to become adults and that process must involve allowing them to become critical thinkers and providing them with a Biblical foundation for evaluating the broad range of ideas that they will encounter in life.

To ‘muse’ means to think. To ‘amuse’ means to not think. Much of the children’s entertainment that is available today is designed to “amuse”. This is especially true of computer games and movies. These forms of entertainment encourage the child to open his mind to predetermined values.

It is amazing what some Christian parents will allow their children to watch. Many computer games involve violence. Most movies contain scenes of compromised morality. These influences go directly to the heart of a child and help to form their conscience—their sense of right and wrong.

…Heart-level communication

Preadolescent children should be encouraged to talk about their inner feelings. Relationships are built with open-hearted communication. There was a time when the teaching was that children were to be ‘seen but not heard’. More recently the pendulum has swung to the opposite extreme where the child becomes the ‘center’ of focus, and the feelings of the child is understood to be paramount.

Both of these extremes create an unhealthy and unnatural parent/child relationship. Instead when we follow God’s direction, the parent must maintain the role of mentor, maintaining the upper hand and providing healthy direction for the child. The child’s feelings may not dominate the relationship, but neither should the child be suppressed to the point that he is made to feel that his feelings are invalid.

The child who is forced to suppress his feelings will have the tendency to become angry and his heart will be redirected to the first person who shows a caring attitude. The child who is emotionally pampered will tend to become extremely self-focused and will struggle in intimate relationships.

Summary

Children are naturally bonded to their parents. Proverbs 17:6 says …the glory of children are their fathers. Most children want to be able to boast about their parents. Our identity is linked to our parents and we often measure our worth by our relationship with our parents. This relationship becomes the framework for future relationships. Many adults struggle with relational issues that can sometimes be traced to parental neglect or outright abuse. If this is your situation there are two things that you should be aware of.

The first is that healing can only be found in a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. None of us have had perfect parents, but Jesus is a perfect friend. Knowing Him intimately fills the relational void of imperfect human relationships.

Secondly, if you did not have a good relationship with your parents you need to find God’s healing for that, or you will most likely repeat the neglect and/or abuse with your own children. We tend to emulate the parenting pattern of our parents unless we make intentional choices to do otherwise.

Children who are happy, contented, and socially adaptable are children who have grown up in a loving environment in which their essential needs have been met. Parenting is a big responsibility, but one that brings with it the greatest fulfillment, complete with eternal rewards.

Tahun-Tahun Pembentukan

Sesungguhnya, Aku akan mengutus kepadamu Nabi Elia sebelum datangnya hari TUHAN yang besar dan dahsyat itu: Ia akan membuat hati bapa-bapa berbalik kepada anak-anaknya, dan hati anak-anak kepada bapa-bapanya, supaya jangan Aku datang memukul bumi dengan kutuk –Mal 4:5-6.

Visi orang tua yang saleh adalah memelihara hubungan yang intim dan memperkaya dengan anak-anak kita. Hubungan keluarga adalah batu-batu pembangun gereja kita dan jalinan masyarakat kita. Jika Anda dibesarkan dalam keluarga yang erat, tempat berlangsungnya keterbukaan dan saling berbagi dengan hati yang terbuka, Anda mungkin menganggap bahwa kehidupan keluarga seperti itu adalah hal yang umum dan “normal”. Sayangnya, tidak selalu demikian.

Dalam artikel ini, kami bermaksud membahas cara-cara menjalin hubungan yang mendekatkan orang tua kepada anak-anak mereka dan anak-anak kepada orang tua mereka. Kami akan berfokus pada tahun-tahun pembentukan, yaitu masa kanak-kanak sejak lahir hingga remaja. Pertama-tama kita akan melihat apa yang dapat dilakukan orang tua untuk “memegang” (mendapatkan dan mempertahankan) hati anak-anak mereka, lalu kita akan membahas upaya-upaya perbaikan bagi hubungan yang tidak berfungsi dengan baik.

Cara terbaik untuk menelusuri mutu hubungan orang tua dan anak adalah memulainya sejak kelahiran dan mengikuti perkembangannya seiring pertumbuhan anak. Anak-anak dilahirkan dengan kebutuhan-kebutuhan dasar yang mendasar. Jika kebutuhan-kebutuhan ini terpenuhi, perkembangan yang sehat akan berlangsung. Jika kebutuhan-kebutuhan ini tidak terpenuhi, anak akan kesulitan berkembang hingga mencapai potensi penuhnya.

Tahun Pertama

Penerimaan

Penelitian menunjukkan bahwa anak dapat merasakan penolakan, bahkan terkadang saat masih dalam kandungan. Jika seorang anak tidak diinginkan, secara alami anak itu akan mencerminkan apa yang dialaminya. Karena itu, mereka cenderung mengembangkan perasaan ditolak dan kemudian tidak menjalin ikatan dengan baik dengan orang tuanya. Dalam hubungan orang tua dan anak yang normal, anak secara alami terikat kepada orang tuanya, dan orang tua hanya perlu memelihara serta memperkuat ikatan yang sudah ada.

Sentuhan Fisik

Dahulu, bayi segera dibawa ke ruang perawatan bayi untuk mendapat perawatan “profesional” begitu mereka lahir. Praktik ini dan “penyalahgunaan” serupa lainnya, seperti ayah yang dilarang masuk ke ruang bersalin, membuka jalan bagi persalinan di rumah. Untungnya, bahkan kalangan medis pun kini telah “menyadari” bahwa ikatan yang kuat terbentuk dalam beberapa jam dan hari pertama kehidupan seorang bayi.

Kebanyakan ibu dan ayah tidak perlu diberi tahu untuk memeluk dan mencium bayi mereka. Bagi mereka yang tidak cenderung dekat secara fisik dengan bayinya, perlu diketahui bahwa jarak fisik pada masa bayi mengakibatkan keterpisahan emosional di kemudian hari. Kita hanya perlu memperhatikan Yesus, perwujudan Bapa Surgawi kita sebagaimana dirinci dalam Kitab Suci, untuk belajar bagaimana orang tua seharusnya menggunakan sentuhan fisik dalam berhubungan dengan anak-anak mereka—Yesus meletakkan tangan-Nya ke atas anak-anak dalam Matius 19:13-15; Yesus memeluk anak-anak dalam Markus 10:13-16; dan di seluruh Perjanjian Baru Yesus menggunakan tangan-Nya untuk memberikan sentuhan yang menyembuhkan berbagai macam penyakit orang-orang yang ditemui-Nya.

Perawatan yang Tepat

Kebutuhan pokok seorang bayi cukup sederhana dan jelas: makanan, penggantian popok, dan tidur yang cukup. Kebanyakan orang tua secara alami akan memenuhi kebutuhan-kebutuhan pokok ini. Dalam kasus langka ketika anak-anak ditelantarkan pada tahap kehidupan ini, akan timbul pergumulan seumur hidup yang menetap.

Usia Dua hingga Lima Tahun

Entah bagaimana, tahun kedua kehidupan dikenal sebagai “masa dua tahun yang mengerikan”. Padahal, itu sebenarnya masa yang luar biasa dan diperlukan bagi anak untuk belajar dan menjelajah. Mungkin tidak ada masa kehidupan ketika seorang anak lebih mudah dipengaruhi. Otaknya berkembang dengan sangat cepat, sehingga memberi peluang besar bagi orang tua untuk memberi masukan.

Berikut beberapa peluang tersebut…

…Belajar Berdoa

Filosofi keluarga kami adalah “jika seorang anak bisa berbicara, anak itu bisa berdoa”. Meskipun mereka mungkin belum banyak memahami siapa Allah, berdoa menanamkan dalam pikiran anak fakta bahwa “Allah ada”. Kesadaran sederhana akan keberadaan Allah ini akan menyertai dan memberkati anak itu sepanjang hidupnya.

Doa-doa awal mereka pasti sederhana, seperti “Terima kasih atas makanan ini. Amin”. Orang tua dapat melatih anaknya berdoa dengan doa sederhana yang meminta anak mengulang setelah orang tua. Anak yang membentuk kebiasaan berdoa sedang meletakkan dasar bagi kehidupan doa yang disiplin.

…Belajar Kisah-Kisah Alkitab

Anak-anak senang dibacakan cerita. Ketika orang tua membacakan sesuatu kepada anak, anak itu percaya pada apa yang dibacakan karena “kata Ibu atau Ayah”. Sebelum usia lima tahun, anak-anak belum mampu membedakan kebenaran dan fiksi. Dalam pikiran mereka, segala sesuatu adalah nyata.

Masa kehidupan ini merupakan waktu yang ideal untuk memperkenalkan anak Anda kepada kisah-kisah Alkitab yang luar biasa. Banyak buku kisah Alkitab tersedia. Pastikan buku-buku itu akurat secara Alkitabiah dan bukan fantasi yang dibesar-besarkan. Kisah-kisah Alkitab yang tertanam dalam pikiran anak akan menyertainya seumur hidup.

…Perkembangan Empati

Penelitian terbaru menunjukkan bahwa empati—kemampuan anak untuk merasakan apa yang dirasakan orang lain—berkembang antara usia dua dan lima tahun. Penelitian yang sama menunjukkan bahwa anak-anak yang dibiarkan terhibur oleh media elektronik pada masa kehidupan ini gagal mengembangkan empati. Masukan visual yang serba cepat dari film dan permainan komputer merangsang otak secara berlebihan dan menghambat perkembangan pengaruh yang lebih halus berupa kepedulian dan perasaan. Selain itu, banyak hiburan ini bersifat penuh kekerasan dan mementingkan diri sendiri. Penelitian ini sangat mengkhawatirkan jika kita mempertimbangkan bahwa kebanyakan anak masa kini tumbuh dengan pola asuh pengganti semacam ini.

Rasul Paulus menubuatkan bahwa pada hari-hari terakhir …manusia akan mencintai dirinya sendiri… –2Ti 3:2. Nubuat ini sedang digenapi dalam kehidupan anak-anak yang gagal mengembangkan empati.

…Perkembangan Ketaatan

Pada usia dua hingga lima tahun, kehendak anak paling mudah dibentuk—artinya, dapat dikondisikan. Orang tua sebaiknya memandang masa ini sebagai waktu utama untuk melatih kehendak anak. Uji utama pelatihan ketaatan adalah apakah anak menanggapi perintah lisan atau tidak. Anak-anak yang mengabaikan perintah orang tua belum belajar taat dan akan tumbuh dengan menempuh jalan mereka sendiri dalam hidup. Anak yang belajar hidup dengan kehendak yang tunduk kepada orang tuanya kelak akan jauh lebih mudah hidup dalam ketaatan tanpa bertanya kepada Allah.

Alkitab memberikan petunjuk yang jelas mengenai penggunaan tongkat. Tongkat dan teguran mendatangkan hikmat, tetapi anak yang dibiarkan berbuat sekehendak hatinya mempermalukan ibunya –Ams 29:15. Obat yang paling efektif untuk pemberontakan adalah tongkat. Hal ini harus dilakukan dengan bijaksana dan secukupnya, tidak pernah dengan marah dan tidak pernah berlebihan. Sampai rasa sakit akibat ketidaktaatan melampaui “rasa sakit” karena taat, anak akan terus tidak taat.

Disiplin yang penuh kasih dan perhatian berdampak mendekatkan hati anak kepada orang tua. Disiplin, JIKA dilakukan dengan benar, berdampak membebaskan roh anak dari rasa bersalah dan memulihkan hubungan anak dengan orang tua. Kami mendapati bahwa anak tertarik kepada orang tua yang memberikan disiplin. Disiplin dapat membuat anak menyesuaikan diri dengan hati nuraninya sendiri sehingga kini ia merasa tenteram—damai dan tenang secara emosional dan rohani. Dalam keadaan damai batin ini, anak kini bebas untuk kembali menjalin hubungan dengan orang tuanya.

Usia Enam Tahun hingga Remaja

Tahun-tahun ini merupakan masa yang sangat penting dalam perkembangan hubungan orang tua dan anak. Selama tahun-tahun ini, anak-anak membangun hubungan dengan orang lain yang terkadang bersaing dengan hubungan mereka dengan orang tua. Ketika anak-anak kita semakin tidak bergantung kepada kita, ada kecenderungan untuk merasa tidak perlu menginvestasikan waktu dan tenaga sebanyak itu guna memelihara hubungan tersebut.

Pemberontakan remaja dimulai sebelum anak mencapai usia remaja. Jika hubungan itu tidak dipelihara selama tahun-tahun praremaja ini, hati anak akan beralih ke tempat lain.

Mari kita lihat beberapa kebutuhan anak pada masa kehidupan mereka ini…

…Hubungan Pribadi dengan Allah

Anak-anak yang dibesarkan di rumah tangga Kristen dan rutin mendengarkan pemberitaan Injil akan tiba pada saat pengambilan keputusan, ketika mereka harus memilih untuk menjadikan Allah ayah duniawi mereka sebagai Allah pribadi mereka. Terkadang kita menyebutnya “usia pertanggungjawaban”. Usia tepat terjadinya hal ini berbeda-beda pada setiap anak, tetapi jika pelatihan orang tua dan pemberitaan Injil cukup efektif, hal itu akan menghasilkan keyakinan akan dosa dan pertobatan pada suatu saat, yang paling sering terjadi selama masa remaja.

Hal ini berdampak pada hubungan orang tua dan anak karena anak yang menolak otoritas Allah juga akan menolak otoritas orang tua, dan sebaliknya. Anak yang sedang mengalami keyakinan akan dosa terkadang murung, menarik diri, dan tidak terlalu kooperatif. Orang tua yang bijaksana akan peka terhadap hal ini dan membantu anaknya dilahirkan ke dalam Kerajaan. Meskipun kami tidak menganjurkan penginjilan anak, kita harus menyadari apakah Allah sedang berbicara kepada hati anak kita dan siap sedia ketika saat kelahiran rohani tiba.

…Rasa Berharga Diri

Masa kehidupan anak ini adalah masa belajar dan melakukan. Anak-anak belajar dengan melakukan, dan hendaknya didorong untuk menemukan karunia kreatif mereka. Proses “belajar dengan melakukan” sering kali melibatkan kegagalan, ketika anak belajar melalui “coba-coba”. Anak-anak tidak seharusnya dikritik jika upaya mereka tidak langsung berhasil. Setelah ratusan kali gagal, Tom Edison akhirnya menemukan bola lampu yang berfungsi.

Rasa berharga diri muncul ketika seorang anak menyadari bahwa “Saya bisa melakukan sesuatu” dan “Saya bisa berkontribusi bagi keluarga dan masyarakat saya”. Anak yang merasa baik terhadap dirinya sendiri dan kemampuan alaminya akan merasa baik dalam hubungannya dengan teman dan keluarga.

Anak yang direndahkan dan dibuat merasa tidak cakap akan menarik diri dari hubungan intim dan mencari pengakuan di tempat lain. Ketiadaan penguatan dari orang tua dalam kehidupan anak dapat memengaruhi hubungannya selama sisa hidupnya. Hal ini hanya dapat diatasi melalui pemahaman akan kasih dan penerimaan Allah yang tanpa syarat.

…Tanggung Jawab Pribadi

Pada masa kehidupan anak ini, anak harus belajar bertanggung jawab secara pribadi. Hal-hal sederhana seperti merapikan tempat tidur, membersihkan kamar, dan membantu pekerjaan rumah tangga mengajarkan mereka menjadi anggota rumah tangga yang bertanggung jawab. Disiplin ini menjadi pola hidup yang kelak memungkinkan mereka menjadi anggota gereja setempat dan masyarakat yang berkontribusi.

Belajar bertanggung jawab secara pribadi sejak dini mengalihkan fokus anak dari menyenangkan diri sendiri kepada hidup selaras dengan orang lain. Banyak orang dewasa yang bergumul dalam hubungan pernah mengalami masa kanak-kanak yang berpusat pada kesenangan diri atau diri sendiri. Orang tua dapat mempersiapkan anak-anak mereka untuk menjadi dewasa dengan melatih mereka menerima tanggung jawab pribadi sejak dini.

…Kebiasaan Belajar yang Baik

Pikiran praremaja seperti ruang hampa karena menyerap dengan baik dan memiliki daya ingat yang kuat. Orang tua yang peduli akan menyediakan banyak bahan bacaan bermutu tinggi bagi anak mereka. Di dunia yang dipenuhi begitu banyak buku, menentukan mana yang bermutu dan mana yang tidak dapat menjadi tantangan.

Sangat penting bagi kita untuk menyediakan buku-buku yang mengembangkan nilai-nilai Kristen yang kokoh dan selaras dengan perspektif Kerajaan kita. Banyak buku semacam itu tersedia dari penerbit-penerbit Anabaptis kita. Kenali minat anak Anda dan dorong mereka memperluas wawasan melalui kegiatan membaca yang luas.

Dorong anak-anak Anda untuk membaca “di atas”, yaitu bahan yang sedikit melampaui tingkat pemahaman mereka. Mereka juga hendaknya membaca “ke luar”, yaitu di luar topik-topik yang secara alami menarik minat mereka. Anak-anak belajar dengan membaca “di atas” dan “ke luar”. Mereka mempelajari kata-kata, fakta, dan konsep baru saat membaca.

Apa hubungannya dengan hubungan orang tua? Orang tua hendaknya terlibat dalam pendidikan anak-anak mereka, baik mereka belajar di rumah maupun tidak. Tanyakan kepada mereka tentang apa yang sedang mereka baca. Sampaikan sudut pandang dan wawasan Anda tentang pokok yang sedang dibahas. Raih rasa hormat mereka dengan menunjukkan pengetahuan dan pendapat Anda.

…Merenung vs. Terhibur

Kita sedang melatih anak-anak agar menjadi orang dewasa, dan proses itu harus mencakup memberi mereka kesempatan untuk menjadi pemikir kritis serta menyediakan dasar Alkitabiah untuk menilai berbagai gagasan yang luas yang akan mereka temui dalam hidup.

“Merenung” berarti berpikir. “Menghibur” berarti tidak berpikir. Banyak hiburan anak-anak yang tersedia saat ini dirancang untuk “menghibur”. Hal ini terutama berlaku bagi permainan komputer dan film. Bentuk hiburan ini mendorong anak untuk membuka pikirannya terhadap nilai-nilai yang sudah ditentukan sebelumnya.

Sungguh menakjubkan apa saja yang diizinkan oleh sebagian orang tua Kristen untuk ditonton anak-anak mereka. Banyak permainan komputer mengandung kekerasan. Kebanyakan film memuat adegan-adegan moralitas yang dikompromikan. Pengaruh-pengaruh ini langsung menyentuh hati anak dan turut membentuk hati nuraninya—pemahamannya tentang yang benar dan yang salah.

…Komunikasi dari Hati ke Hati

Anak-anak praremaja hendaknya didorong untuk berbicara tentang perasaan batin mereka. Hubungan dibangun melalui komunikasi yang terbuka dan tulus. Dahulu ada ajaran bahwa anak-anak harus “terlihat tetapi tidak terdengar”. Belakangan ini, pendulum telah berayun ke ekstrem yang berlawanan, ketika anak menjadi “pusat” perhatian dan perasaan anak dianggap paling utama.

Kedua ekstrem ini menciptakan hubungan orang tua dan anak yang tidak sehat dan tidak wajar. Sebaliknya, ketika kita mengikuti arahan Allah, orang tua harus tetap menjalankan peran sebagai pembimbing, mempertahankan kendali dan memberikan arahan yang sehat bagi anak. Perasaan anak tidak boleh mendominasi hubungan, tetapi anak juga tidak seharusnya ditekan sampai merasa bahwa perasaannya tidak sah.

Anak yang dipaksa menekan perasaannya akan cenderung menjadi marah dan hatinya akan beralih kepada orang pertama yang menunjukkan sikap penuh perhatian. Anak yang dimanjakan secara emosional akan cenderung sangat berpusat pada diri sendiri dan akan bergumul dalam hubungan intim.

Ringkasan

Anak-anak secara alami terikat kepada orang tua mereka. Amsal 17:6 mengatakan …kemuliaan anak-anak ialah ayah mereka. Kebanyakan anak ingin dapat membanggakan orang tua mereka. Identitas kita terkait dengan orang tua kita dan kita sering mengukur nilai diri kita berdasarkan hubungan kita dengan orang tua. Hubungan ini menjadi kerangka bagi hubungan-hubungan di masa depan. Banyak orang dewasa bergumul dengan masalah hubungan yang terkadang dapat ditelusuri hingga penelantaran orang tua atau penganiayaan terang-terangan. Jika Anda berada dalam situasi ini, ada dua hal yang perlu Anda ketahui.

Pertama, pemulihan hanya dapat ditemukan dalam hubungan pribadi dengan Yesus Kristus. Tak seorang pun dari kita memiliki orang tua yang sempurna, tetapi Yesus adalah sahabat yang sempurna. Mengenal-Nya secara intim mengisi kekosongan dalam hubungan manusia yang tidak sempurna.

Kedua, jika Anda tidak memiliki hubungan yang baik dengan orang tua, Anda perlu menemukan pemulihan Allah untuk hal itu; jika tidak, kemungkinan besar Anda akan mengulangi penelantaran dan/atau penganiayaan itu terhadap anak-anak Anda sendiri. Kita cenderung meniru pola pengasuhan orang tua kita, kecuali jika kita dengan sengaja memilih untuk melakukan sebaliknya.

Anak-anak yang bahagia, puas, dan mampu menyesuaikan diri secara sosial adalah anak-anak yang tumbuh dalam lingkungan penuh kasih, tempat kebutuhan pokok mereka terpenuhi. Mengasuh anak adalah tanggung jawab yang besar, tetapi juga membawa kepuasan terbesar, lengkap dengan upah kekal.

Is it only in the heartbreak,
When confusion ‘round me churns,
That I truly seek my Savior’s arms
And my will toward Him turns?

Is it only in the darkness,
When I cannot see my way;
Or when asked of something I do not know
That I think to stop and pray?

Is it only when I feel
The force of evil ‘round me gathered,
That I seek for His protection;
To in His arms be sheltered?

Oh, foolish heart of mine!
How can you call Him your best friend
When it’s only in your trials
That on Him you will depend?

In good times too, you need Him,
Perhaps more desperately;
Since it’s easier to forget to seek
When the way you think you see.

Even when you fail to hear Him,
When by His side you fail to stay,
He will hear you when you cry to Him
And on Him your troubles lay.

But how much better it would be
To earnestly seek His face
As much in the smoother times of life
As in the rougher place!

To seek and to search, to stay by His side,
To share the joy and the sorrow,
The unknowns in His hands, He’ll be at your side
For whatever may come in tomorrow.

–by Katie Good
