تحيات المحبة باسم يسوع، مخلّصنا وفادينا وربّنا. عندما صدر عدد مجلتنا الأخير، بدا أن معظم الأمور في العالم تسير على نحو طبيعي إلى حد كبير. وفجأة، بدأ كل شيء يتغير بسرعة مقلقة وفي ظل غموض شديد. وما لبثنا أن وجدنا فيروسًا لم يسمع به أحد من قبل يستأثر باهتمام الجميع. كم تغيرت حياتنا.

«واعلم هذا أولًا: أنه سيأتي في الأيام الأخيرة قوم مستهزئون، سالكين بحسب شهواتهم، وقائلين: أين هو موعد مجيئه؟ لأنه منذ رقد الآباء كل شيء باقٍ هكذا من بدء الخليقة» – ٢بط ٣: ٣-٤. اضطررت إلى التفكير في هذه الآية حين بدأ كوفيد-١٩ يقلب تقريبًا كل جوانب الحياة رأسًا على عقب. أين وجدت الكنيسة نفسها وسط كل هذا؟ لا شك أننا لم نكن مستهزئين… ونأمل ألا نكون سالكين بحسب شهواتنا… لكن أين كنا؟ ربما استسلم بعضنا للاعتقاد بأن الأمور ستستمر وفق ما كنا نعدّه طبيعيًا، على الأقل في مستقبلنا غير المحدد.

لكن فجأة، اختفى ما كان طبيعيًا. أُغلقت المدارس، ما أجبر كثيرًا من العائلات على الإشراف على تعليم أبنائها في المنزل. وأُغلقت أماكن العمل، ما اضطر كثيرين إلى إيجاد طريقة للعمل من المنزل. وأُغلقت المكتبات، فاضطر الناس إلى القراءة في البيت. وأُغلقت دور الحضانة، ما اضطر كثيرًا من الآباء إلى إيجاد سبيل يتيح لأحد الوالدين على الأقل رعاية أطفالهما في المنزل. وأُغلقت جميع مرافق العناية الشخصية (مثل محال الحلاقة وصالونات الأظافر وغيرها)، ما اضطر كثيرًا من العائلات إلى تدبر كيفية الاعتناء بأنفسهم بعضهم ببعض في البيت. وأُغلقت جميع مراكز الترفيه، ما اضطر العائلات إلى البدء بتسلية أنفسهم بعضهم بعضًا في المنزل.

اضطرت عائلات أكثر فأكثر إلى البقاء في المنزل من دون فرصة للتفاعل مع الآخرين. وكثرت التنبؤات السلبية الصادرة عن المختصين والسلطات ووسائل الإعلام: سترتفع معدلات العنف الأسري، وستتصاعد إساءة معاملة الأطفال، وستزداد حالات الإدمان، وستصبح الأمراض النفسية مشكلة كبرى.

بينما أكتب هذا، بدأت ولايتنا، أوهايو، تخفف أمر «البقاء في المنزل»، لكن مهما تمنى المرء أو أقلقه الأمر، لم يعد الوضع الطبيعي القديم إلى الوجود بعد. ومع مرور الوقت، بدأت تتشكل أنماط جديدة للحياة. ونعم، تحققت بعض التنبؤات السلبية، لكن ظهرت أيضًا، وسط كل ذلك، بعض المفاجآت.

**************************************

صادفت مؤخرًا مقالًا مثيرًا للاهتمام1 نشرته شبكة CNN بعنوان: «لماذا يشعر بعض الأطفال بسعادة أكبر الآن، وآثار أخرى غير متوقعة للحجر الصحي». ومن المستغرب أن المقال لم ينتشر انتشارًا واسعًا، ولم يبدُ أنه حظي باهتمام كبير في وسائل الإعلام. أرى أن هذا النوع من المعلومات ينبغي أن يهم الآباء والأطفال في أنحاء العالم، لكن لسبب ما لم يبدُ أنه نوع الأخبار الذي أرادت غالبية وسائل الإعلام التركيز عليه.

تسير معلومات كهذه عكس اتجاه العالم. فهي ستقوض قدرًا كبيرًا جدًا من النظام المقبول: ستفلس دور الحضانة المخصصة لأطفال الآباء العاملين؛ وستضطر الأمهات إلى التخلي عن مساراتهن المهنية والبقاء في المنزل لرعاية أطفالهن؛ ولن تعود الأنشطة اللامنهجية وأنشطة ما بعد المدرسة ضرورية للأطفال في أي مجتمع؛ وسيصبح الأطفال الذين يتولى النظام تربيتهم تحت رعاية آبائهم بدلًا من ذلك؛ ولن تعود الصعوبات العاطفية والنفسية تُعالج أساسًا بالعلاج النفسي والأدوية؛ والقائمة تطول.

والآن ننتقل إلى المقال الإخباري. على الرغم من مخاوفهم وتوجسهم من كل السلبيات المحتملة لبقاء الأسرة بأكملها في المنزل معًا معظم الوقت، فإن مئات العائلات من أنحاء الولايات المتحدة… شاركت عبر وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي ومنتديات النقاش شعورًا بالارتياح والفرح إزاء ما آل إليه الأمر فعلًا بعد مرور بعض الوقت. وكانت هذه النتيجة غير متوقعة لدى معظمهم، لكنها، بحسب أبحاث المختصين، تتوافق مع ما [يعرفونه] عن أسباب القلق والاكتئاب لدى الأطفال اليوم. ويذكر المقال أنه وفقًا للأبحاث، أحد أكثر التفسيرات المدعومة جيدًا لزيادة اضطرابات الصحة النفسية هو أن الأطفال لديهم أمور كثيرة جدًا تشغلهم، ولا يملكون قدرًا كافيًا من الاختيار فيما يفعلونه. وهذا نتيجة مجتمع بأسره مثقل بالعمل وشحيح الوقت، وأطفالنا هم من يدفعون الثمن.

اقتبس المقال أقوال آباء من أنحاء الولايات المتحدة، بما فيها كارولاينا الشمالية وتينيسي وكاليفورنيا. وتناول ظاهرة مثيرة للاهتمام أُشير إليها باسم طفرة في السعادة لدى الأطفال خلال هذا الاضطراب غير المتوقع لجداولهم المعتادة المزدحمة. وعلى الرغم من دهشتهم وامتنانهم، جاءت نتيجة طفرة السعادة هذه على خلاف ما توقع الآباء تمامًا.

وبحسب أحد الآباء، تتناول الأسرة كلها الآن ثلاث وجبات صحية يوميًا معًا، من دون استعجال؛ والأطفال ينامون أكثر، وتتاح لهم فرصة الشعور بالملل، ثم يجدون الوقت أيضًا لإيجاد حل بأنفسهم. وأخيرًا، بما أنهم يمرون معًا بهذه الفترة من الغموض والانفعالات الشديدة، فقد منحهم ذلك أمرًا يتقاربون بسببه.

يقول بيتر غراي، أستاذ باحث في علم النفس بكلية بوسطن ومؤلف كتاب «أحرار ليتعلموا»: «فجأة أصبح الأطفال قادرين على [توجيه أنفسهم]. لديهم وقت في يوم ربيعي جميل ليجلسوا ببساطة في الخارج ويستمتعوا بأشعة الشمس. إن الأمور التي تتناولها القصائد، والتي حرمنا أطفالنا منها، أصبحت متاحة لهم فجأة. ويعتقد أن الأطفال يحتاجون إلى أن ينموا نموًا صحيًا وسعيدًا—[وأن تتاح لهم] فرصة اللعب والاستكشاف.

أُدرج عدد من الأمور التي يراها الآباء وعلماء النفس والباحثون نتائج لهذا الاضطراب في الجداول المعتادة لدى كثير من العائلات.

  • إنهم يرون آباءهم أكثر
  • لقد صار سلوكهم أفضل
  • هناك ازدياد في روح الألفة بين الإخوة.
  • إنهم أكثر لطفًا بعضهم مع بعض
  • إنهم يلعبون بمفردهم أو مع إخوتهم أكثر
  • إنهم أقل تعرضًا للإنهاك العاطفي
  • إنهم ينامون بصورة أفضل

وتحدثوا عن أن الأطفال باتوا قادرين الآن على أن يكونوا أطفالًا، إذ لم يعودوا في سباق الحياة المحموم. وأصبح لديهم وقت لاستكشاف عالمهم بطريقتهم. ووقت لاستخدام خيالهم وإبداعهم. ولم يعودوا تحت ضغط الإسراع من موعد إلى آخر يحدده الكبار. ولم يعودوا تحت ضغط تحقيق مستوى أو أداء معين استنادًا إلى أقرانهم. ويقول المقال إن الأبحاث تُظهر أن هذه التصرفات الصغيرة قد تمنحهم [الأطفال] دفعة هم بأمس الحاجة إليها لتعزيز ثقتهم بأنفسهم.

وبحسب المقال الإخباري، فإن إحساسهم [الأطفال] بأنهم يسيطرون على حياتهم وأنهم قادرون على التعامل مع الاضطرابات بأنفسهم [هو] عنصر جوهري في سلامتهم العاطفية. ومن أعجب المفاجآت أن الصعوبات العاطفية والاضطرابات النفسية بدأت تنحسر من تلقاء نفسها. ووفقًا لإحدى الأمهات، بدأت ابنتها البالغة من العمر ١٢ عامًا، التي شُخّصت باضطراب فرط الحركة ونقص الانتباه واضطراب طيف التوحد، تُظهر تحسنًا ملحوظًا بعد نحو أسبوعين. وكان التغيير واضحًا إلى حد أن السلوك السلبي الذي كان جزءًا من هوية الفتاة بسبب الاضطرابات التي شُخّصت بها، بدأ في الواقع يعود إلى ما هو مألوف لدى فتاة في الثانية عشرة من عمرها.

وخلاصة القول… تفيد مئات العائلات من أنحاء الولايات المتحدة بأن أطفالهم يبدون أكثر سعادة.

******************************************

مع أننا ندرك أن هذا يستند إلى حكمة علمانية، فإن معظمه مجرد منطق سليم، مستمد من ملاحظة الوقائع بموضوعية. وتؤيد تعاليم كلمة الله، الكتاب المقدس، البسيطة كثيرًا من هذه الاستنتاجات. ويثير اهتمامي أن كثيرين في الكنيسة اليوم يريدون أن يسيروا على خطى العالم فيما يتعلق ببنية الأسرة والنمو الشخصي وتربية الأطفال. ويبدو أن بعضًا في الكنيسة بلغوا مرحلة يشعرون فيها بأن تعاليم الله بسيطة أكثر من اللازم، أو عتيقة الطراز، أو يعتقدون، لسبب آخر، أنها لا تنجح في تحقيق نتيجة ناجحة.

هدفي من تسليط الضوء على هذا المقال الإخباري هو مساعدتنا على أن نرى أن نظام العالم ليس بالجودة التي يُصوَّر بها. فهو لا ينتج نوع الثمر الذي نسعى إليه جميعًا. فلنعد إلى الإيمان بالكتب المقدسة، واتباعها في طاعة بسيطة، والإيمان بأن طرق الله ستنجح حتى في أوقات الغموض التي نعيشها.

أختتم ببعض الأفكار التي أود أن أتركها معنا جميعًا. خلال الأسابيع القليلة الماضية، سمعت أفكارًا شاركها خادمان مختلفان. وكان كلاهما يتعلق بقضية هذا الفيروس والاضطراب العالمي للجداول المعتادة. أولًا، مع أن هذا بدا عقبة كبرى يتعين على كثيرين منا تجاوزها، يمكننا أن نكون على يقين بأنه لن يكون الأخير، ولن يكون الأسوأ. ويمكننا أن نتوقع مواجهة أوضاع أشد صعوبة كلما اقتربت نهاية الزمان. ثانيًا، هناك فكرة مفادها أنه ينبغي أن ننظر إلى هذا باعتباره نداء يقظة لحياتنا الروحية. وينبغي ألا يكون هناك أي شخص لا يسمح لهذا بأن يُحدث تغييرًا في حياته. لا يوجد إنسان مقدس إلى حد لا يحتاج معه إلى التحسن في علاقته بالله.

Joel had a serious problem of taking things which did not belong to him. Sometimes he would sneak mother’s freshly baked cookies from the cookie jar, or he would take Nathan’s magic markers without asking to use them. To make matters worse, Joel would lie or make excuses when he was caught. Mother and Father had to punish Joel many times. They told him that if he continued to take small things without asking for permission, it could lead to stealing bigger things as he grew older.

And God hates stealing!

One day Mother took Joel and Nathan to Weaver’s Country Store to buy shoes. “Look Mother,” Joel said excitedly, pointing to the shiny pocketknives on the counter. “Will you please buy one for me?”

“No, Joel,” Mother replied. “You must wait until you are older for a pocketknife.”

“O.K.,” Joel answered rather disappointedly.

Later, while Mother was fitting shoes on Nathan, Joel wandered front to the pocketknives again. He looked at them longingly. “That white one is a beauty,” he thought to himself. “Oh, if only I could have it! Mother just does not understand that I am old enough to have one. All the other boys my age have pocketknives.” Just then another ugly thought entered his head. “I think I will just take that white one. No one will ever know.” Joel glanced toward the back of the store where Mr. Weaver was helping fit shoes on Nathan. No one was looking, so he quickly reached up, took the white pocketknife from the box on the counter, and stuck it into his pocket.

Turning nervously, Joel walked back up the aisle. His head started to pound, and his heart was thumping so hard he was afraid everyone could hear it. He hoped Mother would take more time fitting shoes on Nathan. Then maybe she would not notice how hot and red his face was getting. Mother always seemed to notice when something was wrong.

But Mother did not notice this time, and soon they were on their way home. After several days, Joel discovered that it was not fun having a stolen pocketknife. He could hardly ever use it for fear of getting caught. He had to keep it well hidden most of the time!

Several weeks passed. Then one evening, Nathan came into the kitchen where Joel and Mother were doing the supper dishes. “Look, Mother! I found this pocketknife under the couch cushion. I wonder where it came from?”

Joel’s heart began to thump wildly as he watched Mother examine the pocketknife. He wished he could dash outside and disappear. He had just slipped the pocketknife under the couch cushion that evening when Mother had walked into the parlor unexpectedly as she announced that supper was ready. He never thought someone would find it there.

Suddenly he realized Mother was looking at him. “Joel, do you know where this comes from?” she asked.

“Oh! Err – well – ah – I think Cousin Mike has a white one like that,” Joel stammered. “It – ah – it probably slipped out of his pocket the other evening when they were here visiting.”

“I see… Well, I will need to ask Aunt Eva about this,” Mother replied calmly as she placed the pocketknife on the window shelf.

Joel felt miserable. It seemed as if Mother’s sad eyes were watching every move he made. Oh, how he wished he had never stolen that pocketknife! Every time he looked at it, sitting there on the shelf, it seemed to grow larger in size! He decided to go to bed early, but when he closed his eyes, all he saw was that ugly, white pocketknife, leering at him from the window shelf!

The next day, Mother called Joel to her. She was holding the white pocketknife. “I called Aunt Eva today, and she said that Mike does not have a pocketknife. Now Joel, tell me… where did you get this pocketknife? And remember, it does not pay to lie,” Mother said firmly as she placed her hand under his chin and raised his drooping head to look into his eyes.

“I – ah – took it from Weaver’s Store,” Joel stammered.

“Do you realize that was stealing?” Mother asked.

“Yes, I do, and I – I am sorry I lied about it too. I will never do anything like that again. I – ah – I felt so awful ever since I stole it,” choked Joel as his body shook with sobs.

“I am glad to hear you say that Joel,” Mother said. “Father and I have been asking God to help you with this problem of lying and stealing. This evening when Father comes home, you will need to tell him all about it, then Father and I will decide what your punishment should be. After that, we will take you back to the store and you can give the pocketknife to Mr. Weaver. Also, since you used the knife, you will need to pay for it with your own money.”

How Joel dreaded facing Father and Mr. Weaver, but later when it was all over, he felt so much better. That day Joel learned a lesson he never forgot.

Joel had er een ernstig probleem mee om dingen mee te nemen die niet van hem waren. Soms griste hij stiekem versgebakken koekjes van moeder uit de koektrommel, of pakte hij Nathans viltstiften zonder te vragen of hij ze mocht gebruiken. Erger nog, Joel loog of verzon smoesjes als hij betrapt werd. Moeder en vader moesten Joel vaak straffen. Ze vertelden hem dat als hij kleine dingen bleef meenemen zonder toestemming te vragen, hij als hij ouder werd misschien ook grotere dingen zou gaan stelen.

En God haat stelen!

Op een dag nam moeder Joel en Nathan mee naar de dorpswinkel van Weaver om schoenen te kopen. ‘Kijk, moeder,’ zei Joel opgewonden, terwijl hij naar de glimmende zakmessen op de toonbank wees. ‘Wil je er alsjeblieft een voor me kopen?’

‘Nee, Joel,’ antwoordde moeder. ‘Je moet wachten tot je ouder bent voordat je een zakmes krijgt.’

‘Oké,’ antwoordde Joel nogal teleurgesteld.

Later, terwijl moeder Nathan schoenen aanpaste, liep Joel weer naar voren, naar de zakmessen. Hij keek er verlangend naar. ‘Die witte is prachtig,’ dacht hij. ‘O, kon ik die maar hebben! Moeder begrijpt gewoon niet dat ik oud genoeg ben voor zo’n mes. Alle andere jongens van mijn leeftijd hebben een zakmes.’ Op dat moment kwam er een andere lelijke gedachte bij hem op. ‘Ik denk dat ik die witte gewoon meeneem. Niemand zal het ooit weten.’ Joel keek naar de achterkant van de winkel, waar meneer Weaver Nathan schoenen aan het passen was. Niemand keek, dus stak hij snel zijn hand uit, pakte het witte zakmes uit de doos op de toonbank en stopte het in zijn zak.

Zenuwachtig draaide Joel zich om en liep het gangpad weer op. Zijn hoofd begon te bonzen en zijn hart klopte zo hard dat hij bang was dat iedereen het kon horen. Hij hoopte dat moeder nog lang bezig zou zijn met Nathans schoenen. Dan zou ze misschien niet merken hoe rood en warm zijn gezicht werd. Moeder merkte het altijd als er iets aan de hand was.

Maar deze keer merkte moeder niets, en al snel waren ze op weg naar huis. Na een paar dagen ontdekte Joel dat het helemaal niet leuk was om een gestolen zakmes te hebben. Hij kon het bijna nooit gebruiken, omdat hij bang was betrapt te worden. Meestal moest hij het goed verborgen houden!

Er gingen enkele weken voorbij. Op een avond kwam Nathan de keuken binnen, waar Joel en moeder de avondafwas deden. ‘Kijk, moeder! Ik heb dit zakmes onder het kussen van de bank gevonden. Ik vraag me af waar het vandaan komt.’

Joels hart begon wild te bonzen terwijl hij toekeek hoe moeder het zakmes bekeek. Hij wilde dat hij naar buiten kon rennen en verdwijnen. Die avond had hij het zakmes net onder het kussen van de bank geschoven toen moeder onverwacht de zitkamer binnenkwam en aankondigde dat het eten klaar was. Hij had nooit gedacht dat iemand het daar zou vinden.

Plotseling besefte hij dat moeder naar hem keek. ‘Joel, weet jij waar dit vandaan komt?’ vroeg ze.

‘O! Eh – nou – eh – ik denk dat neef Mike zo’n witte heeft,’ stamelde Joel. ‘Hij – eh – hij is waarschijnlijk de andere avond uit zijn zak gevallen toen ze hier op bezoek waren.’

‘Ik begrijp het… Nou, dan moet ik tante Eva hierover vragen,’ antwoordde moeder kalm, terwijl ze het zakmes op de vensterbank legde.

Joel voelde zich ellendig. Het leek alsof moeders droevige ogen elke beweging die hij maakte in de gaten hielden. O, wat wenste hij dat hij dat zakmes nooit had gestolen! Elke keer als hij ernaar keek, daar op de vensterbank, leek het steeds groter te worden! Hij besloot vroeg naar bed te gaan, maar zodra hij zijn ogen sloot, zag hij alleen dat lelijke, witte zakmes, dat hem vanaf de vensterbank grijnzend aankeek!

De volgende dag riep moeder Joel bij zich. Ze hield het witte zakmes vast. ‘Ik heb vandaag tante Eva gebeld en ze zei dat Mike geen zakmes heeft. Vertel me nu eens, Joel… waar heb je dit zakmes vandaan? En vergeet niet: liegen helpt niet,’ zei moeder beslist. Ze legde haar hand onder zijn kin, tilde zijn hangende hoofd op en keek hem in de ogen.

‘Ik – eh – heb het uit de winkel van Weaver meegenomen,’ stamelde Joel.

‘Besef je dat dat stelen was?’ vroeg moeder.

‘Ja, dat besef ik, en ik – ik heb er ook spijt van dat ik erover heb gelogen. Ik zal nooit meer zoiets doen. Ik – eh – voel me al zo ellendig sinds ik het heb gestolen,’ snikte Joel, terwijl zijn lichaam schokte van het huilen.

‘Ik ben blij dat je dat zegt, Joel,’ zei moeder. ‘Vader en ik hebben God gevraagd je te helpen met dit probleem van liegen en stelen. Vanavond, als vader thuiskomt, moet je hem alles vertellen. Daarna zullen vader en ik beslissen welke straf je krijgt. Vervolgens brengen we je terug naar de winkel, zodat je het zakmes aan meneer Weaver kunt geven. En omdat je het mes hebt gebruikt, moet je het met je eigen geld betalen.’

Wat zag Joel ertegenop om vader en meneer Weaver onder ogen te komen. Maar later, toen alles achter de rug was, voelde hij zich veel beter. Die dag leerde Joel een les die hij nooit vergat.

I have heard many Christians say they are not satisfied with their relationship with God. They wonder why God does not speak to them like He spoke with people in the Bible, or even in the early church. I have often thought of this, and at times have felt the same way. I have come to realize that God is still speaking with His children today, just as He always has. The problem is that we are not always listening.

Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: –Joh 16:7-8.

I have excellent hearing. However, I had to consider whether I listen to only the things and people I desire and unknowingly block out what I do not want to hear?

Today the god of this world has filled people’s lives with distractions, and while not all are bad, he (Satan) wants our attention and focus to be on other things, then when God speaks to us, we do not hear. So, what happens when we stop listening to God? He stops speaking, and we eventually drift away from truth. God gave everyone a conscience. It is a wonderful thing that keeps us on the strait and narrow way. But God’s word says that if we continue to ignore the prodding of the Spirit, our conscience will stop working properly. Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron; –1Ti 4:1-2. In other words, we do wrong, but since our conscience doesn’t work any longer, there is no feeling there. We begin to justify our actions; we are always right.

I remember years ago as I was driving to work, I noticed a police car coming in my direction. I then realized I was not wearing my seat belt, so I slyly slipped it on, hoping he had not noticed. To my disappointment, he turned around and pulled me over. He asked me a very straightforward question. “Sir, did you just put your seat belt on when you saw me?”

I smiled and told him with an apology that I did. He went back to his car and several minutes later he returned. He told me that he sees many people do the same thing. They see him and quickly put their seat belt on, but he has never had anyone admit to it. They all argue with him that their seat belt was already on. He gave me a warning and thanked me for being honest.

It is sad that today, so many people no longer listen to their conscience, which is telling them to do right. Instead, even when they know they are wrong they argue, trying to deny or justify their wrong. We expect this from the world, but is this a practice that we are seeing more and more in the church today? I have even heard many people use the Bible to try to justify their wrongdoing. Have we stopped listening to God? Have we pampered ‘self ’ to the point that we no longer can admit when we are wrong? Would we rather look ‘right’ and have a guilty conscience? Or humble ourselves, admit our failure and rejoice with a clear conscience. Friends, do we value a clear conscience? Can we say with the apostle Paul that we …have lived in all good conscience before God until this day … to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men –Act 23:1-24:16.

Let’s look at the account of David and Bathsheba. David was a man after God’s own heart, so why did this happen? The account is in II Samuel chapter 11. It was the time when kings went forth to battle, and they had a battle going with the children of Ammon. But David tarried still at Jerusalem. When we begin to do things the way we want and ignore the call of God in our lives, we hinder the Spirit. So, David is just hanging around; it says that David was laying on his bed. Was he seeking God? It doesn’t seem like it. An ancient proverb says that ‘idleness is the devil’s workshop’. David decides to take a stroll on the roof. Was David innocent even at this time? Maybe David already knew he could see this woman from his rooftop? Maybe he had been tempted before, ‘at even tide’, to look over toward Bathsheba’s home. Either way, he now found himself in an awkward situation. What amazes me is there was no thinking—David does not seem to give his conscience any time at all to work. He simply sent messengers to go and bring her to him, and then he laid with her. Again, it seems that David’s conscience is not working. But rather he goes right into coverup mode. He calls for Bathsheba’s husband and eventually has him killed… and then marries Bathsheba. But God was not done with David. In II Samuel chapter 12 it says that God sent Nathan to David. Often before God gives us over, He sends a messenger. Maybe it’s a brother in the church, maybe it’s a church leader. Are we aware of, and listening to, the messengers God sends to us?

Nathan went to David and told him a story…

There were two men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor. The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds. But the poor man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.

And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him. And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity. And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man… –2Sa 12:4-7.

David now came face to face with his sin; there was still time. David repented with genuine godly sorrow and was forgiven (read Psalm 51).

David could have become angry with Nathan and had him killed. Or what if Nathan would have refused to go talk to David because he feared him? When we want a clear conscience, I believe people around us will know that and it will be easy for them to come and talk to us about sin in our lives. But too often the opposite happens; we would rather live the way we want and shield ourselves from the counsel of others, and when a brother or sister comes to talk to us, we get angry and they don’t come talk to us again.

The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise –Pro 12:15.

If Nathan would have refused to talk to David, maybe David would never have seen his sin. It is our responsibility to talk to one another and it leads to a clear conscience. It often doesn’t feel good when our conscience is pricked, but that is the way God designed it, so we act upon a guilty conscience. Unfortunately, there are many other accounts in God’s word where someone refused to repent, and God’s judgement was poured out.

When our conscience is pricked, we have two choices: either to get angry and deny, or to humble ourselves and repent. It is really that simple. What do we find ourselves doing when God speaks to us through our conscience? Are we broken?

In the book of Acts, we have a few accounts of how people responded to their conscience being pricked. The first account is in chapter 2, the day of Pentecost. Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit, lifted up his voice and spoke some very hard things to the large crowd that had gathered. It says that after Peter was finished preaching, the people were pricked in their heart. So how did these people respond? They …said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do? Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost –Act 2:37-38. And about 3,000 souls were added to the Kingdom.

When we respond to that pricking of the heart, or the voice of God to our conscience, God hears us and will forgive us! However, if we turn just a few pages in our Bibles we see another response to the pricking of God in our conscience.

In Acts chapter 5 we see that the apostles went about preaching and healing the sick, and the high priest and those that were with him put them in prison. But God opened the doors and released them. Notice that this group of more than likely very young men, and new in the faith, rose up early the next morning and went into the temple to teach. They were sold out. That day the high priest wanted to talk with the disciples, so he sent someone to the prison, but they were not there. Then came one and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people –Act 5:25. So, they went to the temple and brought them to the high priest. Peter then again began to speak boldly, telling them that they should obey God rather than man: …we are his witnesses of these things; and so is also the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to them that obey him. When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel to slay them –Act 5: 32-33.

Again, we see God speaking, convicting the conscience, but notice their reaction to the voice of God: ‘They took counsel to slay them’. Even though we are believers, we still tend to give a similar response when our conscience is pricked. We want to neutralize whatever it was that was spoken to us. In similar manner as David had Uriah killed, the Sadducees sought to slay the disciples, Herod beheaded John the Baptist, and the World killed our Lord, we avoid people that speak truth and say the hard things that God wants us to hear. The Lord is hated by the world because he testifies …of it, that the works thereof are evil –Joh 7:7.

Maybe we begin to have itching ears, hearing only what we want. We rid ourselves of the presence of people who love us and desire to speak into our lives. We often forget that our conscience is a gift from God and a very important part of a believer’s life. When it stops working, we are in big trouble.

A guilty conscience has proven to be a very difficult thing to deal with. It has caused many to turn to drugs and alcohol. It has also caused many like Judas to take their own life. Many people do not understand that a troubled conscience is God’s way of calling someone to himself. There is great hope for a bad conscience. It is not pills, or classes, or drugs, or entertainment. It is the Lord Jesus Christ and only Him. It is impossible to drown away a bad conscience.

What is worse than a bad conscience is a seared conscience. This occurs when someone has ignored God’s calling to repent and turn from their wrong for so long that He gives them over to their sin. He allows them to think that what they are doing is okay. This is a position that is very dangerous, and few find their way back to truth.

One hundred years ago it was common for a town or village to only have one sheriff to control its crime. Forty years ago, someone asked one of these then-retired sheriffs how they were able to control all the crime by themselves. He said that it was easy; back then, men’s consciences still worked. He went on to say that most criminals would eventually turn themselves in. They would rather face prison than continue living with a guilty conscience.

Today there are many criminals on the run, and men everywhere comfortably living in sin. It seems that their conscience is no longer working, being seared with a hot iron. That is not my concern today, but rather my concern is for the church of Jesus Christ. Do we have a clear conscience before God? Are we really looking forward to the return of the Lord? Do we have joy in our lives, relationships, and marriages? Are we actively pursuing the Kingdom of God, or are we trying to ease our conscience with the ways of the world, money, entertainment, pleasure, and the likes?

My children wanted a dog for some time, so I finally decided it was time and brought a puppy home. The children fell in love with it over the next months. Then someone stole it. The children were devastated, and they prayed every night that God would bring the puppy back. One day as we walked home from the Sunday service a puppy came running from a small house, jumping and yipping. We quickly realized it was our puppy. I walked over to the house and asked the man if this was his dog. He said that it was, so I asked him where he had gotten it. The man claimed he had purchased the dog. I then asked him if he was a Christian; guiltily he said he was. I smiled and told him that he should know that God knows the truth, that God sees everything. I patted him on the back, and we walked home.

Then we waited… sure enough, there was a knock at the door. Opening the door, I saw the man holding our puppy. He said he was sorry and gave the puppy back. I shook his hand and told him that God was pleased with his response to his conscience. The man walked away with no puppy, but with something far greater, a clear conscience before God.

When we choose to ignore our conscience, we eventually become bitter; we believe everyone is out to get us. We have a problem with the sermons we hear, we have a problem with our spouse and children. We shut ourselves off, we separate ourselves from God and his people.

If you find yourself in this state, remember, a clear heaven is only a prayer away.

The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise –Psa 51:17.

Jag har hört många kristna säga att de inte är nöjda med sin relation till Gud. De undrar varför Gud inte talar till dem som han talade med människor i Bibeln, eller till och med i den tidiga församlingen. Jag har ofta tänkt på detta och har ibland känt likadant. Jag har kommit till insikt om att Gud fortfarande talar till sina barn i dag, precis som han alltid har gjort. Problemet är att vi inte alltid lyssnar.

Men jag säger er sanningen: Det är bäst för er att jag går bort. Ty om jag inte går bort, kommer Hjälparen inte till er; men om jag går bort, ska jag sända honom till er. Och när han kommer ska han överbevisa världen om synd, rättfärdighet och dom: – Joh 16:7-8.

Jag har utmärkt hörsel. Ändå var jag tvungen att fundera över om jag bara lyssnar på de saker och människor jag vill lyssna på och om jag omedvetet stänger ute det jag inte vill höra.

I dag har denna världens gud fyllt människors liv med distraktioner, och även om inte allt är dåligt vill han (Satan) att vår uppmärksamhet och vårt fokus ska ligga på annat, så att vi inte hör när Gud talar till oss. Vad händer då när vi slutar lyssna på Gud? Han slutar tala, och till slut glider vi bort från sanningen. Gud har gett alla ett samvete. Det är en underbar sak som håller oss på den smala och rätta vägen. Men Guds ord säger att om vi fortsätter att ignorera Andens maningar, kommer vårt samvete att sluta fungera som det ska. Men Anden säger uttryckligen att i de sista tiderna ska några avfalla från tron och hålla sig till förföriska andar och onda andars läror; de ska tala lögner i hyckleri; de har fått sitt samvete brännmärkt med ett glödande järn; – 1 Tim 4:1-2. Med andra ord gör vi fel, men eftersom vårt samvete inte längre fungerar känner vi ingenting. Vi börjar rättfärdiga våra handlingar; vi har alltid rätt.

Jag minns att jag för många år sedan, när jag körde till jobbet, lade märke till en polisbil som kom körande mot mig. Då insåg jag att jag inte hade bilbältet på mig, så jag satte diskret på mig det i hopp om att polisen inte hade märkt något. Till min besvikelse vände han om och stoppade mig. Han ställde en mycket rak fråga: ”Sir, tog ni just på er bilbältet när ni såg mig?”

Jag log och bad om ursäkt och talade om att det hade jag gjort. Han gick tillbaka till sin bil och kom tillbaka efter några minuter. Han berättade att han ser många människor göra samma sak. De får syn på honom och tar snabbt på sig bilbältet, men han har aldrig varit med om att någon erkänner det. Alla hävdar att bilbältet redan var på. Han gav mig en varning och tackade mig för att jag var ärlig.

Det är sorgligt att så många människor i dag inte längre lyssnar på sitt samvete, som säger åt dem att göra det rätta. I stället argumenterar de, även när de vet att de har fel, och försöker förneka eller rättfärdiga det de gjort. Vi förväntar oss detta av världen, men ser vi samma beteende allt oftare i kyrkan i dag? Jag har till och med hört många använda Bibeln för att försöka rättfärdiga sina felsteg. Har vi slutat lyssna på Gud? Har vi skämt bort ”jaget” så mycket att vi inte längre kan erkänna när vi har fel? Skulle vi hellre vilja verka ha ”rätt” och ha ett skyldigt samvete? Eller ödmjuka oss, erkänna våra misslyckanden och glädjas åt ett rent samvete? Vänner, värdesätter vi ett rent samvete? Kan vi säga tillsammans med aposteln Paulus att vi …har levt med ett fullkomligt gott samvete inför Gud ända till denna dag … alltid ha ett samvete som är utan anstöt inför Gud och människor – Apg 23:1-24:16.

Låt oss se på berättelsen om David och Batseba. David var en man efter Guds eget hjärta, så varför hände detta? Berättelsen finns i Andra Samuelsboken, kapitel 11. Det var den tid då kungarna drog ut i strid, och de låg i krig med ammoniterna. Men David stannade kvar i Jerusalem. När vi börjar göra saker på vårt eget sätt och ignorerar Guds kallelse i våra liv, hindrar vi Anden. David gick alltså bara omkring och drog; det står att David låg på sin bädd. Sökte han Gud? Det verkar inte så. Ett gammalt ordspråk säger att ”sysslolöshet är djävulens verkstad”. David bestämmer sig för att ta en promenad på taket. Var David oskyldig ens då? Kanske visste David redan att han kunde se den här kvinnan från taket? Kanske hade han tidigare frestats att se mot Batsebas hus ”vid aftontid”. Hur det än var fann han sig nu i en besvärlig situation. Det som förvånar mig är att han inte verkar ha tänkt efter alls – David tycks inte ge sitt samvete någon tid att verka. Han skickade helt enkelt budbärare för att hämta henne till sig, och sedan låg han med henne. Återigen verkar Davids samvete inte fungera. I stället går han genast in i mörkläggningsläge. Han kallar till sig Batsebas man och ser till slut till att han blir dödad … och gifter sig sedan med Batseba. Men Gud var inte färdig med David. I Andra Samuelsboken, kapitel 12, står det att Gud sände Natan till David. Ofta sänder Gud en budbärare innan han överlämnar oss åt oss själva. Det kanske är en broder i församlingen, kanske en församlingsledare. Är vi medvetna om och lyssnar vi till de budbärare Gud sänder till oss?

Natan gick till David och berättade en historia …

Det fanns två män i en stad: den ene var rik och den andre fattig. Den rike hade mycket stora hjordar av får och boskap. Men den fattige hade ingenting utom ett enda litet tacklamm, som han hade köpt och fött upp. Det växte upp tillsammans med honom och hans barn; det åt av hans mat, drack ur hans bägare och låg i hans famn. Det var som en dotter för honom.

En gång kom en resande till den rike mannen. Denne ville inte ta något av sina egna får eller sin egen boskap och tillreda det åt den resande som hade kommit till honom, utan tog den fattige mannens lamm och tillredde det åt mannen som hade kommit till honom. Då upptändes Davids vrede kraftigt mot mannen, och han sade till Natan: ”Så sant Herren lever: den man som har gjort detta förtjänar döden! Han ska ersätta lammet fyrfalt, eftersom han gjorde detta och inte hade medlidande.” Då sade Natan till David: ”Du är den mannen!” … – 2 Sam 12:4-7.

Nu ställdes David ansikte mot ansikte med sin synd; det fanns fortfarande tid. David omvände sig med äkta, gudomlig sorg och blev förlåten (läs Psalm 51).

David kunde ha blivit arg på Natan och låtit döda honom. Eller tänk om Natan hade vägrat att gå och tala med David för att han var rädd för honom? När vi vill ha ett rent samvete tror jag att människorna omkring oss kommer att märka det, och då blir det lätt för dem att komma och tala med oss om synd i våra liv. Men alltför ofta händer det motsatta; vi vill hellre leva som vi själva vill och värja oss mot andras råd, och när en broder eller syster kommer för att tala med oss blir vi arga, och då kommer de inte och talar med oss igen.

En dåres väg är rätt i hans egna ögon, men den som lyssnar till råd är vis – Ords 12:15.

Om Natan hade vägrat att tala med David kanske David aldrig hade sett sin synd. Det är vårt ansvar att tala med varandra, och det leder till ett rent samvete. Det känns ofta inte bra när samvetet sticker till, men Gud har utformat det så för att vi ska handla när samvetet anklagar oss. Tyvärr finns det många andra berättelser i Guds ord där någon vägrade att omvända sig och Guds dom föll.

När samvetet sticker till har vi två val: antingen blir vi arga och förnekar, eller så ödmjukar vi oss och omvänder oss. Så enkelt är det. Vad gör vi när Gud talar till oss genom vårt samvete? Är vi förkrossade?

I Apostlagärningarna finns några berättelser om hur människor reagerade när samvetet stack till. Den första berättelsen finns i kapitel 2, på pingstdagen. Petrus var fylld av den helige Ande, höjde sin röst och talade mycket hårda ord till den stora folkmassa som hade samlats. Det står att människorna blev stingna i hjärtat när Petrus hade predikat färdigt. Hur reagerade de då? De …sade till Petrus och de andra apostlarna: ”Bröder, vad ska vi göra?” Petrus svarade dem: ”Omvänd er och låt er alla döpas i Jesu Kristi namn till era synders förlåtelse, så ska ni få den helige Andes gåva – Apg 2:37-38. Och omkring 3 000 själar lades till riket.

När vi reagerar på detta styng i hjärtat, eller på Guds röst till vårt samvete, hör Gud oss och kommer att förlåta oss! Men om vi bläddrar bara några sidor framåt i våra biblar ser vi en annan reaktion på Guds tilltal till vårt samvete.

I Apostlagärningarna, kapitel 5, ser vi att apostlarna gick omkring och predikade och botade sjuka, och att översteprästen och hans anhängare satte dem i fängelse. Men Gud öppnade dörrarna och befriade dem. Lägg märke till att denna grupp troligen mycket unga män, nya i tron, steg upp tidigt nästa morgon och gick in i templet för att undervisa. De hade gett allt. Den dagen ville översteprästen tala med lärjungarna, så han skickade någon till fängelset, men de var inte där. Då kom någon och berättade för dem: ”Se, männen som ni satte i fängelse står i templet och undervisar folket” – Apg 5:25. De gick då till templet och hämtade dem till översteprästen. Petrus började åter tala frimodigt och sade att de måste lyda Gud mer än människor: …vi är vittnen till detta, och det är också den helige Ande, som Gud har gett åt dem som lyder honom. När de hörde detta blev de ursinniga och ville döda dem – Apg 5:32-33.

Återigen ser vi Gud tala och överbevisa samvetet, men lägg märke till deras reaktion på Guds röst: ”De ville döda dem.” Även om vi är troende har vi fortfarande en tendens att reagera på liknande sätt när samvetet sticker till. Vi vill oskadliggöra det som har sagts till oss. På samma sätt som David lät döda Uria sökte saddukéerna döda lärjungarna, Herodes halshögg Johannes Döparen och världen dödade vår Herre, undviker vi människor som talar sanning och säger de svåra saker som Gud vill att vi ska höra. Herren är hatad av världen eftersom han vittnar …om den att dess gärningar är onda – Joh 7:7.

Kanske börjar vi få kliande öron och bara höra det vi vill höra. Vi gör oss av med närvaron av människor som älskar oss och vill tala in i våra liv. Vi glömmer ofta att vårt samvete är en gåva från Gud och en mycket viktig del av den troendes liv. När det slutar fungera är vi illa ute.

Ett belastat samvete har visat sig vara mycket svårt att hantera. Det har fått många att vända sig till droger och alkohol. Det har också fått många, som Judas, att ta sitt eget liv. Många förstår inte att ett oroligt samvete är Guds sätt att kalla en människa till sig. Det finns stort hopp för den som har ett dåligt samvete. Lösningen är inte piller, kurser, droger eller underhållning. Den är Herren Jesus Kristus, och ingen annan. Det är omöjligt att dränka ett dåligt samvete.

Värre än ett dåligt samvete är ett brännmärkt samvete. Detta sker när någon så länge har ignorerat Guds kallelse att omvända sig och vända sig bort från det onda att han överlämnar personen åt hennes synd. Han låter henne tro att det hon gör är okej. Detta är ett mycket farligt tillstånd, och få hittar tillbaka till sanningen.

För hundra år sedan var det vanligt att en stad eller by bara hade en enda sheriff som höll ordning på brottsligheten. För fyrtio år sedan frågade någon en av dessa sheriffar, som då hade gått i pension, hur de hade kunnat hålla brottsligheten under kontroll helt på egen hand. Han sade att det var enkelt; på den tiden fungerade fortfarande männens samveten. Han fortsatte med att säga att de flesta brottslingar förr eller senare brukade överlämna sig själva. De föredrog att möta fängelsestraff framför att fortsätta leva med ett belastat samvete.

I dag är många brottslingar på flykt, och män överallt lever obekymrat i synd. Det verkar som om deras samveten inte längre fungerar, utan har brännmärkts med ett glödande järn. Det är inte det jag bekymrar mig för i dag; jag bekymrar mig i stället för Jesu Kristi kyrka. Har vi ett rent samvete inför Gud? Ser vi verkligen fram emot Herrens återkomst? Har vi glädje i våra liv, relationer och äktenskap? Strävar vi aktivt efter Guds rike, eller försöker vi stilla vårt samvete med världens sätt, pengar, underhållning, njutningar och liknande?

Mina barn hade länge velat ha en hund, så till slut bestämde jag mig för att det var dags och tog hem en valp. Under de följande månaderna blev barnen förälskade i den. Sedan stal någon den. Barnen var förtvivlade, och varje kväll bad de att Gud skulle låta valpen komma tillbaka. En dag när vi gick hem från söndagsgudstjänsten kom en valp springande från ett litet hus, hoppande och skällande. Vi insåg snabbt att det var vår valp. Jag gick fram till huset och frågade mannen om det var hans hund. Han sade att det var det, så jag frågade var han hade fått den ifrån. Mannen hävdade att han hade köpt hunden. Då frågade jag om han var kristen; skuldmedveten svarade han ja. Jag log och sade att han borde veta att Gud känner sanningen och ser allting. Jag klappade honom på ryggen, och vi gick hem.

Sedan väntade vi … och mycket riktigt knackade det på dörren. När jag öppnade såg jag mannen stå där med vår valp. Han sade att han var ledsen och lämnade tillbaka valpen. Jag skakade hans hand och sade att Gud gladde sig över hur han hade reagerat på sitt samvete. Mannen gick därifrån utan valp, men med något mycket större: ett rent samvete inför Gud.

När vi väljer att ignorera vårt samvete blir vi till slut bittra; vi tror att alla är ute efter oss. Vi har problem med predikningarna vi hör, vi har problem med vår make eller maka och våra barn. Vi stänger in oss, vi skiljer oss från Gud och hans folk.

Om du befinner dig i detta tillstånd, kom ihåg: en klar himmel är bara en bön bort.

Guds offer är en förkrossad ande; ett förkrossat och bedrövat hjärta föraktar du inte, Gud – Ps 51:17.

Who would have ever imagined that a little germ which cannot be seen with the human eye, has put the entire globe in a tizzy, a panic, and an economic disruption? I have not seen a pandemic of this magnitude in my lifetime and, when this first emerged, I was one of the gainsayers who could not believe it would cripple our world to this extent. Questions abound, conspiracy theories are propagated, and fear has run rampant throughout the world as the entire globe responds to the pandemic. Will there be a cure, or will this continue to be a scourge in our world? If this little virus trespasses into my physical body, what is the chance of survival? Will it affect any of my loved ones? The questions are innumerable. Where it has come from has been theorized by many, but does anyone really know? Where is God in the whole thing? Did it surprise Him? Is it God’s judgment on humanity? These and many other questions are being asked by many sincere people and the answers that are given often contradict one another.

One of the outfalls of the pandemic is the government invasion into the church and our personal lives in a way that has been unprecedented in my and your lifetime. Suddenly, we are faced with decisions that many of us have not thought through. When, and how much, should the government mandate things in our lives when we clearly believe in separation of Church and state? What are my rights? What will I do if I lose my business? Will I cash in the stimulus check that is supposed to arrive in the mail in the near future?

There is a verse in Peter that reminds me that if anyone should have answers in this time of pandemic, we as Christians should. But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: –1Pe 3:15. We may not know the origin of the virus, nor the outcome, but we do know Who knows all things, and that it was not a surprise to Him. It is the right time to turn to the Lord Jesus Christ, the One who holds all things by the power of His Word. If anytime in recent history the Christian has an opportunity to be salt in the earth and light in the world, it is during this time of upheaval. So, what should the response of the Christian be?

Consider this verse in Luke: Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth… –Luk 21:26. For the Christian, earthquakes, famines, and pestilence should be no surprise since they have been prophesied to us through the Word of God. And while these things are happening and will happen, God has provided clear scriptural mandates for us as Christians to follow. We are clearly commanded in the scripture to not worry about tomorrow: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof –Mat 6:34.

So, we as Jesus’ disciples know that God will give us wisdom and grace for the difficulties of today. We are commanded to not borrow tomorrow’s troubles. We need to be reminded once again, in this time, as always, God will provide grace for today that will be great enough to sustain peace in the midst of the storm, and will provide it tomorrow if we live. Let us learn a lesson from Peter and the disciples—to focus on Jesus. We need to trust Jesus even when He seems to be asleep in the boat, rather than focusing on the storm that is raging all around us. Jesus was in control whether he was sleeping or awake and still is. But we might say, “How do I know if I will have food or clothing, or my business tomorrow?” And again, we hear the Savior say, “Look at the lilies, the fowls of the air, and learn a lesson from them!” We cannot even do some of the simplest things by God’s estimation, like add a cubit to our stature, so why would we try to deal with the hard things of providing for a tomorrow that is out of our control? Do these commands fit for the year 2020 and the pandemic that we are facing? I am sure that, in theory, we can agree, but can we internalize these verses and make them a very prominent place in our lives today?

There are principles given in God’s Word that, if we have not embraced them, we will also ‘reel in a tizzy’ when faced with things like the pandemic that is completely out of our control. One of those principles is the clear teaching that suffering is a way of life for the follower of Jesus. And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together –Rom 8:17.

The ‘health and wealth’ gospel that is peddled by many preachers today is a false doctrine and can leave a person reeling when they are faced with health or economic loss. We need to be okay with suffering, we need to embrace it; we need to arm ourselves with the same mind as Christ. The loss of our business, home and yes, even our own lives also, by economic disaster, storms, or accidents is not outside the realm of the will of God for the Christian. We know that God can eliminate any of these calamities and will protect us from them all IF He so wills. But whether He does or not is God’s prerogative and we are the happiest IF we surrender our lives completely to Him in faith, and trust Him to keep us, whether with little or with much.

Another principle we need to reckon with is that we have no rights except the right to the Tree of Life. For us as Christians it makes little difference if we are citizens of the United States or not. We have many privileges for which we are very grateful for, but we should not think we have a right to own, keep, or buy, or that we have a stake to claim in this world. In the Holy Scriptures we are reminded that we are but pilgrims and strangers here (see Heb 11:13-16). As Abraham and the other patriarchs, we have no abiding city here but look for a city …whose builder and maker is God –Heb 11:10.

There are plenty of lawyers offering to fight for our rights, but the truth of the matter is, our citizenship is in Heaven and we are just ambassadors here and can be kicked out by society and need to leave all anytime without a moment’s hesitation. If this will be a reality, we need to live our lives with all our things held with an open hand. We do not have the right (only the privilege)—to own land, to have enough food, to enjoy good health, and to live without suffering—nor should we fight for those so-called rights, but we, God’s people, must put on the mind of Christ and be willing to leave all behind for the sake of Christ and trust Him completely for our sustenance. Jesus said He sees one sparrow fall to the ground and reminds us that we are worth more than many sparrows. Jesus calls us to hate all that we hold dear here on this earth: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple –Luk 14:26.

As Christians, we do not plan to stay here on this earth; we are anticipating Heaven. The scriptures express this sentiment when it not only considers the whole earth groaning to be delivered from this death and decay, but that we ourselves are also groaning to be delivered. Should there be such a strong pull to be here that our hearts fail us …for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth…? –Luk 21:26. Should we much rather cry out “how long Lord Jesus” “so come”? Even as the apostle intimates as he wrestles with being “betwixt two”—For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: Nevertheless to abide in the flesh is more needful for you. –Php 1:23-24. The apostle clearly indicates “having a desire to depart and be with Christ is far better,” and the only thing that holds him here is the fact that there is work to be done.

Another area we should be awake to, is our vulnerability during this time of no church services. We may be tempted to go on-line and be fed spiritually by those who are false prophets or those who teach false doctrine. We need to “try the spirits” and know whose feet we are sitting at. Be selective to whom you might listen, or from whom you might allow your family to take nourishment. We, as fathers, are called to lead and lead we must. The burden is on our shoulders to help our families navigate through these uncertain times. We as fathers may need to be more proactive during this time. It is a call to us to rise up and lead our wives and children. Not only do we have to watch “whose feet we are sitting at”, but we need to lead our families with confidence, calling them to trust in God, and leading them in prayers of faith. We need to provide them with an example of faith and trust in God that no amount of buffeting will shake. This time of upheaval will not knock us off our feet IF we are rooted and grounded in Christ.

At a time like this, we need to make wise decisions, even decisions concerning the future, but still refrain from falling into the panic mode and running around as if we have no Heavenly Father. We also need to lead our families in being careful not to believe everything that one hears, but to be aware of where our news is coming from and to consider how reliable it is. Conspiracy theories abound concerning how this virus started and the political agenda theorized to be behind it. Refrain from spending time following these conspirators and rather follow the scripture mandate, “casting down imaginations.” The simple truth is this, we do not know, and if we did know it still should not change the way we live and our overall response. God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, of love and a sound mind. John tells us to not “believe every spirit, but to try the spirits to see whether they be of God.”

I believe that this is an awesome opportunity to reach out to our fellow brothers and sisters by praying for one another and by staying in touch so that we can ‘weep with those that weep’ and ‘rejoice with those that rejoice’. Some of us have jobs and some do not. God’s Word tells us that those who have are to give to those who do not have so that there may be an equality. It is a time to reach out to the elderly in our church or community and stay in touch by mail or phone. This is a time in which the lonely will only get lonelier. A cheery word, or a letter in the mail, and whatever other resources you can appropriately use may be just the thing that those around you need.

During the times of mandatory “stay at home”, there is a whole group of our society that will face challenges that they have not seen up to this time. According to various news sources there has been an increase in domestic violence since family members are spending much more time together than they normally do. But let this not once be named among us. This is the time for us as God’s children to maximize on “in home” relationships. The Bible calls us to “redeem the time” and this can be done by making the most of our time together as a family. Spend time together—reading the Bible, praying together, singing together, and just simply doing enjoyable things together—things that will nurture growth and love in our relationships. We need to be creative as fathers in bringing our family together in a way that will produce an atmosphere of unity and oneness.

One question that begs an answer is this, “Should the government dictate whether we have church or not?” This is something we need to answer since for some areas of the country it is more than a suggestion but has become mandatory. I believe that since the suggestion/order to not meet together during this time is for the purpose of not spreading a virus that is quite contagious, this then fulfills the scripture “to love our neighbor as ourselves.” It is a good opportunity to show the public that if the mandate does not ask us to violate the scripture, then we choose to honor the government. There may come a time soon enough that we will be asked to do something that we cannot do with a clear conscience and then we will need to stand and “obey God rather than men.”

Some feel a twang of guilt because of the verse, “to not forsake the assembling of ourselves together”, however, this seems to be addressing a habit or a way of life. I suppose this is dealing with the lazy, slothful heart that does not see the benefit of getting together. We want to get together… As soon as we can get together again, we will take advantage of it. There is a big difference between those who cannot get together for a short time and those that choose not to since they do not see the value of it. For the present time, it seems the best testimony to our world and public relations to honor the mandate since they are not fighting against our faith and God. Let’s just take care to not let this become our new normal. Let’s keep our eye on a path forward to once again practically function as a local body.

What can we do? Pray more than ever that God would use this to win the lost and refine the church. Spend time building relationships with those you are closest to and have been encouraged to stay home with. Let this pandemic prepare us for what God has for us in the future. Let us be very careful how we talk about the government and some of the rulings that have come out through this all. We are called to honor the king and we need to spend more time thanking God for our freedoms than maximizing on the negative—I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; –1Ti 2:1-3. For the Christian, …we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Rom 8:28.

Quem poderia imaginar que um pequeno germe, invisível a olho nu, deixaria o mundo inteiro em alvoroço, em pânico e em crise econômica? Nunca vi uma pandemia desta magnitude em minha vida e, quando ela surgiu, eu estava entre os que duvidavam, incapazes de acreditar que ela paralisaria nosso mundo a tal ponto. Há inúmeras perguntas, teorias conspiratórias são difundidas e o medo se espalhou pelo mundo inteiro enquanto todos reagem à pandemia. Haverá uma cura, ou isso continuará sendo uma praga em nosso mundo? Se este pequeno vírus invadir meu corpo, quais são as chances de sobrevivência? Afetará algum dos meus entes queridos? As perguntas são incontáveis. Muitos especularam sobre sua origem, mas alguém realmente sabe? Onde está Deus em tudo isso? Isso o surpreendeu? É o juízo de Deus sobre a humanidade? Muitas pessoas sinceras fazem essas e muitas outras perguntas, e as respostas dadas frequentemente se contradizem.

Uma das consequências da pandemia é a interferência do governo na igreja e em nossa vida pessoal de uma maneira sem precedentes em toda a minha vida e a sua. De repente, deparamo-nos com decisões sobre as quais muitos de nós não refletimos. Quando e até que ponto o governo deve impor medidas em nossa vida, quando acreditamos claramente na separação entre Igreja e Estado? Quais são os meus direitos? O que farei se perder meu negócio? Devo descontar o cheque de estímulo que, supostamente, chegará pelo correio em breve?

Há um versículo em Pedro que me lembra que, se alguém deve ter respostas neste tempo de pandemia, nós, como cristãos, devemos tê-las. Mas santifiquem Cristo como Senhor em seu coração; estejam sempre preparados para responder a qualquer pessoa que lhes pedir a razão da esperança que há em vocês, com mansidão e respeito. –1Pe 3:15. Talvez não saibamos a origem do vírus nem o que acontecerá, mas sabemos quem conhece todas as coisas e que isso não foi uma surpresa para ele. Este é o momento certo para nos voltarmos ao Senhor Jesus Cristo, aquele que sustenta todas as coisas pelo poder de sua Palavra. Se em algum momento da história recente o cristão tem a oportunidade de ser sal na terra e luz no mundo, é durante este período de convulsão. Então, qual deve ser a resposta do cristão?

Considere este versículo em Lucas: Os homens desmaiarão de terror, apreensivos com o que estará sobrevindo ao mundo… –Lc 21:26. Para o cristão, terremotos, fomes e pestes não deveriam ser surpresa, pois foram profetizados para nós por meio da Palavra de Deus. E, enquanto essas coisas acontecem e ainda acontecerão, Deus nos deu mandamentos bíblicos claros que devemos seguir como cristãos. As Escrituras nos ordenam claramente a não nos preocuparmos com o amanhã: Portanto, não se preocupem com o amanhã, pois o amanhã trará as suas próprias preocupações. Basta a cada dia o seu próprio mal. –Mt 6:34.

Assim, nós, discípulos de Jesus, sabemos que Deus nos dará sabedoria e graça para as dificuldades de hoje. Recebemos a ordem de não tomar emprestados os problemas de amanhã. Precisamos ser lembrados mais uma vez, neste tempo, como sempre, de que Deus proverá hoje graça suficiente para sustentar a paz em meio à tempestade e a proverá amanhã, se estivermos vivos. Aprendamos uma lição com Pedro e os discípulos: concentrar-nos em Jesus. Precisamos confiar em Jesus mesmo quando parece estar dormindo no barco, em vez de nos concentrarmos na tempestade que ruge ao nosso redor. Jesus estava no controle, estivesse dormindo ou acordado, e continua a estar. Mas talvez digamos: «Como sei se terei comida ou roupa, ou se meu negócio estará de pé amanhã?» E, mais uma vez, ouvimos o Salvador dizer: «Olhem para os lírios, para as aves do céu e aprendam com eles!» Nem sequer podemos fazer algumas das coisas mais simples, segundo a avaliação de Deus, como acrescentar um côvado à nossa estatura; por que, então, tentaríamos lidar com as coisas difíceis de prover para um amanhã que não está sob nosso controle? Esses mandamentos se aplicam ao ano de 2020 e à pandemia que enfrentamos? Tenho certeza de que, em teoria, podemos concordar, mas será que podemos interiorizar esses versículos e dar-lhes um lugar de destaque em nossa vida hoje?

Há princípios apresentados na Palavra de Deus que, se não os tivermos abraçado, também nos farão «ficar em alvoroço» quando enfrentarmos coisas como a pandemia, que está totalmente fora de nosso controle. Um desses princípios é o claro ensinamento de que o sofrimento faz parte da vida de quem segue Jesus. E, se somos filhos, então somos herdeiros; herdeiros de Deus e coerdeiros com Cristo, se de fato participamos dos seus sofrimentos, para que também participemos da sua glória. –Rm 8:17.

O «evangelho da saúde e da prosperidade» propagado por muitos pregadores hoje é uma falsa doutrina e pode deixar uma pessoa abalada quando ela enfrenta a perda da saúde ou dificuldades econômicas. Precisamos aceitar o sofrimento; precisamos acolhê-lo; precisamos nos armar com a mesma disposição de Cristo. A perda de nosso negócio, de nossa casa e, sim, até mesmo de nossa própria vida, por desastre econômico, tempestades ou acidentes, não está fora do âmbito da vontade de Deus para o cristão. Sabemos que Deus pode eliminar qualquer dessas calamidades e nos proteger de todas elas, SE assim quiser. Mas fazê-lo ou não é prerrogativa de Deus, e somos mais felizes SE rendermos completamente nossa vida a ele em fé e confiarmos que ele cuidará de nós, quer tenhamos pouco, quer tenhamos muito.

Outro princípio com o qual precisamos nos conformar é que não temos direitos, exceto o direito à Árvore da Vida. Para nós, como cristãos, faz pouca diferença sermos ou não cidadãos dos Estados Unidos. Temos muitos privilégios pelos quais somos muito gratos, mas não devemos pensar que temos o direito de possuir, conservar ou comprar, nem que temos uma parte a reivindicar neste mundo. Nas Sagradas Escrituras, somos lembrados de que aqui somos apenas peregrinos e estrangeiros (ver Hb 11:13-16). Assim como Abraão e os outros patriarcas, não temos aqui cidade permanente, mas buscamos uma cidade …cujo arquiteto e edificador é Deus. –Hb 11:10.

Há muitos advogados oferecendo-se para lutar por nossos direitos, mas a verdade é que nossa cidadania está no Céu, e aqui somos apenas embaixadores; a sociedade pode nos expulsar, e precisamos deixar tudo a qualquer momento, sem hesitar por um instante. Se isso vier a se tornar realidade, precisamos viver mantendo tudo o que temos com a mão aberta. Não temos o direito (apenas o privilégio) de possuir terras, ter alimento suficiente, gozar de boa saúde e viver sem sofrimento — e não devemos lutar por esses chamados direitos; nós, porém, o povo de Deus, devemos revestir-nos da disposição de Cristo e estar dispostos a deixar tudo para trás por amor a Cristo e confiar completamente nele para nosso sustento. Jesus disse que vê um pardal cair ao chão e nos lembra de que valemos mais do que muitos pardais. Jesus nos chama a odiar tudo o que estimamos aqui nesta terra: Se alguém vem a mim e não odeia seu pai, sua mãe, sua esposa, seus filhos, seus irmãos e suas irmãs e até a própria vida, não pode ser meu discípulo. –Lc 14:26.

Como cristãos, não planejamos permanecer aqui nesta terra; aguardamos o Céu. As Escrituras expressam esse sentimento ao considerar não apenas que a terra inteira geme para ser libertada desta morte e decadência, mas também que nós mesmos gememos para ser libertos. Será que existe um apego tão forte a este mundo que nosso coração desfalece …de terror, apreensivos com o que estará sobrevindo ao mundo…? –Lc 21:26. Não deveríamos antes clamar: «Até quando, Senhor Jesus?», «Vem, pois»? Como o apóstolo dá a entender ao debater-se entre «duas possibilidades»: Estou pressionado dos dois lados: desejo partir e estar com Cristo, o que é muito melhor; contudo, por causa de vocês, é mais necessário que eu permaneça no corpo. –Fp 1:23-24. O apóstolo indica claramente que «desejar partir e estar com Cristo é muito melhor», e a única coisa que o mantém aqui é o fato de que há trabalho a fazer.

Outra área para a qual devemos estar atentos é nossa vulnerabilidade durante este período sem cultos na igreja. Podemos ser tentados a acessar a internet e receber alimento espiritual de falsos profetas ou de pessoas que ensinam doutrina falsa. Precisamos «provar os espíritos» e saber a quem estamos ouvindo. Sejam criteriosos quanto a quem escutam e de quem permitem que sua família receba alimento espiritual. Nós, como pais, somos chamados a liderar, e precisamos liderar. Cabe-nos ajudar nossas famílias a atravessar estes tempos incertos. Talvez nós, pais, precisemos ser mais proativos neste período. É um chamado para nos levantarmos e conduzirmos nossas esposas e nossos filhos. Não precisamos apenas prestar atenção a «quem estamos ouvindo», mas também liderar nossas famílias com confiança, chamando-as a confiar em Deus e conduzindo-as em orações de fé. Precisamos dar-lhes um exemplo de fé e confiança em Deus que nenhuma adversidade abale. Este período de convulsão não nos derrubará SE estivermos enraizados e alicerçados em Cristo.

Em um momento como este, precisamos tomar decisões sábias, inclusive decisões sobre o futuro, mas ainda assim evitar entrar em pânico e correr de um lado para outro como se não tivéssemos um Pai celestial. Também precisamos orientar nossas famílias a tomar cuidado para não acreditar em tudo o que se ouve, mas a prestar atenção à origem das notícias e avaliar sua confiabilidade. Abundam teorias conspiratórias sobre como este vírus começou e sobre a suposta agenda política por trás dele. Evitem passar tempo seguindo esses conspiradores; sigam, em vez disso, a ordem das Escrituras: «destruindo raciocínios». A simples verdade é esta: não sabemos, e, mesmo que soubéssemos, isso ainda não deveria mudar a maneira como vivemos nem nossa resposta geral. Deus não nos deu espírito de medo, mas de poder, amor e equilíbrio. João nos diz para não «crer em todo espírito, mas provar os espíritos para ver se procedem de Deus».

Acredito que esta é uma oportunidade extraordinária para nos aproximarmos de nossos irmãos e irmãs, orando uns pelos outros e mantendo contato, para que possamos «chorar com os que choram» e «alegrar-nos com os que se alegram». Alguns de nós têm emprego, outros não. A Palavra de Deus nos diz que os que têm devem dar aos que não têm, para que haja igualdade. É hora de procurar os idosos da nossa igreja ou comunidade e manter contato por carta ou telefone. Neste período, os solitários ficarão ainda mais solitários. Uma palavra animadora, uma carta pelo correio e quaisquer outros meios que vocês possam usar de maneira adequada talvez sejam exatamente o que as pessoas ao seu redor precisam.

Durante os períodos de «permanência obrigatória em casa», há um grupo inteiro em nossa sociedade que enfrentará desafios que nunca havia enfrentado. Segundo várias fontes de notícias, a violência doméstica aumentou, pois os membros da família estão passando muito mais tempo juntos do que normalmente passam. Mas que isso jamais seja mencionado entre nós. Este é o momento de nós, filhos de Deus, aproveitarmos ao máximo os relacionamentos «dentro de casa». A Bíblia nos chama a «aproveitar bem o tempo», e podemos fazê-lo aproveitando ao máximo o tempo que passamos juntos em família. Passem tempo juntos — lendo a Bíblia, orando juntos, cantando juntos e simplesmente fazendo juntos coisas agradáveis — coisas que promovam o crescimento e o amor em nossos relacionamentos. Nós, pais, precisamos ser criativos ao reunir nossa família de uma maneira que produza um ambiente de união e comunhão.

Uma pergunta que exige resposta é esta: «O governo deve determinar se podemos ou não realizar cultos?» Precisamos responder a isso, pois em algumas regiões do país isso deixou de ser apenas uma sugestão e se tornou obrigatório. Creio que, como a recomendação ou ordem para não nos reunirmos durante este período tem o objetivo de impedir a propagação de um vírus bastante contagioso, isso cumpre então o mandamento das Escrituras de «amar o próximo como a nós mesmos». É uma boa oportunidade para mostrar ao público que, se a determinação não nos pede que violemos as Escrituras, escolhemos respeitar o governo. Pode chegar em breve o momento em que nos pedirão que façamos algo que não podemos fazer com a consciência tranquila; então precisaremos nos posicionar e «obedecer antes a Deus do que aos homens».

Alguns sentem uma pontada de culpa por causa do versículo «não deixemos de nos reunir», mas parece que ele se refere a um hábito ou modo de vida. Suponho que trate do coração preguiçoso e indolente que não vê o benefício de se reunir. Queremos nos reunir… Assim que pudermos voltar a nos reunir, aproveitaremos essa oportunidade. Há uma grande diferença entre aqueles que não podem se reunir por um curto período e aqueles que escolhem não fazê-lo porque não veem valor nisso. Por enquanto, parece que o melhor testemunho para o nosso mundo e para as relações com o público é respeitar a determinação, já que ela não se opõe à nossa fé e a Deus. Tomemos apenas o cuidado de não deixar que isso se torne nosso novo normal. Mantenhamos os olhos no caminho adiante, para voltarmos a funcionar na prática como uma igreja local.

O que podemos fazer? Oremos mais do que nunca para que Deus use isso para conquistar os perdidos e refinar a igreja. Dediquemos tempo a construir relacionamentos com aqueles que nos são mais próximos e com quem fomos incentivados a ficar em casa. Que esta pandemia nos prepare para aquilo que Deus tem para nós no futuro. Tenhamos muito cuidado com a maneira como falamos do governo e de algumas das decisões que foram tomadas durante todo esse período. Somos chamados a honrar o rei e precisamos dedicar mais tempo a agradecer a Deus por nossas liberdades do que a enfatizar o lado negativo —Exorto, portanto, que, antes de tudo, se façam súplicas, orações, intercessões e ações de graças por todos; pelos reis e por todos os que exercem autoridade, para que tenhamos uma vida tranquila e pacífica, com toda piedade e dignidade. Isso é bom e agradável diante de Deus, nosso Salvador. –1Tm 2:1-3. Para o cristão, …sabemos que todas as coisas cooperam para o bem daqueles que amam a Deus, daqueles que são chamados segundo o seu propósito. –Rm 8:28.

The early church in olden days
Had a desire to tell
The sinner about Jesus Christ,
About Heaven and hell.

Indeed, they were not perfect souls,
But yet they loved their Lord;
And strove to follow this command
In spite of peril and sword.

The more people they converted,
The more the tension grew.
The wicked rulers of the land
Did not know what to do.

A lot of folks were burned at stake,
Some put in dungeons cold,
Because they spread the Gospel word
With faith and courage bold.

These brave soldiers who suffered much
Were such bright lights indeed,
But to tell others about God
They still did see a need.

Now many years since then have passed;
We Christians tend to say
“Be an example to the world;
You need not tell the way.”

But if this point of view were true,
Then I would like to know:
As did the church in olden days,
Why doesn’t our church grow?

Is it that in America,
The fire has grown cold?
Since faith is good, why don’t we share
As did the saints of old?

In other lands this very day,
The fire is burning bright;
Because Christians are zealous there
And vigorous in fight.

While we thank God for freedom here,
They praise their Lord on high.
And thank Him that for Jesus’ sake
They suffer and they die.

So as martyrs in other lands
Are shedding blood for God,
If we would also spread God’s Word,
Our blood would stain our sod.

Is it a blessing from our God
That our country is free?
Or is it ‘cause we aren’t a “threat”
To the society?

Are we ashamed or have no time?
Dear friends, the time is nigh.
If we don’t bring the folks to God,
The populace will die.

So, in conclusion, friends, let’s take
The path that Jesus trod,
Showing lost souls, the narrow way,
That leads men home to God.

– Darren Brubaker

كانت الكنيسة الأولى في الأيام الغابرة
تتوق إلى أن تخبر
الخاطئ عن يسوع المسيح،
وعن السماء والجحيم.

حقًّا، لم يكونوا نفوسًا كاملة،
لكنهم أحبوا ربهم؛
وسعوا إلى اتباع هذه الوصية
رغم الخطر والسيف.

كلما زاد عدد من اهتدوا على أيديهم،
اشتد التوتر أكثر.
ولم يعرف حكام البلاد الأشرار
ماذا يفعلون.

أُحرق كثيرون على الخوازيق،
وأُودع بعضهم زنازين باردة،
لأنهم نشروا كلمة الإنجيل
بإيمان وشجاعة جسورين.

كان هؤلاء الجنود الشجعان الذين قاسوا الكثير
أنوارًا ساطعة حقًّا،
ومع ذلك رأوا حاجةً
إلى أن يخبروا الآخرين عن الله.

والآن، بعد أن مضت أعوام كثيرة منذ ذلك الحين؛
نميل نحن المسيحيين إلى القول:
«كونوا قدوةً للعالم؛
لا حاجة إلى أن تدلّوا الناس على الطريق».

لكن إن كانت وجهة النظر هذه صحيحة،
فأود أن أعرف:
لماذا لا تنمو كنيستنا،
كما نمت الكنيسة في الأيام الغابرة؟

أترى أن النار في أمريكا
قد خبت؟
ما دام الإيمان أمرًا حسنًا، فلماذا لا نشاركه
كما فعل القديسون في الزمن الغابر؟

وفي بلاد أخرى، في هذا اليوم بعينه،
تتقد النار ساطعة؛
لأن المسيحيين هناك غيورون
ويكافحون بحيوية.

وبينما نشكر الله على الحرية هنا،
يمجّدون ربهم العليّ،
ويشكرونه لأنهم، من أجل يسوع،
يتألمون ويموتون.

فبينما يسفك الشهداء في بلاد أخرى
دماءهم من أجل الله،
إن أردنا نحن أيضًا أن ننشر كلمة الله،
فستلطّخ دماؤنا ترابنا.

أهي بركة من إلهنا
أن بلدنا حر؟
أم لأننا لسنا «تهديدًا»
للمجتمع؟

أم نخجل أم ليس لدينا وقت؟
أيها الأصدقاء الأعزاء، لقد أوشك الوقت أن ينفد.
إن لم نأتِ بالناس إلى الله،
فسيهلك الناس.

فلنختتم، أيها الأصدقاء، ولنسلك
الطريق الذي سار فيه يسوع،
مبيّنين للنفوس الضالة الطريق الضيق،
الذي يقود البشر إلى موطنهم عند الله.

– Darren Brubaker
